The women have the floor..

Yesterday at midday a crowd of women gathered in front of the Będzin Magistrat (town hall), shouting that they should be given food products.
When the women began[?] to speak in raised tones, the police came and dispersed them.
—o—
Vice-voivode leaves his post
The current vice-voivode in the Kielce voivodeship, Dr. Krapefel[?], is leaving his post. The vice-voivode is to become a notary in Zamość.
—o—
New zinc-white factory.
As we learn, the zinc-white (zinc oxide) factory being built by the Polish Zinc Company in Będzin will be completed at the beginning of March of this year. The factory, equipped according to the latest technology, will produce 300 wagonloads of zinc white a year; the quality of processing will be the same as the zinc whites of the German factories.
—o—
Echoes of the events in the Będzin synagogue.
As our readers remember, a few weeks ago a great scandal took place in the Będzin synagogue, during which knives and revolvers were brandished[?].
The epilogue of the events will take place on the 20th of this month in the Będzin court. It is interesting that the Koziegłowy[?] rabbi has also been summoned as a witness.
—o—
Coal for the poor — Sunday.
On Wednesday evening there was a meeting of the coal commission, which decided that the coal distribution is to begin next Sunday at the premises of the Będzin kehilla.
—o—
No distraints for advance payments („zaliczki“).
The Chamber of Commerce in Sosnowiec has turned with a memorandum to the Ministry of Finance concerning the mass distraints being carried out over the advance payments (zaliczki) on the turnover tax[?] (obrotowy).
In the memorandum the Chamber of Commerce points out that according to a ruling of the Supreme Administrative Tribunal there is no right to carry out distraints for the advance payments. One may only impose a fine for delaying payment, but distraints may be made only after the whole turnover[?] has been assessed,
Taking into account the needs of the state treasury, the Chamber of Commerce demands that for advance payments too a 14-day grace period be given, and only afterwards should the money be collected by strict means.
We point out in this connection that yesterday was the last deadline for paying the advance payments. Anyone may apply to the head of the tax office (naczelnik[?]) with a request to pay the advance over 2 months in smaller instalments.
—o—
A „secret Jewish military organization“ uncovered..
On Monday[?] evening the Sosnowiec Betar held a meeting at its own premises. In the middle of the meeting the police arrived and led the leaders of the „military organization“ to the police station (komisariat).
After checking the young people's identity papers and [—] they were released.
It is worth[?] noting that the „Jew-friendly“ „Express Zagłębia“ writes at length about this affair, and in letters as big as for kiddush levana the paper tells its Jewish readers all the details of how the Sosnowiec police received[?] confidential information about the „secret Jewish military organization“ in Sosnowiec, and gives the names of the „field marshals“ who issue orders by the sign „Feld-Chai“ (Tel Chai).
—o—
Youth organization „Menorah“.
At the Revisionist organization in Będzin a youth organization named „Menorah“ has been founded.
Tonight an urgent meeting of members of the Revisionist organization takes place at its own premises.
—o—
Conference on the Red Cross.
This week the former minister Darowski[?] was here and held a conference with several doctors on current Red Cross matters.

On Annulling Old Taxes. What Does the New Circular Say?

[Taxes — Finance Ministry circular.] The Ministry of Finance has sent all the treasury chambers (izby skarbowe) a new circular (okólnik), in which the competence of the "offices" (urzędy skarbowe) and the "chambers" (izby) to grant reliefs and to spread tax arrears into instalments is considerably widened.
The circular states:
1) The treasury chambers are authorized[?] to remit arrears of income tax due up to and including the year 1930, but not more than up to 500 złoty; that is, if one owes more, it cannot be remitted. In cases where larger sums of "income" [tax] (dochodowy) are owed, one may apply directly to the Ministry of Finance.
2) The treasury chambers may remit arrears of turnover tax amounting to no more than two thousand złoty, apart from fine and interest, if the debt can no longer be collected.
3) The treasury chamber has the competence to spread into instalments, for a period of up to 12 months, such "pratekt"[?] sums as amount, without fine, interest and enforcement costs, to no more than one hundred thousand zł.
4) The treasury offices receive the competence to allow all tax arrears amounting to up to ten thousand złoty, apart from fine, interest and enforcement costs, to be paid off in instalments over 6 months, in exceptional cases even up to one year.
5) The offices also have the right to postpone entirely[?] the payment of tax arrears amounting to up to 5 thousand zł. for a period of two months.
In individual exceptional cases one may also postpone for up to 1 year.
6) These postponements and instalment arrangements cannot be made for the "advance payments (zaliczki) of industrial tax (podatek przemysłowy) and income tax (dochodowy)".
These advance payments may be spread over only two instalments, and paid off within 2 months.
7) The offices and the chambers have the competence, in all cases of spreading into instalments or postponing, to reduce the rate[?] of the interest charged for delay in payment. It may be reduced to as little as 1 percent per month.
Under this new circular the competence of the offices regarding postponement and instalments has been considerably widened, and the competence of the chambers regarding remission of uncollected taxes has also been widened.
If one wishes to apply to the chamber to annul "tax arrears" (zaległe podatki) that cannot be collected because the taxpayer has become impoverished, one must write out the petition and address it to the chamber, but one must submit it to the local office with a request to forward it to the chamber.
In such a petition, for remission of tax arrears, one must state why one cannot pay the taxes owed, why one sees no possibility of ever being able to pay them, state how far one has been impoverished, and ask that the tax debt be remitted.
The office carries out a detailed check as to whether the taxpayer is really unable to pay. And if after two such investigations it is confirmed with witnesses that the tax debt really cannot be collected and that the taxpayer is really unable to pay — the debt is annulled.
The Content of the "Volksbund" Complaint to the League of Nations.

[Upper Silesia — German minority.] As is known, the German "Volksbund" has turned to the League of Nations with a complaint concerning the elections to the Sejm and Senate.
Its content is as follows:
Katowice, 7 January (stycznia) 1931, Młyńska[?] Street 23. Invoking Article 147 of the Geneva Convention, [we] [—] point out[?] that in the months of październik [October] and listopad [November] 1930 acts of violence against the German minorities were deliberately organized from the Polish side in Upper Silesia.
The main accusation is directed[?] against the "Union of Polish Insurgents" (Związek Powstańców), the Polish press, the Polish authorities, the courts, the police, etc.
The materials supporting the accusations take up 93 printed pages, and the texts of the leaflets etc. have been photographically reproduced from the originals.
In conclusion the "Volksbund" expresses the hope that the League of Nations will consider the whole as an urgent question, together with the "gastes"[?] [perhaps: complaints] of the German government concerning its minorities.
From Sport.

[Sport.] (A—ski) Last week international [skating[?]] exercises took place on the Katowice artificial ice rink. Distinguishing themselves were the famous champion pair from Hungary[?], Olga Orgonista and Sándor[?] Szalay, and the 15-year-old Hilde Holovsky[?] (Vienna) enchanted the assembled public with her manner of performing the exercises. The world champion Sonja Henie has in her a strong rival.

What's New in Upper Silesia?

[Upper Silesia — news.]
Struggle against Jewish trade.
On Wednesday a meeting of the Christian merchants of Upper Silesia took place in Königshütte [Królewska Huta, now Chorzów].
The committee that called the meeting issued an appeal calling on all Christian merchants and tradeswomen to come to the meeting, at which the item of how to combat the "erudine[?] [probably: 'dirty'] Jewish competition" will be considered..
Verdict in the case of the murdered police sergeant.
On Monday the Rybnik court concluded the trial of the 8 Germans who had been accused of murdering a police przodownik [sergeant] in Golasowice during the election riots.
After the prosecutor's speech the court handed down a verdict under which 2 persons are sentenced to a year and a half in prison, 1 to one year in prison and 4 to 6 months; one was acquitted.
On wages.
On Tuesday a conference of industrialists and delegates of the mine workers took place in Katowice. Up to 200 delegates took part in the conference.
After a report by Mr. Stańczyk it was resolved to begin negotiations on fixing new wages.
The negotiations have [—][?] begun.
To the session of the League of Nations.
The Voivode of Katowice left yesterday for Geneva, where the sessions of the League of Nations are taking place.
Unhappy love and... rat poison.
The 17-year-old Maria S. in Wielkie Hajduki, intending to commit suicide, took "shuts"[?] a little rat poison. The reason for the suicide is an unhappy love.
German complaint against Poland
The "Deutscher Volksbund" in Upper Silesia last Monday sent a complaint to the League of Nations about alleged terror against the Germans in Polish Upper Silesia during the Sejm and Senate elections.
Visit of Lloyd George's secretary.
On Sunday Gareth Jones, Lloyd George's secretary, came to Upper Silesia to acquaint himself with the minorities question. Jones was received by the Katowice Voivode Grażyński, who in a lengthy interview gave him detailed explanations about the situation of the German minority in Upper Silesia.
That's a livelihood too..
In the month of April the general director of the community of interests of the Bismarck steelworks, "Królewska" and the "Laura" steelworks will leave his post on account of age. As reported, this post is to be taken over by the former Minister of Commerce Kwiatkowski.
The Brest affair in court.
On Saturday the editor of "Gazeta Robotnicza" in Katowice stood trial, accused of reprinting an article from "Robotnik" about the Brest affair.
The editor declared that the content of the article is in accordance with reality, and he asks that Deputy Lieberman and Senator Korfanty be summoned as witnesses.
The court agreed to this and postponed the trial to another date.
Demonstration in honour of Korfanty.
On Sunday a large demonstration in honour of Korfanty took place in Katowice. All the Chadecja [Christian Democratic] deputies and senators in Upper Silesia took part in the demonstration.
On "Plac Wolności" a speech was given by Sejm deputy Krzywowski[?], who declared that "Upper Silesia will not be frightened off by the Sanacja terror".
Dąbrowa

[Dąbrowa — local news.]
Performance of Oskar Rufel.
The performance at the great concert in the "Venus" on Saturday the 10th of this month by Oskar Rufel, professor at the Silesian Music School), Michał Wiger (baritone) and Hermann Löwenstein (well-known dramatic actor) gave the audience great pleasure.
Prof. Rufel possesses a fine technique. He plays cleanly and surely, and more than virtuosity is felt in his violin art. Characteristic of the gifted violinist is his penetration into specifically Jewish music and rendering it with soft Jewish sweetness.
Mr. Michał Wiger possesses a beautiful lyrical baritone and fine diction. He performed the prologue from "Pagliacci" splendidly.
Mr. Hermann Löwenstein brilliantly performed: "Der Gasn-Poyker" ["The Street Drummer"] by Halpern, "Volf" ["Wolf"] by Alex. Blok.
The attackers of Beitner's bakery punished.
Last year, during a demonstration of the unemployed, there was an attack on Beitner's bakery, where bread and also cash were robbed.
As the main culprits 2 persons were charged, who were sentenced this week by the Sosnowiec district court to two months in prison.
Moral preachers..
In the local "Kosmos" hall the Polish theatre of Sosnowiec gives a performance every Wednesday.
Last Wednesday it was announced that the well-known comedy "Yefi Klepczyk"[?] would be performed.

The owners of "Kosmos", however, after acquainting themselves with the content of the comedy, agreed that the comedy should indeed be performed.

A Letter to the Editor.
[Letter to the editor — tenants' association.]
I have the honour to inform those who for many years entrusted me with the office of president of the Tenants' Association that as of 1 January 1931 I have resigned from that office, both as president and as a member of the board.
I thank you, Mr. Editor, for printing these few lines.
Respectfully, M. Lewin.
Our Economic Interests. (What is new with the city-council elections? One ought to take a look at where things stand in the world.)

That means we are now, thank God, rid of the elections — first of all of the worse ones, the Sejm and Senate elections — and one can already breathe easily and make a reckoning of the soul.. But insofar as the citizens of Poland have already been freed[?] from the election ceremonies, we, the inhabitants of Zagłębie, are not yet finally rid of it all. True, we will not have to stand for Sejm and Senate elections now, but in return we still have city-council elections ahead of us.
The dissolved self-governments in Sosnowiec, Będzin, Zawiercie and Czeladź surely cannot, under the prevailing conditions, remain so forever, so that sooner or later the election of new members of the municipal self-governments will surely be ordered.
As we hear, people are even preparing for the "spectacles" already, and the behind-the-scenes politics is already beginning to operate. Of course "the street" and "the people" know nothing of all this yet, but behind closed doors[?] something is already being done and the necessary preparations are already being made.
As can be foreseen, turnout at the elections will be small, quite simply because the public is already fed up with the endlessly repeated[?] new elections; yet one must not underrate[?] local public activity, which plays a very significant role at the present time. Municipal work cannot nowadays be brushed aside[?] with a wave of the hand, because too many burdens [lie][?] on the city's citizens on the one side, and on the other side they [the municipal bodies] also really[?] render the citizens many services[?] and in any case bear much responsibility towards us. When we have a municipal self-government [running][?] ever more colossal undertakings[?], we must not, already from this standpoint, take these institutions lightly; we must not forget that all of us together carry the burdens on our shoulders, we pay for all the budgets they put together, and therefore we must watch how the work is done, how and in what manner the building is built.
True, many capable people, who could have brought us much benefit, are withdrawing from useful activity, and their place is beginning to be taken, here and there[?], by little men with miniature notions, who pursue a kind of "income politics" or keep inciting[?] one against the other and are out only to shatter everything that could be built intensively; or else — we also have such as only look to accommodate themselves to the "poritz" [the lord], want to be his obedient servants, and lick the rod with which they are whipped.
And precisely from this standpoint — because we see that there will push their way onto the [?] [unclear word, perhaps "stage"] tiny, small-minded[?] little men, whose notions are crawling and fawning in the "ma-yafit" manner, who are nothing more than enslaved souls, or who are out for nothing but always living in hostile camps and brawling over personal ambitions — for that reason we must not stand at a distance and look on with a light heart as beautiful horizons and useful plans become a heap of ruins forever.
With pain in the heart and heavy spirits one watched the last city-council sessions, the manner in which they were conducted: many useful, urgent questions could not be resolved — not, God forbid, for ideological or principled reasons, but because one had tripped up the other, because he had been waiting to settle accounts with him and at the first opportunity paid him back the debt.. Public questions, however urgent and useful to the community they may have been, were turned into private intrigues, into petty agitation. Very often, unfortunately, it came down to the lowest[?] level, so that people quite forgot that they had been elected by the city to occupy themselves with communal work, which has such important significance in public life.
And if things have looked like this until now, it is reasonable to suppose that later it will be still worse, that now such people will try to grab the seats [lit. "little benches"] of whom we will only first[?] hear[?] — whoever has the nerve to climb onto the public's back; and of course in that case we would sink much lower in the public sense, because then there would truly be no limit to public lawlessness.
From this standpoint we must not remain indifferent to the city-council elections; we must not dismiss the question with a "feh!": "What does it concern me? Let others worry about the community, I'll keep going my own way[?]." Communal [kehilla-type] affairs must not be taken so lightly when one sees that they are beginning to sink ever deeper into the deep abyss and arrive at unheard-of, frivolous irresponsibility.
One must not allow all sorts of black crows to spread their wings freely and frankly, who are out for nothing but poisoning the air, heavy enough as it is. Ignoramuses ["amei ha-aretz"] must be removed as representatives in our Jewish world — let alone when it is a matter of their having to be Jewish representatives in joint activity in municipal institutions: then we are put to shame twice: once when they cannot open their mouths, and a second time because they are not up to the task of solving[?] such decisive[?] public problems: they neither find their way in what is being discussed, nor can they defend and give reasons for what is at stake.
And therefore we must not be frivolous and naive; we must already now see to it that ignorance does not flutter[?] freely over the Jewish street and bring us shame and pain, and that we are not improperly represented, so that at the first opportunity we would have no one to defend us and speak in our name.
It would already now be necessary to create some kind of committee of conscious people, who would not only not allow shadow and darkness to be smuggled into our world, but would have the task of explaining to all sorts of strata of the population the necessity of going to the elections and having conscious Jewish representatives, who would be capable not merely of sitting there but also of defending, of fighting if need be, and of illuminating our Jewish and economic interests, which we need so badly at the present, worst moment.
Selekt.
The Wedding of Full Orphans by the "Hachnasat Kalla" Society in Będzin

As we have already written, the board of "Hachnasat Kalla" [dowering of brides] in Będzin took the initiative to make a wedding for 2 full orphans ["runde yesoymim" — orphaned of both parents].
The wedding, which took place in the hall of the "Talmud Torah" and was celebrated with the greatest splendour[?], aroused interest among the broad strata of the Jewish population, who came to take part in the celebration of the 2 full orphans. Absent were only the so-called invited "notables" ["pney"], who, as it turns out, were afraid that it might, God forbid, cost them a few guilders [złoty]...
The expenses of the wedding were borne by the board members of the above-mentioned institution, not just to discharge an obligation; rather they prepared[?] a wedding with all the trimmings[?], even music and a badchan [wedding jester] as well.
The "unterfirers" [those who lead the couple to the canopy] were Messrs. R' Yosele Grugerman[?] and Yekl Unger with their wives. The chuppah, which took place in the courtyard, was attended by hundreds of people.
In the middle of the rich banquet "toasts" were made in honour of the society. A written greeting was sent by Mr. L. Bauszykowski[?], who announced at the same time that the "Gemilut Chasadim" [interest-free loan] fund was giving a "droshe-geshank" [wedding-sermon gift] of 25 zł., and the Bauszykowski family — half a dozen spoons.
At the calling-out of the droshe-gifts close to 400 zł. in cash and a large number of household articles and furniture were collected.
The "in-laws" made merry until dawn.
Our Panorama

[Zagłębie — feuilleton: a satirical round-up of the small towns; Olkusz, Będzin, Słomniki, Strzemieszyce, Zawiercie, Modrzejów, Czeladź.]
The small towns are mighty. — An ultimatum from Olkusz. — An appeal by worshippers to the Jewish people. — Sabbath „spectacles“ — A hard question. — Victims of a dance contest. — A luckless society. — Paid for maftir. — „Demons“ in a Jewish bank.
It is an old rule that „God sends the cure before the plague“. Tell me, for instance, what would our darkened life of today look like if, God forbid, there were not to be found on the globe such places as Olkusz, Strzemieszyce, Skała and even such a metropolis as Będzin? Health to their bones! They, the little towns with their gabbaim, are after all like a healing balm for our sick souls.
Here, for example, with us in Zagłębie the election business has already been forgotten; were it not for the „din-Torah“ between Reb Yitzchok and Reb Hershl in Warsaw, we would almost have forgotten that Sejm elections once took place. On the other hand, the Olkusz supporters of [list] 17 do not stop sending us ultimatums that we should, for the sake of the public, proclaim before the whole world that „in Olkusz the whole town is up on wheels [= in an uproar]; preparations are being made to appoint a new rabbi and new shochtim, so that all shall hear and see that a rabbi who lives off the whole town should not meddle in any other politics; for other big towns too it will be a great lesson; we'll yet see how we settle accounts with the Vayakhel-Pekudei people; soon there will be kehilla elections in Olkusz, etc., etc.“
The „manifesto“ will without any doubt „stir up the whole world“, and every „state“ will delegate a representative to Olkusz, to the „town that is up on wheels“...
—o—
A group from the Będzin bet-midrash, too, appeals to the whole world about an important matter. Because of its great importance I have the honour of presenting the manifesto as in the original...
„Jews of Będzin! — so the appeal begins — the highest time has come to sound the alarm about the terrible danger that threatens the Jewish people. One must not keep silent when a gang of shkotzim insult the rabbi in the bet-midrash; when Fajwel Szwajcer was gabbai this did not happen; with all our strength we must remove the apikorsim, the dissolute shkotzim.
One must not forget that we live in the age of radio and airships; only we have fallen behind the times in which we must live; Mr. Fajwel Szwajcer must be gabbai“...
Clear words, it seems; so there lies a duty on the Jewish people to raise heaven and earth by means of the radios and airships so that Fajwel Szwajcer becomes gabbai of the Będzin bet-midrash...
—o—
Słomniki does have a gabbai; nevertheless „the apikorsim, the hooligans [kholtayes]“ have complete control over the local bet-midrash there. The „spectacles“ take place every Sabbath — people have time — so they test their strength...
And when you fight, you don't stop to check where the blows land and who gets them; in the latest „boxing“ the victim, alas, was a Torah scroll, which was torn in two...
The Jews of Słomniki fasted a day for it, but they had hardly sobered up when they went back again to the „holy work“...
— As long as people say that among Jews the crisis reigns...
—o—
The Jews of Strzemieszyce are occupied with the hard question whether a man observing a yahrzeit is obliged to lead Musaf before the lectern or not.
The „hard“ matter became topical because of the new gabbai, an artisan, who did not allow their „pshitshivanik“ [?], who had yahrzeit, to lead Musaf before the lectern...
We do not possess the „qualifications“ to state our opinion on this, and we hand it over to the district court, which will most probably make clear to the Jews of Strzemieszyce who is guilty — the yahrzeit-man or the artisan gabbai.
—o—
About the „events“ in Zawiercie we ought, in truth, to have kept silent: for when we pick on ordinary mortals, gabbaim or other holy vessels, we at least have no fear of „attacks“, whereas the Zawiercie affair already concerns our legionnaires, the Betarniks, the „real robbers“, so that „it smells of gunpowder“...
On the other hand, though, one would need a „heart of stone“ not to tell „before the whole world“ the tragedy of several Zawiercie dancers, women and men, who became „victims“ of the „Mah-yafit“-niks — pardon, of the Betarniks...
And this is how it happened.
Betar in Zawiercie arranged a dance evening with „the most terrible surprises“...
Among the „surprises“ there was also a dance contest with a prize of a bonbonnière worth no less than 5 złoty.
Well, well, the crowd of dancers competed for [?] the 5-złoty prize till the sparks flew...
After the „mitzvah-dance“ the committee went off to deliberate and decided that Mr. Drezner had danced best; but since a policeman had also taken part in the contest, one must not shame him — a policeman after all — so he should get the bonbonnière...
When the verdict did not please the „dancing public“, the committee changed its decision: the bonbonnière should be exchanged for two bars of chocolate, one bar for the policeman and the second bar — for Drezner.
The latter would not accept the „gift“ and, together with part of the „national heroes“, „danced“ out of the hall, and the celebration was disrupted...
—o—
Disrupted again this year was the „Vayechi“ kiddush of the Chevra Kadisha in Będzin.
The holy society, which all year long „fills up“ the gmina [community] treasury, has a tradition of making a kiddush on the Sabbath of the portion Vayechi. Last year the kiddush was disrupted by the rabbi, and this year by the president, who „twisted“ for so long until he had „twisted out“ the traditional kiddush...
— When one says a „dead society“, it doesn't quite fit...
—o—
Modrzejów, too, is keen that the deeds of the local „strong family“ be „described“.
There is there, in Modrzejów, it is said, a family that believes in the „strong hand“. If anyone wrongs them, he at once gets his verdict, and basta...
And it came to pass that one of the family had yahrzeit and a desire to get maftir! But the trouble is that the maftirs for the whole year are let as a concession, and when the concession-holder would not give up the maftir, he very nearly became a niftar [deceased] for it...
— Yes, yes, long life to them, the lively little Jews; they really refresh us in such a hard time...
—o—
The „report“ from Czeladź is an exception: the report tells us not about aliyot or benches, but about „not-good ones“ [demons], who, God save us, have got into the local bank and are throwing the officials out of it.
The first victim to fall was an 18-year-old girl, then a father who, besides small children, also has a wife...
The „reducer“ [?] has „tightened the screw“ [?]. It would be interesting, though, also to know how the „not-good ones“ gained control of the Czeladź bank...
Man Amrin [?].
On a Slippery Road

[Będzin — kehilla and rabbinate; the shochet affair.]
(Why do neither the rabbinate nor the kehilla leaders answer the accusations? What is the upshot?)
Two weeks ago a letter was printed in the columns of our paper from non-partisan Hasidim of Będzin, who had turned to the rabbinate and to the kehilla leaders on the grounds that they want to "smuggle through" a shochet (ritual slaughterer) for the town, and they — the writers of the letter — say quite openly that they "will not let a shochet be smuggled through for a bribe [łapówka]".
We were sure that, in response to such a letter of accusation, in which both the rabbinate and the kehilla leaders are charged with nothing more and nothing less than bribery, they would be compelled to throw off these grave accusations and would surely want to wash themselves clean of such a dirty stain. Unfortunately, however, these highest representative bodies of ours have taken a mouthful of water, whereby the accusation is confirmed; and therefore the Jewish population is all the more agitated, and everyone asks: what is being done there again? What are they doing once more behind our backs and at our expense?
Well, the non-partisan Hasidim come to the conclusion that an inquiry should be carried out, whose task would be to find out whether the town needs a fifth shochet at all, and if it turns out that it does — then another candidate, to whom the post of shochet comes by inheritance, has precedence.
The question as such does not interest us, because it is not we who are competent in this matter, and it [sic: "he"] need not interest us. After all, for that we have our highest representative bodies, which are appointed over kashrut and over guarding everything pertaining to the religious functionaries; but when these representatives of ours are accused of nothing more and nothing less than dishonesty, and they do not answer it — it is no wonder that their prestige falls in the eyes of the Jewish population, in the eyes of all those who are members of the Jewish kehilla administration.
That the slaughtering question is not in order with us, that a witch's wheel is spinning around it, that someone wanted to hush it up by force, that someone wanted to steal the whole "thou shalt not steal" out of it — that was almost certain, since it has already been shown several times that we have no need of a new shochet at a time when the old ones do not properly receive their pensions; but still nobody reckoned that it would go so far that, when people come and publicly accuse public institutions of dishonest deeds, they would remain just as indifferent as if nothing at all, as if it were not they who were meant, as if the witch's wheel were not spinning around them.
Does our rabbinate know how far they are demoralising everything that pertains to the Jewish religion? Do they know what impression such silence makes in the eyes of the population, in the eyes of the most varied strata of the broad masses? Do they give themselves an account of where they are leading with these deeds?
True, it is an old story that the rabbinate in general takes no account of the printed word and for some reason does not answer any accusation, any reproach; but one must nevertheless know that there is a difference between one accusation and another, between one reproach and another; after all, not everything can be weighed on one and the same scale, not every object can be measured with one and the same measure. One must give oneself a precise [misprinted] account of every event, in order to know how far it touches [misprinted], how far it penetrates into human hearts.
And what more can there be, when Jews, comrades, Hasidic people come along and say openly and accuse, before the whole congregation, both the rabbinate and the kehilla representatives of unseemly deeds, of smuggling and of bribery — and nothing; no answer, as if nothing had happened, as if nobody had said anything at all, and as if the talk were about someone else.
Cannot this tactic be compared to the kind of people who, when one spits in their face, pretend not to notice and let it be understood that it does not concern them at all, that nobody spat in their face, but that it is simply raining?
Well, that may be tolerated, as it is, when it concerns private persons and private matters; in no way can anything like it be compared to a case that concerns the community, that touches the public!
It is unheard of that public matters should be settled in such a despotic and such an irresponsible way. Are these moneys not taken from the public? Are the shochetim and the rabbinate and all the religious functionaries not maintained by the Jewish population?
A question about a fact — do they perhaps doubt that they are maintained by all of us, and that therefore they need not reckon with us and need render no account, however strong the accusation may be? Who knows, perhaps they have no idea how and from what sources the moneys come in which are paid out to them?
Otherwise it is impossible to imagine so much lawlessness, so much clumsiness. Such a tactic is incomprehensible, inconceivable. Everything must have a limit, a measure, a bound — so why do we not see it in this case? Why do our parnassim [community leaders] and religious leaders not give themselves an account of how deep they have crawled into a filthy abyss? Have they really sunk so deep that they no longer [know] where they are in the world? Are they already certain that everything they do is good and fine, and that when one points out to them the most dreadful thing, which corrupts and dishonours their name, it is nothing at all? Are they sure that everything they do, however undignified and banal it may be, will not lower their prestige? Where does their certainty in all this come from, when we see that their lustre has long since faded, that people have stopped listening to the said representative bodies with the seriousness of former times and with the firm belief that truth and justice, righteousness and fairness reign there?
And despite all this they do not realise that it is neither nice, nor good, nor healthy to go on along this slippery road, where the danger of slipping has so many chances? Must one start drilling the grown-up leaders — who supposedly have so little experience — from the alef onward, as if they had only just stepped out into the public arena? If not — if everything were in perfect order — they would at least have needed to answer such open accusations of bribery. They must not forget that they owe Jewish Będzin an answer, and the answer must be a clean one, a clear one, not a superficial [?] one, not an evasive one.
Those at whom the accusation is aimed must answer, and the answer must be, as stated, a clear one; but as long as this is not cleared up before the public, so long will you not be vindicated.
R. Les.
Race

Drama in 3 acts by Jan Fabricius[?].
(Staged by the „Dovid Herman Theatre“).
The theme is not a new one.
An Englishman who is stationed in India falls in love there with a Hindu woman, a temple dancer, and as the product of this mutual love a boy is born.
The child's father does not want to leave him in India, where culture is enormously[?] backward, and when the child grows up he sends him to London, to school.
Years go by. The mother can hardly wait for the moment when she will be able to see her son, who is due to return from England. Her whole being is taken up with just the one single desire: to embrace her child as quickly as possible and to stay together with him forever.
At last the happy day has come. Little Guy returns from London, but instead of falling joyfully into his mother's outstretched arms, he turns away from her in fear.
The various toys which the mother and her free[?] (possibly: faithful) servant obtain for the boy in order to win his affection are of no help. He laughs at the toys, which represent various Indian heroes. „Are these your knights, with such crooked legs? — the boy asks, laughing — I don't need such silly toys, rather buy me a compass“.
With his photographic camera little Guy throws a fright into everyone around him; the servant Pravira in particular is seized by a manic terror when the boy wants to photograph him. The Asiatic servant simply dies of fright when the boy tells him that soon he will find himself inside the little box (the camera).
The mother suffers terribly from the fact that her son still remains a stranger to her. She looks for various means by which to win his affection, but all without success. She places her last hope in the priest-sorcerer Pavikrama[?]. He, who speaks with „Allah“, who knows his wishes and knows his ways — he will give her son back to her.
After long entreaties Nia-i Lasmi[?] succeeds in prevailing upon her husband that the priest may come to her, but only on condition that she does not show him the child.
The priest comes, and under the effect of the magic prayer, in which the saying „Short is life, the soul eternal“ is repeated over and over, he succeeds in putting the unhappy mother into a magnetic half-sleep, and with the dagger that the sorcerer gives her she murders her child, and a moment later she[?] dies herself.
The drama gives expression to the terrible racial antagonism, the dreadful struggle of two cultures that hate each other. The native hates with all the fire of his bitterness of soul the unbelieving white man, who in turn looks upon the native as a creature that stands lower than a beast.
The acting of the performers:
Dina König in the role of Nia-i Lasmi[?] created the type of a deeply suffering mother, for whom mother-love is the whole content of life. She loves her husband with all her soul, with all her senses, but her love for her child is stronger still. In her acting we are reminded[?] of the fine, subtle emotional gamut of a mother's heart; she thereby causes the spectator to be carried away and to live through[?] her tragedy together with her.
Yosef Kamen[?] in the double role is brilliant as the servant Pravira; he succeeded in creating the type of a primitive Asiatic who has been absolutely untouched by European civilisation. In the role of the Englishman, however, he is not particularly strong.
Rakow as Pavikrama[?] was weak. The effect of the drama would have been much stronger had the role been cast with a suitable talent.
R. Gert[?] in the role of the maid Karshina[?] — very good, although at times she was a little too shrill.
Limanak[?] as the child, satisfactory.
Sh. R.
Yente Has Rheumatism

[Humour — sketch.]
— Mendl, I'm wasting away, I'm dying; Mendl, come with me to a doctor.
— What's wrong with you, Yente?
— I don't know: I only know that my feet and hands pull, tear, pull, stab, and every limb of mine hurts.
— Maybe you have the flu?
— No, Mendl, it's not the flu, I have no headache, no fever.
— Maybe this is the beginning of the flu, and the headache and the fever will only come later?
— Mendl, are you starting already with your jokes? You know I hate it!
— You don't know what's good for you, Yente. Jokes are the best medicine; laughing is healthy.
— One doesn't feel like laughing when one isn't healthy.
— Maybe you should have a good sweat, Yente?
— When a doctor tells me to sweat, I'll sweat!
— Well then, that means going to the doctor? — I ask Yente.
— Yes, one is already looking[?], gevalt!
So we went off to Doctor Hopke, right in our own block.
Dr. Hopke let Yente know that she has rheumatism in her bones.
— So what must she do about it? — I want to know.
Says the doctor: for such things warm countries are good, where the sun always shines, where there is no snow, no frost, no winter, where the sun burns and bakes right through the bones. And that is Pistyan [Piešťany, the spa in Czechoslovakia]. There is no better place for rheumatics — says Dr. Hopke — long live Maran[?]!
— How much should it cost?
— Not much. About 40 dollars a week. You need to be there a whole winter; seven or eight hundred dollars — you'll manage it very easily.
— Thank you for the advice.
Having paid Dr. Hopke for the visit, we go out into the street, stop and think.
I ask Yente:
— Well, what do you say to that?
— I knew I had rheumatism, but I didn't want to tell you; I wanted the [doctor] to tell you. Now do you know?
— What good does it do me that I know, when there's no money? How can I afford seven or eight hundred dollars for Pistyan?
— And if I die, will it be better? — asks Yente.
— Hard to say... maybe yes and maybe no.. If I soon get another little wife, a prettier one, a younger one, a quieter one, it will be better. And if I get an older one, an uglier[?] one, a bigger screamer, it will be worse, much worse!
— There you go again with your wisecracks. Doesn't it bother you at all that I have rheumatism?
— And if it does bother me, so what? Of course[?] it bothers me; but what can I do?
— You know what? Let's try[?] — go to a second doctor, says Yente.
— Throw away another 20 złoty?
— It's worth 20 złoty to hear what he'll say; maybe he'll say something different.
— He'll certainly say something different. I already know the local doctors.
— Let's see for ourselves.
And we went off to a second doctor, a man with a name.
When we came in, we were told to sit and wait for our "turn".
The waiting room was packed with sick people, and everyone was waiting.
The public has nothing to do, so it talks — and what does it talk about, the public? About illnesses, operations, medicines, hospitals and about doctors.
Says one Jewish woman with a swollen nose and thick lips and blotches on her face, whose dress is much, much longer at the back[?]: this doctor once saved my sister from death. He, the doctor, was driving to a patient in his car, and on the way he ran over and killed a young woman of 32; and my sister was supposed to be in that area that day and wasn't — had she been at that very spot at that very minute, she would have been killed. That means she was saved from death.
Another woman speaks up, a younger one, a modern[?] one: "Madam, you are — forgive me — a cow."
Well, well! At once a war broke out between the two women, and it didn't take long before both were pulling each other's hair, and both shouted and shrieked, and one could[?] barely, with great trouble, pull them apart.
We all laughed. Only one young man with a bandaged hand remarked: "That's what two Yentes say — woe to their husbands."
My Yente wanted to jump out and show the young man who she was.
But I barely managed, in fear, to calm her down.
And now comes our turn. We go into the doctor's room. Yente is questioned, examined; the doctor ponders and says: "There's nothing wrong with you, you've talked yourself into being ill. Go home and don't be silly. All you need is a compress [—], take a cold bath every morning, or a Priessnitz compress, don't laugh[?] much, don't eat fatty foods, sleep on your right side and keep your mouth shut... Sleeping with an open mouth is very unhealthy; it's enough that the mouth is open all day long..."
On the way out from the doctor, Yente told me she already felt a little easier...
Meanwhile it's quiet, hush, at my home. Especially at night: Yente obeys the doctor and sleeps with her mouth shut...
B. Kondner[?].
Under the Sign of Peace and Unity

(For the general meeting of the Sosnowiec Artisans' Association)
It is an old rule: to destroy is very easy, to build up — enormously hard. Much toil, time, effort, devotion and harmonious cooperation are necessary to put up a useful building; with the help of a little bit of dynamite, on the other hand, the most beautiful palace flies into the air within a few seconds.
The creative capacities of the average person are very limited and reach only up to a certain marked limit. The main thing is — to create, to build. And in the course of building comes the completion, the perfecting. Mistakes and disappointments are not ruled out. Every work has its sunshine and its shadow. The "one-hundred-percent" person has not yet been born. Naturally the eye of the observer, of the onlooker from the side[?], notices especially the mistake and aims its sharp critical arrows at the creating "bird"[?]. But it is more than certain, and easy to understand, that this very same mistake (if not a bigger one!) would have been committed by the critic himself, had he been in the position of the one giving the report...
Certainly there is not the slightest doubt that criticism — calmly thought-out and objective criticism — is a healthy "dessert" after every activity report. Criticism for criticism's sake, however — a "lo ya'aleh ve-lo yavo" [neither here nor there] tactic — is absolutely harmful.
There are born intriguing natures that cannot bear any calm and peaceful cooperation. There are also stormy souls who are first-class fighters[?] in a period of storm and stress — but for normal, harmonious constructive work they are, despite their considerable talents, not capable.
At a general annual members' meeting of an economic organisation, all the psychologically and socially differently-thinking currents come to prominent expression.
———
Apart from the general, very severe economic crisis in the country, by which the Jewish artisan has perhaps been hit hardest of all, the past year of activity was, for the Jewish artisans' movement in general, very rich in critical moments, and only thanks to the restraint, the calm character and the sense of responsibility of individuals, leading persons, was the integrity of the Sosnowiec organisation preserved — more plainly: a catastrophe was averted.
As a factual illustration the following three chapters will fully suffice, for instance: 1) the split in the central leadership (the expulsion from the C.C. [Central Committee] and the executive of a number of respected, deserving artisan activists); the last elections to the Sejm and Senate (the separate political line of the Zagłębie Supreme Council, created and led by the Sosnowiec organisation) and 3) the historic date of 15 December 1930 and the changed relationship (for the better) towards the Kielce Chamber of Crafts.
As an economic organisation the Artisans' Association is a thoroughly apolitical and non-partisan (better[?]: supra-partisan) institution, a river with all kinds of fish. The successful carrying-out of various general campaigns must therefore be described as one of the most important merits of the outgoing board.
Certainly there will be members who will find, precisely in the favourable[?] positions, as usual, "partners in sin". With such comrades it is by no means an easy thing to conduct a debate of persuasion. It only needs to be stated in weighed[?] truth and lawfully[?]: the outgoing board was ready at any time, at the slightest demand of the membership, to give up its place to those who consider themselves more worthy to hold board offices. But such bold office-seekers[?] did not come forward, and the board had to and had to [carry on], being supported by the confidence of the broad mass of members. That, it seems, is convincing enough.
———
Naturally the programme of a general meeting divides into 2 main parts: a report is given[?] on the work done so far, and on the basis and consideration of events the guidelines for future activity are marked out.
The chief merit of the outgoing board was without doubt peace and unity. Although not everyone was of the same opinion on all matters, harmonious cooperation nevertheless ran like a red thread through the whole year's activity, and every important decision was always taken unanimously — beginning with the renovation of the premises[?], the reorganisation of the guilds, evening courses, members' talks, and ending with tax interventions and the struggle against decrees against artisans. Not all fingers are equal — but the hand is one and binds them all together into one whole.
So it was in the whole past — and the same we must expect from the whole future:
— peace and unity.
———
Heavy clouds have recently pressed upon the artisans' sky: the guild law, master's examinations, an enormous influx of new small masters, workers who have become independent (even[?] the competition of the most capable[?] element), the tax burden and the like — troubles and calamities grow overnight.
Let the members' ranks therefore close more tightly, let them band together[?] more firmly arm in arm, shoulder to shoulder, in the continuing[?] hard but not desperate struggle for the just interests of the Jewish artisan, for the easing of the critical situation!
The chief foundations of every creative, of every productive work are — peace and unity. Let therefore the meeting of those who draw their pedigree from R' Yitzhak the Smith and R' Yohanan the Shoemaker, those who live from the work of their own fingers and the sweat of their own brow, proceed under the sign of peace, unity and good will, under the sign of the General Central Jewish Artisans' Union: "In unity is our strength"!
A. G-k.
The World Federation „Maccabi“

The world federation „Maccabi“, which embraces all organisations that stand on national ground and occupy themselves with sport, has arranged a week in which the idea of physical education was propagated and money was collected for the „Maccabi“ fund.
Physical education. One must admit that the idea is not popular in the Jewish street — or, more correctly, it is not yet popular enough. True, thousands of Jews came to a match of Vienna Hakoah. Before the match and after it people talked more about the event than about the greatest and best cantor or preacher who comes to town. It was an event of the first rank. It is also true that a match arranged by our home-grown heroes draws a bigger crowd than the best lecture, and if the newspaper happens to leave something out of its report, a fuss is made, delegations run about, and the error has to be „corrected“. Accordingly it turns out that the interest in sport is very great and that it is the most popular occupation among us. Nevertheless it seems to me that the matter of physical education is still not properly spread among us and does not take the place in our life that is due to it.
We live in an era of sport. Everything people do, whether for pleasure or from necessity, is in our time transformed into a sport, a race, a wager. Ever since men and horses have lived in the world, a man walked and a horse ran. The man walked because he had to walk, and the horse ran because it was driven. Today horse-running has been made into a sport, and thousands of people come to the races („wyścigi“), wager[?] fortunes on which horse will reach the finish first. And the cult of horse-racing was invented by the English; for them it is the greatest event, everyone comes to the race, even the King in person must come. If he does not come, it is a scandal, he has insulted... whom, the horses or the people, I do not know. The race-course at Derby[?] near London is the place where the ladies come in the newest toilettes. From there the fashion first spreads over the whole world.
People walk because they must, because they want to. So it was always thought. Then came sport and showed that people can not only walk but also run, and it became a run with a wager, with a championship. Who has not heard of the Finn Nurmi, who beat the world champion Dr. Peltzer! And of the Polish student Petkiewicz[?], who outran Nurmi, you have surely heard. In short, man and his gait, slower or faster gait, has become a sport, a game, a wager.
And fighting, too, is an „article“. Father used even to say that only[?] drunkards fight. But on this point too he lived in error. Fighting is an art — one learns that from the American „gener“[?] Dempsey, who has the strongest hands and delivers the real punch. He is more famous and beloved in the world than the philosopher James[?]; as for earning money, that is another story: what such a fist-fighter earns with one successful punch, the philosopher does not earn in eighty years of hard toil and labour.
And why only running, hitting and fighting? Other human strengths and weaknesses are also a matter of sport today. These days in Sofia, the capital of Bulgaria, a smoking contest took place, and whoever managed to smoke more cigarettes (papirosy) within a set time remained the winner.
I know that sport is little popular among us. We have not yet properly appreciated its significance. The point is to overtake, to surpass, to do everything faster, nimbler; and whoever attains perfection, whoever really runs faster, gives the better punch, is indeed the victor in life as well. Today[?] the song goes: „one walks on it with a small step“. The Sabbath, when one counts the steps and takes care not to take too great a stride — alas, there is no Sabbath any more; today one must take big steps, today one must know how to run; if one walks slowly one really comes too late. And this very task the „Maccabi“ has taken upon itself, and therefore the action it has undertaken, the „Maccabi“ week, is a sympathetic enterprise and deserves to be supported.
Sh. Y. S.
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion (Va'era)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and styled by Y. Y.
Parashat Va'era.
—o—
a) "And God spoke unto Moses" (Ex. 6:2).
"He spoke with him in judgment, because he had spoken harshly, saying: 'Why hast Thou dealt ill with this people'" (Rashi).
A leader must stand up for his people to such an extent that he has the audacity to demand justice for the people even from God Himself, so to speak. And therefore, when Moses took the boldness to hurl a plain [?] reproach at God Himself — "Why hast Thou dealt ill with this people" — when God, so to speak, saw that he did not spare even Him when the good of the Jews was at stake, then — "He spoke with him: judgment": God said to him: you may judge the Jews, you are worthy to be their leader.
Rabbi Meirl of Przemyślany.
—o—
b) "I will bring you out... I will deliver you... I will redeem you.. I will take you" (Ex. 6:6–7).
Because of these four expressions we drink four cups. (Midrash)
R' Yaakov, the Rabbi of Lublin, with his little boy (later Rabbi R' Heshel) were once in the town of Mezh [?] (Reichslager [?]) and stayed "with" a rich man who, as is the way of such men, was also a miser. He treated them to wine in tiny little glasses. The sharp-witted little boy soon found a way to needle [?] the stingy [?] rich man and said: "Daddy, when we said at Passover: 'Rabbi Yehuda gave them mnemonics: DeTZaKh, ADaSH, BeAHaV', I wondered: why did Rabbi Yehuda find [?] it necessary to abbreviate the plagues? Now I understand it. Rabbi Yehuda did it for the misers. If such a rich man honours his Passover with the four cups as we have now, in such teeny cups, and on top of that one must spill [?] ten drops at the plagues — what will be left in the little cups? A plague... Therefore he abbreviated it, so that one spills [?] only three times, and seven plagues remain over [?]. And it seems — concluded little Heshele — that Rabbi Yehuda was concerned that misers are found only at hand [?], for 'Rabbi Yehuda gave in them (hands [?]) signs'; his deed [?] was meant as a warning [?] for the fat [?] rich men..."
R' Itzikl of Volozhin and the Lubavitcher Rebbe (the author of "Tzemach Tzedek") were once summoned to Petersburg to hold a disputation with a priest about the blood libel. The priest wants to prove "explicitly" that Jews need Christian blood at Passover, since Rabbi Yehuda says DeTZaKh, ADaSH, BeAHaV. The acronym DeTZaKh says: "Dam tzrichim kulchem" — "you all need blood" (we all need blood).
What does one answer such an enemy of Israel?
R' Itzikl speaks up: the acronyms say something else: DeTZaKh — "Dovrim [printed: Zovrim] tzorreinu kulam" (our enemies just talk), ADaSH — "Alilat dam sheker" (in truth the blood libel is false), and BeAHaV — "Bnei Avraham chalila zot" (God forbid that Abraham's children should do such a thing).
—o—
c) "The swarms" (Ex. 8:16 [so printed]).
Arov was a plague in which all the beasts and wild animals fell upon Egypt. According to the Midrash, the "lice" also came along among them. One asks: the lice had already been a plague of their own, so why do they come a second time?
A rich man celebrated his son's wedding with a ten-day feast. On the first day the relatives were invited, on the second — the Torah scholars, on the third — poor people, etc. There was one guest who sat at the table on the first day, the second day and the third day. A servant asks him: How can this be? Each day is meant for different people. He answers: the first day is meant for relatives, the second — for Torah scholars, the third — for poor people. I am a relative, a Torah scholar and a pauper all at once, so I come on all the days...
At first the lice came as specially invited guests; afterwards, when all the wild animals were mobilised, the lice are in-laws too...
Ohel Yitzchak.
—o—
d) "Show a wonder for you" (Ex. 7:9).
According to the plain sense of the verse it should say "show me a wonder", not "for you".
Moses should have spoken to Pharaoh thus: I know that your sorcerers can also display black magic. But they forget [?] that only now; they themselves know that it is worth nothing. Therefore "show a wonder for you" — give me a wonder in which you yourselves will also believe, "for you".
Rabbi Elimelech of Leżajsk.
—o—
e) "And also the ground whereon they are" (Ex. 8:17).
According to the Midrash, all the wild and domestic animals from foreign lands came with the Arov. But this is difficult: there is a creature, "Avnei [?] ha-Sadeh" [the 'man of the field'], about which the books say that it is tied to the earth by a cord. How did it come?
To this the verse says: "and also the ground whereon they are" — the piece of earth came along...
The Vilna Gaon.
—o—
f) "The Lord is righteous, and I and my people are wicked" (Ex. 9:27).
Would Pharaoh really have called himself wicked?
He spoke thus: "The Lord is righteous, and I" — I and God, we are both righteous; but "my people are the wicked" — my people are wicked.
Rabbi Yehoshua'le of Ostrowa [?].
• • •
The Radzyń Rebbe, R' Mordechai Yosef of blessed memory, once said:
In "Brich Shmei" we say "that You prolong our life in goodness, and that I be counted among the righteous". What connection does living long have with being a tzaddik?
But the meaning is this:
The world keeps getting worse. The heretics of old would today be perfect tzaddikim. That is the meaning of the prayer we ask of the Master of the Universe: let us live long, and we too will one day be tzaddikim...
Only Rumours?

[Editorial — Poland, the economic crisis and government policy.] And once again the air begins to fill with rumours that it is coming, here comes the government's great, planned relief work; that the long-yearned-for struggle against the economic crisis is coming and on its way. There is talk of gigantic, planned investment works which are to give employment to tens of thousands of hungry unemployed in the country; the investment works are to be undertaken on a large scale, hundreds of kilometres of highways will be built, the railway network will be extended, they will begin to drain the Polesie marshes, etc., etc.
In general — if this time we are really not to be disappointed, if it really turns out that this time it is not one of those dishes with which the fantasy of every starved stomach so loves to play, then we truly stand before the first great deeds of the government.
If the rumours prove true, it will be a proof that the May camp [Piłsudski's Sanacja camp, since the May 1926 coup] has finally, after barely 5 years, come to the conviction that the most burning problem for the state is not changes to the constitution, but helping the country out of the economic crisis and the population out of its hard and bitter want. And if so, the hand of peace must necessarily be stretched out to all those with whom war has been waged until now.
We now have to deal in Poland with a system of government that does not hold with words. Words, according to [?] this system, are superfluous; the main thing is deeds. Such a system is perhaps quite good from one side, but it also has a second side, that of morale, and this side is no longer so good. Because information to the population is doled out sparingly and the country is constantly faced with accomplished facts, the rumours multiply. And after the rumours always comes disappointment, which leaves behind a much greater hangover [Katzenjammer] than before — and that is bad, very bad.
Times in Poland have never yet been as bad as now. The economic crisis in the country has almost done its work. There are by now almost more unemployed than employed workers, more people without a livelihood than people with one, more ruins than firmly founded [?] workshops, and the firms that still stay on their feet are [uncertain word] that the slightest further aggravation of the crisis can overturn. This is no time to feed anyone with hollow rumours of salvation that may come to nothing [Yiddish idiom: "end in an attic"]
Real deeds! A practical start of a great, ramified rescue and relief work must be undertaken — and undertaken right now.
This time the rumours must no longer remain mere rumours...
Ps.—
"Literarishe Bleter" Enter Their Eighth Year

[Literature and press — "Literarishe Bleter".] It is one of the rare cases in the history of the Jewish press that a literary periodical should appear without interruption for seven whole years. The "Literarishe Bleter" [the Warsaw Yiddish literary weekly] have achieved this very wonder.
It is owed to the special interest of the Jewish reader in this periodical. From the very beginning the "Literarishe Bleter" set themselves the task of informing the Jewish reader of everything that goes on in the Jewish literary world, as well as in the Jewish theatre, art and the cultural world; the most important literary and theatrical phenomena of the whole world are also regularly [described] [?] in the "Bleter".
For several years now the "Literarishe Bleter" have been the centre at which news arrives, essays about the various attempts and experiments of the creative Jewish spirit, and from which reports go out again, greetings to all, all who live by the vital force of the living Jewish word. And it is no wonder that all those connected with Jewish creation — the artist-painters, actors, cultural activists — regard the "Literarishe Bleter" as their own organ.
In every issue the "Literarishe Bleter" print poems, selected [?] articles on the most important cultural and literary problems; pictures are also brought, reproductions of theatre productions and of works of art. Especially rich is the chronicle section of the "Literarishe Bleter".
The "Literarishe Bleter" link the scattered and dispersed Jewish cultural communities. The most important Jewish writers and artists take part regularly in the "Literarishe Bleter".
It must be added that the "Literarishe Bleter" are published by the Kletskin publishing house without any profit whatsoever. Thus they deserve to be supported by the friends of the Yiddish language and literature.
Apart from the issues themselves, the "Literarishe Bleter" have for several years been giving very important book premiums. So far there have been given Romain Rolland's "Jean-Christophe", Knut Hamsun's best works, Leo Tolstoy's novels and stories, H. G. Wells — "World History", Thomas Mann's "The Magic Mountain". In the year 1931 Maxim Gorky's novels will be given.
Bright Prophecies (A Short Feuilleton)

[Feuilleton.] An English scholar prophesies that in the year 1931 a kind of accumulator will be invented which will collect sunlight by day, and at night the darkness of the streets will be lit with that light.
(From the press.)
The world says: "A fool is half a prophet." But there is another saying too: "When a fool throws a stone into the water, ten wise men cannot take it out."
Years ago the inventor of the mechanical machine was also a "fool". The inventor of electricity, of the railway, of ships, of the cinema, of flying — all these inventors were in their time "fools"; now they are all wise men, and who knows whether in the future our new "fool" of [?] the "eternal day" will not also be a wise man...
Ah, if this "foolishness" should become wisdom, if this achievement should become a fact, it will be a fresh death-blow to a whole row of darkness-seekers.
First of all the power station [elektrownia] will get a blow. What will one need the power station for, if one will press a button and brightness will pour out over the broad [?], great world? No illuminated advertisements will be made, no night trams will run, the night concerts will close, no "night sessions" of the kehilla, the town council etc. will take place.
The worst share [?] will fall to married women and married men who like to snatch a night-time date [?] in a garden or in a "[—] alley" — the light will "catch" [?] them at every step...
The worst defeat will be suffered by the "lords of the night" — the thieves. It will be impossible to do any "masmatn" [? thieves' cant], impossible to go to an "opening" of a door, of a till — the light will "kill" their "pyanushke" [? thieves' cant].
Who else will suffer from the night-light — Jews; Jews will not be able to bless the new moon... [printed "mekhadesh zayn", for "mekadesh"]
But nevertheless — let us wait for the bright prophecies. Perhaps...
A—K.
Rabbi Hager's Stay in Antwerp

In the „Yidishe Prese“ [Jüdische Presse], which appears in Antwerp, we read the following notice about the visit of Rabbi Hager.
The „Mizrachi“ took advantage of the stay of Rabbi[?] Hager, the Rabbi of Sosnowiec, one of the eminent Mizrachi rabbis, in Antwerp, and organised an Oneg Shabbat with the participation of the honoured guest.
Rabbi[?] Hager inspired the assembled with his wonderfully beautiful, substantial speech and made a great impression.
Rabbi Hager spoke about the meaning of Chanukah, the Maccabean struggle, the present situation in Eretz Israel, and Judaism; his speech was interwoven with a series of midrashim and sayings of the Sages. He turned especially to the youth, that they should strengthen their work for a Jewish Eretz Israel.
A heartfelt „yasher koach“ from all those assembled accompanied the calm, beautiful speech, which gave the listeners a spiritual delight.
After that Rabbi Hager spoke at the tea evening of the „Mizrachi“ and at the Chanukah celebration of the „Sha'arei Torah“ yeshiva.
Communiqué of the Shekel Committee for 5691

At the last liquidation meeting, which took place on Wednesday night at the premises of the Zionist Organisation in Będzin, the sale of shekels for 5690 was wound up.
The Revisionists together with Betar sold 76 shekels, „Hitachdut“ — 44, Herzliya — 36, Gordonia — 13, Tze'irei Mizrachi — 10, Mizrachi — 10, Poalei Zion — 8, Hashomer Haleumi — 5.
The Zionist organisation „Negoi“[?] returned (tsu pum[?]) as many as it had taken.
Remaining in debt for shekels sold: the organisation „Chayot“[?] for 40 shekels, 60 zł.; Mr. Magnes[?] for 10 shekels — 15 zł.
For the year 5691, 3,500 shekels were brought[?], which have been almost entirely sold.
At the meeting the motion of Mr. A. Diamant was adopted, to protest most strongly against the attempts of several authorities[?] who are working[?] to postpone the 17th Zionist Congress.
At the same time all Polish members of the Actions Committee are called upon to ensure by all means that the 17th Congress take place on the appointed date, 24 February.
The resolution was sent to the Central Shekel and Central Election Committee, and also to the appointed[?] chairman of the Actions Committee, Mr. H. Farbstein.
From the Book Table

A book of quiet beauty. On „Shmuel and David“ — a poem by Yechiel Lerer, Gitlin publishers, Warsaw, 1930.
There are[?] summer birds which sing before the sun rises. Then they soar very high, and from there they send down their quiet, sweet trills and fill the whole space of the sky with quiet joy and exaltation.
To this kind of singer belongs, without doubt, the young, talented poet Y. Lerer.
If in his poems until now Lerer sang simply for the sake of song, his latest great poem „Shmuel and David“ is of a very broad and beautiful scope.
Through quiet, tender images the poet leads us through the whole struggle and power-contest between David and Saul, so that we see everything before us as if alive.
It is enough for the reader to read only the first page, and at once he is carried away and captivated by the quiet tone, by the most lofty, beautiful poetic images with their „begosn“[?], with the scent of the field, „glum“[?] and the breath[?] of the forest — and the reader will no longer get up[?] but will quietly read[?] chapter after chapter to the end.
At that time, when Saul is entangled in a war with the Philistines, and the prophet Samuel, sent by God, comes to Jesse, David's father, and tells Jesse to bring from the field all his seven sons, who are strong as cedars, swift as the stag on the mountains of Judah, and all fit to wear the crown — the prophet nevertheless stops at Jesse's youngest son, at little David, who also comes from the field, called by his father:
„A young shepherd boy, his cheeks still rosy,
with a shepherd's song in his mouth:
O my little sheep! I have left them alone,
a hungry wolf may suddenly fall upon them,
and who will help them then, the weak ones?
You will help them! — calls out the prophet —
the innocent sheep against bloody wolves,
his brothers in battle against Phil[istine][?] foes,
with royal ointment I moisten his limbs,
and anoint you forever as shepherd of the people,
to guard my guiltless lambs.“
And when the war drags on and the camp grows restless, old Jesse sends the youngest of his sons, little David, to go[?] and see what his brothers are doing, and then[?] little David sets out on the road.
„Woe unto you, Goliath, you giant of the Philistines!
Somewhere a little shepherd has now left his night's resting-place,
not waiting for the morrow;
something important he has surely forgotten in his mind,
if he runs so early on the road to the battlefield;
had you seen it, Goliath, you would have smiled with contempt.
But laugh on, you strong ones, sure of your arm,
at shepherds' tales[?], at golden dreams!
If in the dark of night, while you sleep so securely,
one awakens, roused from the stillness,
chosen[?] by God himself, [—] starred[?],
what then is your might[?], your arm, you yourselves worth!
A shepherd from Bethlehem has now left the sheep[?],
the knapsack on his shoulders, the staff in his hand,
guided by the stars, guarded[?] by their wink[?],
he wants in a doze[?] [—] to hand over!
To the battlefield he runs, indeed[?],
and[?] mighty deeds [—] —
grant me, God, just once such a night.“
And when the war drags on still and a great unrest has seized the whole camp and all the young giants go about with a quiet sorrow in their eyes, the poet shows us, in the chapter „Shlitim[?] and Ramah“, the picture of how the girls used to go every day with their pitchers to the little spring for water and used to mirror their faces and [—][?] in the water; but since all the young men went off to war, all the girls have sunk into quiet grief.
And once, when the girls ask at the little spring whether their beloved will come home whole from the war, the little spring answers them:
„Why do you ask me, little sisters [—][?]: if your beloved return, you will rejoice with all your heart; if not — you will lament and rend your clothes; but I will flow — you may weep or laugh — carefree as always, on my appointed way.“
And after David has thus[?], unexpectedly even to himself, won so great a victory over Goliath, only then does the struggle begin, at first quietly, on the part of Saul, who feels how power slips out of his hands and passes to David. The futile persecutions begin against the young hero, who had won such a[?] decisive[?] victory over the Philistines.
But David extricates himself from all dangers and remains the victor. And in the last battle, when Saul wants to try his own fate and himself leads the last battle — he loses, because his fortune has turned[?] from him, on account of the sin of the innocent blood shed of the priests of Nob and the little babes[?], whom Saul had ordered all slaughtered, and they all now lie slaughtered; a shudder seizes him for his bloody deed, which cries out to heaven, and here his downfall begins.
The encouragement of his son Jonathan does not help, who himself runs first into battle with his brothers; the battle is lost and Jonathan falls first together with his brothers in battle, and when the Philistines encircle Saul from all sides, he falls on his own sword and death releases him from madness[?].
Through the whole quiet poem there runs like a red thread the wholeness of David, the brokenness of Saul and the beautiful love of Jonathan for David.
The book is clean[?], properly published, and deserves to be read.
G. Sternberg, Warsaw.
What's New in Zagłębie?

[Page 7 — "Zaglembier Tsaytung" No. 3. Date boxes:] Friday, 27 Tevet 5691 — Piątek 16 stycznia 1931 [Friday, 16 January 1931].

BĘDZIN

The rise in the rent tax is not on the agenda.
So the Council of Ministers assures.

In connection with the newspaper reports that the government intends to raise the rent tax ("dire-gelt"), the board of the local Merchants' Association sent the following declaration to the competent authority:
"In view of the widespread rumours that the government is considering a project to strengthen the building fund by raising the rent tax, the board of the Będzin Merchants' Association feels it its duty to draw the attention of the government bodies to the fact that the project has caused unrest in merchant circles, since raising the rent tax will further aggravate the present, already so severe, crisis."
This week the Merchants' Association received a reply from the Council of Ministers, announcing that the matter of raising the rent tax is for the time being not on the agenda.

Conference of small traders' representatives with the head of the tax office.

On Saturday a delegation of the Small Traders' Association presented itself to the new head (naczelnik) of the local tax office, Dr. Kru-Kopka[?].
The delegation, consisting of Messrs. S. Cymberknop[?], D. Nitler[?] and D. Gutensztajn, handed the head a memorandum in which were set out[?]: 1) the crisis now being undergone in Poland by the merchant class in general and the Jewish small traders in particular, because of which they are unable, with the best will, to meet the heavy tax burdens; and 2) that the Jewish small traders should be granted equal rights and that their representatives [be admitted] to all bodies where matters concerning the Jewish small traders are dealt with.
The head received the delegation very cordially, and in his reply stressed that he is aware of the difficult situation of the merchants and will therefore manoeuvre between what is possible and the obligations of the taxpayers.
The conference lasted about 2 hours. It is to be hoped that the new head will endeavour, as far as his possibilities allow, to ease the heavy tax burden at the present moment.

Zionist leaders in Będzin.

At the beginning of next week editor A. Goldberg and Dr. M. Klumpel[?] are coming to Będzin on important current Zionist matters.

Came in from the street and died.

The day before yesterday 56-year-old Lea Rozenberg came in from the street to her flat. On arriving home Mrs. Rozenberg said she was not feeling well and fainted. Despite all rescue measures the woman died within a short time.

The houses will get new numbers.

This month, at the demand of the Kielce voivode, a new numbering of the houses and of the unbuilt plots will be carried out throughout the town.

Military booklets must be in order.

This week Mr. Cymberknop[?] received an urgent summons from the starostwo (district office) to present himself, Mr. C., on Wednesday at the starostwo, [room?] 25[?].
When Mr. C. received the summons he was frightened and could hardly wait, in great suspense, for the appointed date to learn what he was accused of.
On arriving at the starostwo Mr. C. learnt that he was accused of his military booklet (which he has had for over 9 years already) not being in order; for this Mr. C. was fined 5 zł.

2,000 zł for institutions.

The prematurely deceased Adolf Sperbasz[?], who was known as a quiet philanthropist, donated before his death 500 zł to the "Dobroczynność" (charity society) and 500 zł to the orphans' shelters (ochronki). In addition the family of the deceased allotted a thousand to a number of institutions.

Registered letters until 7 p.m.

Thanks to the efforts of the Merchants' Association, registered letters are now dispatched at the post office until 7 in the evening.

Meeting of commercial employees.

This Saturday evening a meeting of all commercial employees of Będzin will be held in the "Piast" hall, with very important questions on the agenda. The attendance of all commercial employees is most important.

Turnover declarations.

The Merchants' Association asks us to point out that the turnover declarations (zeznania) for the year 1930 must be submitted by 15 February.

Sosnowiec
Kehilla representatives "care" about Jewishness...
On Tuesday evening a meeting took place in the home of Mr. K. Langer[?] with the participation of representatives of the kehilla board and council.
The agenda of the meeting was the budget for the year 1931, but at the proposal of several kehilla representatives a very "important" matter was dealt with at the meeting, one that illustrates how far[?] the Sosnowiec communal leaders are absorbed[?] in "important" communal matters.
The matter consists in this: the town cantor holds his tallit on his shoulder while praying...
It was indeed resolved to turn to the cantor and demand that he throw the tallit over [his head] when he prays.
— And yet[?] people have complaints against our kehilla representatives that they are not active[?].
—o—
The "domestic peace" among the temporary "city fathers".
In the appointed[?] "Rada Komisaryczna" [commissarial city council] a conflict broke out between Commissioner Kuśniak and Councillor Wieczorek[?]. The conflict arose because Mr. Kuśniak insulted Wieczorek[?] over a certain matter. Things went so far that Wieczorek[?] turned to the Commissioner with a letter stating that he resigns his mandate.
