The Mirage of Livelihood

[Election slogan across the top of the page:] 2 2 All Sosnowiec voters vote only for List 2 2

It is probably a natural phenomenon that among us people have stopped talking about livelihood itself — about the fact that from day to day more and more branches of Jewish subsistence are being broken off, about the need to create new sources of income for Jews — and instead people talk constantly about matters of credit, borrowing, repaying, protests [of bills], auctions and the like.
For this kind of credit has become among us almost the only, or at any rate the most important, source of subsistence.
People keep asking: if Jews have nothing and earn nothing, then what do they live on? And one finds no answer to that — and that is indeed the right answer: they live on borrowing.
True, borrowing and repaying is not productive work; and all the more so if one does not repay — then it is certainly not productive. But that is how it is: people have already been torn away from the original branch of livelihood, they hang in the air and feed themselves on surrogates of bill-of-exchange dealings.
So there has arisen in the press a dispute of the authorities as to how this "livelihood" should be carried on further.
Some newspapers hold that a source of sustenance must be preserved so that it should not be spoiled; if we live on credit, one must see to it that the credit is not torn up; for that it is necessary that debts be paid, and whoever does not pay should have it taken from him by force; and since [?] the Polish laws make the process of collection by executions (distraint) difficult, the law must be changed and the court system reorganised — credit must be put on a firm footing, and then one will be able to live on it.
This theory may perhaps hold for Christians, for whom credit is not yet the main source of subsistence. Among Jews, however, an opposite opinion has arisen.
Whoever looks at Jewish life even from the side can see that the Jewish merchant has lately been occupied not so much with his business as with credit operations and tax operations. The original złoty taken in from sales has been pushed into the background by the contrived, tormented patchwork of borrowing, paying, prolonging, snatching and juggling.
If one were to press an average Jewish merchant to pay, he is finished at once. All his juggling is, after all, limited to putting things off.
Therefore among Jews the demand is, on the contrary, to slacken the reins, not to allow any auctions, so that the little wheel keeps turning — and then Jews will have "a livelihood"..
This is our highest certificate of poverty. Neither by pressing nor by slackening will it be possible to bring about a situation in which millions of people live on credit alone, if they have no running income from their businesses.
When the borrowed złoty is used up, no other comes in its place — neither now nor later — and it must inevitably lead to bankruptcy.
A bankruptcy not of individuals, but of the whole system.
We must therefore not let ourselves be misled by the mirage. We must return to the source, think and talk about livelihood itself.
We must demand, without ceasing, that the field of Jewish livelihoods should not be narrowed, but on the contrary, that for Jews at least narrow little doors to new fields of subsistence should be opened. We must not grow weary of talking about it, just as it is not loathsome to seek a cure for an old chronic illness.
We must fight our way through to the right to live from our own work and not from fantasy-money. We must multiply our energy in the political struggle for precisely this right. No obstacle may stop us — and certainly no fantasy.
And one of the most dangerous fantasies is the groundless snatch-and-grab borrowing.
P. K.
From the general meeting of the "Linas ha-Cholim" society in Będzin

[Będzin — institutions and society.]
On Sunday a general meeting of the "Linas ha-Cholim" society was held in Będzin, in the society's own premises. The meeting, at which no extraordinary questions had been foreseen — such as that "the old people should be obliged to eat before praying", or that "from this day on the kitchen should not be strict about matters of kashrut" — nevertheless aroused enormous interest among the "sharp" Ger Hasidim, who left their election rally in great haste and came to the meeting.
Later it turned out that the rush had happened on an order "from above": that a member of the board who does not sympathise with the deeds of the Będzin "Agudah" [Agudat Israel] should be struck off.
Before a packed hall the meeting is opened by the chairman Mr. Sz. Ratner, who invites Mr. Max Landau to preside; in the presidium: B. Feltz [?], L. Landner, Y. Katz; secretary — M. Lewin.
Secretary L. Rosenblum delivers reports on the activity in the years 1929 and 1930. The reports show that the annual budget amounts to about 60,000 zł., covered by the municipal (magistrat) subsidies and by the payments for the maternity home.
The report also gives a clear picture of the attitude of the kehilla leaders so far towards the institutions. It is worth noting that of the subsidies for the years 1927, '28, '29 and 1930, which amount to nearly 20,000 zł., the gmina [municipality] has remained in debt for no less than 15 thousand zł.
The report of the maternity home is given by its director, Dr. Ferber. He points out the importance of the institution for the poorest part of the population, but there is still — says the doctor — much to be done so that the institution stands at the proper level. From the statistical material we learn that up to last Sunday 1893 children had been born in the institution (may they multiply).
After the reports thanks are expressed to Dr. Ferber and to the board. At the same time, a protest against the kehilla board for its harassment.
The budget, in the amount of 1·2 [?] thousand zł., is adopted. (The budget includes a sum of 40,000 zł. for enlarging the society's building.
105 persons took part in the elections. The result: almost all the previous members were re-elected. The only change is this: Mr. Ch. Dafner was elected to the board, and Ch. Rozencwajg as deputy.
Under the item "free proposals" the proposal of Mr. Kakatek [?] was adopted, to resume the campaign of night watches [mishmorim, at the bedside of the sick].
What Was Heard, What Was Seen.

[Będzin, Sosnowiec and Dąbrowa — weekly feuilleton; kehilla elections.] Transmitted by Ben Amotz.

Their happiness disturbed..
Sunday morning.
In the street people are still talking about the splendid march of the national [Zionist] youth, which went off on an excursion into strangers' forests; it is told that for a whole week the organisers of the excursion turned to a whole series of persons who hold the rights to the neighbouring forests, begging that they allow them and give them the chance to enjoy one single day in the forests, but everywhere they received the same answer:
"Nie pozwalamy" [Polish: "we do not permit"]...
The conversation is suddenly broken off and everyone's eyes turn to Third of May Square [Plac 3 Maja], where on a bench by the "mizrach wall" a Jewish couple is sitting; "he" has his arms around "her" and
— resounding kisses ring out...
The scene provokes merriment, the number of the curious grows bigger and bigger, all the traffic "comes to a halt", the crowd is rolling with laughter at the couple.
— They're kissing...
— "Ya sar[?] nishtz sai man wab...im, sai ma ch-ab, yakh" [a garbled phrase in the original, apparently distorted or mimicked speech; not deciphered]
— and a kiss...
In a great hurry a policeman approaches, who is "jealous" [Yiddish eyfer-zikhtig, German eifersüchtig] of "free love", especially on a Sunday, and he drives the crowd apart, and also separates the kissing couple
— their happiness disturbed...

If not for the "power of forgetting"...
It is a clear thing that happy is the man in whose brain there is also a little chamber where the power of forgetting "works"; if not for that, it is hard to believe that anything would ever have been created in the world — why create, work, chase after money, wealth, if suddenly a voice is heard calling:
— "Little man, come home now"...
Ah, if people did not forget what was and what will be, the world would have had no existence; the "Aguda" [Agudat Israel] would not have revived paragraph 20, and the Dąbrowa [Dąbrowa Górnicza] national activists would not have invented special places with "specific interests".
Here before us lies a document dated 1924; kehilla elections took place then too, and the national activists then distributed election appeals (in Polish, of all languages), in which the Jewish voters in Dąbrowa were urged to "cut out the boils, the religious sect, the parasites, those who robbed provisions from widows and orphans, the..."
"Times change": in the year 1931 the boils have become flowers, the thieves and the parasites — new creatures with specific interests...
— Fortunate is humanity, which possesses a hidden treasure
— the power of forgetting...

Holy "miracles".
In the "Kapital" hall, at the meeting of list 16. On the platform stands a rabbi and speaks; from his mouth pour pearl-like sayings, sharp-witted quips, parables, and above all:
— he tells of "miracles and wonders".
— Of whom do you think?
— Of the "Torah-true" youth, who are brought up according to Carlebach's "Shulchan Aruch".
And the rabbi relates:
"My eyes have seen wonders: on Friday night the mizrach [eastern] wall in the Sosnowiec synagogue was clean of every inscription and looked like a mizrach wall in a synagogue.
How surprised I was — the rabbi cries out — when I saw on Sabbath morning how from the mizrach wall the words shone down:
— Vote for the list...
"I saw myself how young fellows, with 'violets' [black eyes] under their eyes, tore down on the Sabbath the posters of an opposing list.
— Rebbe — an interjection is heard from the assembled — the "miracles" are no news to us; we here can tell of a greater miracle, of "a miracle" when on Friday night, at midnight, the rabbi's seat in the Sosnowiec synagogue was hacked into little pieces...

The "Pożarna Komenda" [Polish: fire brigade]
The Don Cossacks were always the loyal ones, the devoted ones, the ones who fought to the blood; hardly had the smell of revolution made itself felt anywhere in the land, they were sent, the loyal servants, there where they were needed, and it became quiet...
In the Będzin "Aguda" too such a detachment exists: these are older "soldiers" with years-long shtibl traditions, who stand on guard so that the Agudist "positions" are not touched.
This detachment is not used for ordinary work, such as breaking up meetings, giving a welcome to a Mizrachi rabbi and the like — those are cheap articles with which it is not worthwhile for such loyal servants to bother; but when it is a matter of rescuing the "Talmud Torah" from the hands of the sinners, or of striking a person off the board of "Linat ha-Cholim", then a signal is given and the "fire brigade" is ready for service...
And if any of you, Będzin readers, saw how on Sunday afternoon the Itche-Meirs, the Pintches and the Moshes were running and hurrying, you should know that they were running to fulfil a holy mission of...
Let everything stay as it was — so they ordered — except So-and-so son of So-and-so; him one must push away.
— The "fire brigade" carried out its mission, but not completely...

Make way, honour of the Torah...
The day of the kehilla elections is approaching, and the shofar call of the "Guardians of the Torah and Religion" [Shomrei ha-Torah ve-ha-Dat] already resounds again in the Jewish street — "Make room!" Make way [Yiddish makht a vare, from Polish wara], listen to our words, walk in our paths, and above all
— vote only for our holy list...
At the same time a second voice is heard: the voice of a widow, who begs with tears those who are so meticulous about the "Yesodei ha-Torah" [school], that they carry out the ruling and pay her the debt left to her by her late husband, a melamed [teacher] with the "Yesodei ha-Torah" people...
And this ruling was issued not by some Mizrachi rabbi, but by none other than our Będzin rabbinate, which is a close relative of the institution with the splendid name — "Yesodei ha-Torah".
Here is the ruling [in Hebrew in the original]:
"Concerning the dispute between the heirs of the late R. Shlomo, of blessed memory, Lustiger, and the committee of the Yesodei ha-Torah cheder here, between whom there has already been an arbitration [printed: 'bimhem'], and the arbitrators decided that the committee shall give the widow of the aforementioned deceased the sum of 1,650 złoty; but as to the dates of payment they had not yet reached agreement — the matter has now been settled before us: the order of payment of the aforementioned sum of 1,650 złoty shall be thus: the sum of 250 złoty the committee shall give her now in cash, and for the remaining sum of 1,400 złoty the committee shall give her nine bills of exchange [veksln], eight of them each for the sum of 155 złoty and one for the sum of 160 złoty ['zlotes']. As to the dates of payment — one bill each month, and the due date of the first bill shall be the 15th of May of this year, and so on each month on the 15th one bill, so that the due date of the last bill comes to the 15th of January ['stitshen', Polish styczeń] 1932. For the sum of 250 złoty which is to be given to her in cash they shall give her a cheque for the 25th of this month. Note: the sum of 1,650 is apart from the debt that was owed to R. Shlomo, of blessed memory, already in his lifetime [printed: 'bechayav' misspelt]."
So then, make way, for with the Torah in hand one goes to the elections; but do not forget, my esteemed friends [ח״ח], that in that very same Torah there is also the verse:
— "Ye shall not afflict any widow or orphan"...
The Elections and Kehilla Affairs

(Our indifference. — What shall we achieve by it? First of all we must go to the elections.)
People complain that hard times have come, so that every single person has to wage a hard struggle for his existence, and the worst of it is that we do not believe that "my help will come" — how and from where salvation will come. One is used to going through various periods in human life; each of us understands perfectly well that things cannot always be good, just as they are not always bad — before everyone's door the sun must shine one day. The steadfast citizen, the sensible European, therefore takes every crisis for a quite normal phenomenon. One knows that, just as from time to time a storm-wind and an unwelcome hail pass through and cause damage, so exactly does a crisis come too; but like the storm-wind, so too crises are periodic phenomena, passing meteors — so that, true, they bring damage, true, they bring chaos (tohu va-vohu) into normal life, but as soon as they pass they belong to the past, and gradually, slowly, one begins to come to oneself again and the situation becomes normal once more, conditions begin to improve.
Now, however, the worst thing, as said, is that we do not know how long the crisis will last like this, and we begin to fear it as one fears a chronic disease that grows more dangerous the longer it lasts — and that is what brings pessimism into our ranks.
And here we are already facing elections to the Jewish kehillot, and somehow one does not see the interest; something is not as it should have been. Kehilla board members were imposed on us — so we kept hearing all along — and though their term had long since ended, one could not get rid of them; so it is self-evident that the news of electing new boards should have aroused enormous interest, and it remains a riddle when we look at the apathy and indifference that reign in the Jewish world. We are often asked: what has actually happened, that the Jewish street is so frozen towards its own interests? But this, one must explain, has a great deal to do with the crisis. It is surely not so hard to grasp that when one has heavy everyday worries, one has neither the head nor the heart to occupy oneself with public interests, however topical, however urgent, however necessary they may be — priority always goes to the first need, which is a livelihood (parnose): bringing home a living for tomorrow. Yes, life, existence, is the strongest magnetic force, from which we cannot tear ourselves away; as if in iron pincers they remain clamped into everyday life.
So this means that the present apathy is understandable; the reasons are not so hard to understand. But one cannot content oneself with that. True, one's head is not in it, but that still does not mean that it is good so, that one must stay at that.
We hold that precisely at a critical and serious time, when every grosz plays a significant role, we must see to it that we treat all our public affairs with the greatest attention — not to speak of when material complications are also involved. It is well known that we carry our public institutions on our own shoulders — not to speak of the Jewish gminas (communities), which have larger budgets, and everything must be covered by the Jewish population, so that every average Jew is quite heavily taxed. A trifle, how much the Jewish gminas cost us — and what do we get from them? What have they improved and what have they achieved? Are we not ashamed before ourselves to keep repeating that the more they cost the Jewish population, the less and less we get from it as time goes on? Don't we know it? Don't we see it? Don't we feel it? Doesn't it weigh on our shoulders?
And further, the same thing. Once, when the kehilla was no more than a "metim-shtibl" (a house for the dead), it had its mikveh, and when it happened that, God forbid, a poor man died, it buried him for free. Now, however, it is quite different: how many times, for example, has Będzin already given money for the new mikveh, and still one does not see it ever "ripening" — one still stands at the same dead point. Is that not a scandal? Can such affairs be allowed to be conducted like this, without any order and control? Did the town give little for the mikveh — and was a report given to anyone? Was the population shown a public statement of accounts? Is this not public money, which must be reckoned with and for which one must render an account? Is it really permitted to take money from the community at any time, without there being any order, and in return give nobody anything? And what more is needed — the gmina has reached such a sad level that not long ago a poor man died in Będzin and the gmina did not bury him, because there was nobody to pay the burial costs, so that the neighbours had to collect the sum in the street. That is the lofty level at which the present kehillot stand. This means that the kehillot cost us quite considerable sums, from which we not only get nothing, but they sink ever deeper and deeper. The question thus arises whether we can tolerate that the most important institution in the town, which moreover costs us so much money, should find itself in such a sad state? May we allow it? Can we in this case remain indifferent even at so serious a time as we find ourselves in now? Can we afford such luxuries, that money be drawn out of Jewish pockets from which the community will enjoy nothing? We therefore hold that precisely at such a time, when every Jewish grosz comes so hard, one must take an interest in the fate of the kehillot. We cannot, and also may not, allow ourselves to throw money simply to the winds, and therefore we must see to it that we have proper board members — board members to whom we can entrust our kehilla interests, responsible board members in whom we can have full confidence. That is why we must not remain indifferent to the present elections.
The crisis will possibly vanish, the situation will perhaps improve with time, and then people will come to themselves, and when they see the mistake that was made because of the apathetic attitude they will not be able to forgive themselves — but then it will be too late; yesterday cannot be brought back. Therefore one must be alert now, and we must stop for a while and consider whom we shall send as representatives into the Jewish kehilla, who is fit to be our board members, whose aim should be to raise us up.
It is now high time; we already stand before the "Hayom harat olam" (the Day of Judgment) [printed "Khayom"], so that however confused and worried we may be, we must reflect for a while and we must see to choosing the most suitable, most honest and most energetic candidates. We must not forget that as representatives we must have such board members as we need not be ashamed of.
First and foremost one must see to going to the elections, regardless of the fact that the time and the day are not the most suitable. In any case we must prove to the public that the Jewish kehillot interest us and that we want their fate to be ever better and to have a guiding line, so that the representatives have the understanding to build such public enterprises as the people needs.
Let all the movements first of all employ the most varied means so that every person entitled to vote goes to the elections; let every Jewish citizen have the interest and understanding to send there people of whom the Jewish people need not be ashamed. If only a small number of votes is cast, it will thereby show that we do not need this kehilla representation — which in fact we certainly must have, only of course in an ever better edition, in ever better forms. And therefore we have no other counsel but first of all to go to the elections and elect people who are responsible, logical, and who have the interest and understanding to raise up kehilla affairs.
R. Let.

Great sporting event in Lwów.

On 23 August of this year an international shooting match will be opened in Lemberg (Lwów) under the patronage of the President of the State, Mościcki.
The sporting event, which is being held in Poland for the first time, is the 28th meeting of the nations for winning the champion's title in the art of shooting.
Represented at the event will be Brazil, Denmark, Finland, France, Greece, Spain, Norway, Switzerland and Italy, which have announced that they will take part in the sports festival in Lwów.

The poor little old kehilla...

M. Mandelzon
As a newspaper man who, all the same, has a bit of a Jewish heart, I went to pay a sick-call on the old kehilla, whose days are numbered and who is already shuffling, any moment now, into the world of truth.
In what a state I found her is better left untold. I will only say this: may my enemies and your enemies fall from all their greatness and find themselves in her condition, and may we and our friends, as long as we live, be guarded and protected from such things!
The little old woman received me coldly, with a gloomy look, and to my greeting she hardly answered.
"Granny doesn't recognise me?" I asked, astonished.
"Why shouldn't I recognise you?" she answered me listlessly and angrily. "Little blood have you drained from me? Little have you joked at my expense? Not one minute have you given me peace! You always made fun of me."
"Let Granny not be angry with me!" I pleaded with her. "I never meant Granny any harm, God forbid! I only wanted Granny to be a little more modern, more worldly."
"And who didn't want that, who?" she grew even more agitated. "Do you think I don't know what is good and what is beautiful? Your granny, you think, was born such a fanatical, benighted one as you see her now? You reckon it suited me to darken my few years without a crumb of light and joy?"
"Then why did Granny pull such old age upon herself and cling only to the Korban Mincha prayer-book and the Tsene-Rene, and never even go out now and then to catch a bit of fresh air and delight in the beautiful world?"
"What are you asking me for?" the little old woman sighed deeply. "Ask them, those shmendrehotses [?] in their zhupitses [Hasidic coats]! Ask them why! Who made me into such an old Jewess in my best years, if not they? Who, if not they, locked me up in this narrow, stuffy, dark little room, so that I should wither and waste away here? I was young, pretty, full of hope and life; I had a feeling for everything new, important and modern — then they came, took all that away from me and wouldn't let me take even one free step... They were my murderers, my hangmen, and only over them do I have to weep and lament."
"Let Granny not grieve!" I comforted her, deeply moved. "For this Granny will have a fat share in the world to come."
"Don't pour salt on my wounds! Better keep quiet!" the little old woman shouted with all her strength. "What good is 'the world to come' to me when I don't know the taste of 'this world'... But [printed 'arer'] it's lost," she calmed herself at once. "My life is a lost game anyway; if only my daughter, who is now coming to take my place, may have a better, brighter luck than I — if only she at least..."
At this point the door was flung open in haste, and into the little room poured a gang of 'gast-Cossacks' [?] of the famous rabbinical 20th regiment... and, as if racing to grab shirayim [printed 'shrayim'] at the rebbe's table, they threw themselves at the little old woman and started kicking her, pinching, beating, thrashing her to death, shouting meanwhile: "Old hag! With a young man, no less? With such a shaygets, a clean-shaven one, you'll go kissy-kissy and do business?" And they wanted to go at me too and give me the real 'mishkavta' [?]... But at the last minute a lucky idea occurred to me and I let out a cry: "Help, fire! It's burning!" And that saved me, because as soon as they heard of 'fire' and 'light', they were seized with trembling and took themselves off to where the pepper grows — to Ger...
The Promissory Note (Wechsel) — Is a Worthless Scrap of Paper!

We wish to touch here on a very topical and sorely painful matter, which is of particular interest to Zagłębie, where the main nerve is: commerce.
It concerns the enormous lawlessness in the payment of debts and promissory notes, the fact that the court (for civil and commercial matters) can achieve as good as nothing here, and that the whole administration of justice in this respect is a complete fiction.
People talk about putting our credit conditions in order, about the need for an influx of foreign capital into Poland, but the precondition must be the reorganisation of the judiciary.
It has already become a kind of axiom in the world that in Poland only he pays who wants to pay. And if someone has no desire to, one cannot compel him to by normal means.
One files, for example, a lawsuit. One waits for months until the first hearing, and when, with luck, the date is finally set, the debtor puts forward groundless objections, which are examined in further proceedings that are scheduled months ahead. And only after that does an affair of months begin, before it passes through all the various instances, until one finally arrives at the execution (enforcement).
But only here does the 'never-was-and-never-created' nature of the whole business begin to show. The creditor, who already holds the writ of execution, suddenly learns that all his efforts[?] and demands so far were in vain, because the debtor has managed by various means to frustrate the carrying out of the execution (printed 'skvekutsye'). A special breed of petty scribblers and 'hole-in-the-corner lawyers' has already arisen, who undertake [?'brigim'] to have all auctions annulled very quickly.
Above all, the situation in this respect is fatal in [all?] Congress Poland. Literally 95 percent of all executions end with a stock report from the komornik (bailiff) that 'the auction did not take place for lack of buyers', and that is the end of the agonisingly long and costly court procedure.
The komornik becomes the highest instance, which decides finally on the creditor's claims, and the decision is known from the outset...
The debtors know this very well, and to all the various reminders and friendly little letters from the creditors they answer cynically:
'If you want to settle the debt, I'll put down so-and-so much for you. If you won't agree to that, we'll see when and how much you'll get out of it by going to law!'
So much for open debts. It is even worse in the promissory-note procedure. Here there is total lawlessness. A promissory note in Poland has altogether ceased to have any value; it is no longer a document on which one can collect anything. This is perhaps the greatest catastrophe for our credit system. The modern, broadly ramified[?] protection of the creditor (sic; presumably 'debtor') is, in our conditions, one great abuse.
Non-payment has already become a system used en masse; it has already become a psychosis, and economic life suffers from it immeasurably.
An anti-credit atmosphere is being created, i.e. an atmosphere in which domestic credit is burdened and foreign credit is practically non-existent.
And when one speaks with foreign firms about lending to Poland, one often hears the answer:
First reform your judiciary, and only then will we be able to talk about credits!
This painful matter is discussed very broadly and from all sides in the Kraków 'Kurier', and the author reaches the conclusion that the civil and commercial procedure in our judiciary must be radically and fundamentally reformed, if we do not want to go under completely.
M. G—n.
Shloyme-Yone Wants to Become a Dozor

(Monologue of a Będzin Jew with a respectable beard and burdened with daughters.)
— May my colleague Reb Aryeh Leybl live a hundred and twenty-one years, who saw to it with the authorities that in the present kehilla elections Paragraph 20 should apply [the article of the kehilla election rules allowing exclusion of those openly estranged from Judaism], which in plain Jewish language means: beard-shavers, sinners, may-their-names-be-blotted-outniks — 'poshol von!' [Russian: get out!] — out of the kehilla.
Only now do I know that I, Shloyme Yone, can also have the pleasure of becoming a dozor [member of the kehilla board] among our dear Jews, and people will even call me 'Panie dozorca' [Mr. Board-Member]. What, doesn't it suit me? On the contrary, show me a better candidate than me as dozor. And really, I have everything that a man of today will need to have, and you will by no means find anyone better than me. By the way, let me tell you that I have long been waiting for this little bundle; after all, it is simply not nice that such a Jew as I, with a dignified countenance, with an important [ważna], honourable long beard, with half a dozen daughters, the youngest of whom has long been ripe to hear the wedding musicians play — that such a sort of Jew should never yet have been a dozor in the gmina? Fie, it's not nice.
As for your saying 'a beard' — you should know that there are[?] beards and beards. Go and walk the whole town and you'll see whether you'll find such a 'vessel' as mine, because you must know that my beard comes from the neck and has a 'połączenie' [connection] with the eyebrows and ears, so that it is kosher and upright according to my friend Reb Leybl's paragraph all round — in length and in breadth. Yes, it seems to me that the fact that I am on the board of the 'Shomrei Shabbos Society' will not harm my dozorship either. What more do you want — the mikveh? Ah, there, you see, I'm at home. Not a day goes by that I am not in and out of the mikveh; it doesn't even cost me any money. And daughters — is that a trifle to you? As you see me, I am a real father of children and cannot say 'where are my children?'. Apart from my old stock, I mean the half-dozen older daughters, I have young stock too, so you can see plainly that I am the first and best candidate to be dozor.
And at making 'porządki' [order] in the gmina I'll really be good all over again[?]: I have already laid out a whole plan about it. First of all, burials will be free, cholent pots will be set out free, and women as well as men will be allowed to carry on the Sabbath. Besides that I have a whole series of important deeds, with which the local public will be very pleased.
In short, my time has come. I am sure that everyone will vote for me, and if women too should have the vote, I (printed 'hamb') certainly have no doubt whatever that my seat is assured[?]. What did you think — that it's a free-for-all? Must one[?] always let the sinners of Israel be the rulers over the community? Never mind, today we already know how to knock. At another time a Jew like me could have lived out his biblical years and known nothing of such things as dozorship; but today, when we have people in the Sejm and a paragraph is drafted — then who [else] will wish me well?
Who has a beard? — Shloyme Yone.
Who goes to the mikveh? — Shloyme Yone!
Who is in Shomrei Shabbos, who has daughters? — Shloyme Yone, of course! Therefore I say: may Aryeh Leybl live a hundred and twenty-one years, who kept watch at the authorities that Jews like me should have the greatest hopes of becoming kehilla men.
'Doloy' [Russian: down] with the beard-shavers!
'Niech żyje Szloma Jona!' [Polish: Long live Shloyme Yone!]
Vote, all as one, for Shloyme Yone, who wants to and must become dozor!
A. Feig.
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion (Bamidbar)

Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion
Collected and stylised by Y. Y.
Parashat Bamidbar
—o—
a) In the wilderness of Sinai... after they came out of the land of Egypt (1:1)
The Torah first speaks of the greatness of humility. "Bamidbar" [in the wilderness] — with the one who makes his own "I" ownerless like a wilderness; "Sinai" — with the one who keeps himself low like Sinai, the smallest of the mountains — with him God speaks.
But there is also a false humility, a so-called humility; humility merely as a pose. Therefore, right where humility is praised, it is added "after they came out of the land of Egypt", for the Gemara (Bava Kamma 61) expounds this verse to mean that God distinguishes exactly between [true] tekhelet and a man who wraps himself in imitation tekhelet: kla-ilan [indigo]. Yes — not humility only in people's eyes, but also before God, before one's conscience... Noam Megadim.
• • •
Humility does not mean being abased and lowly in one's own eyes, being a shlimazl. No — whoever has no holy audacity (azut di-kedusha) in him has no share in the Torah.
Nor has humility without wisdom any value. A fool's humility is nothing...
Likutei Etzot (Rabbi Nachman of Bratslav).
• • •
Rabbi Raphael of Bershad used always to praise God for not having given a commandment to think highly of oneself... "For — he would say — if, God forbid, He had, how could I, a good-for-nothing, fulfil the commandment of pride? I, who am nothing at all?"... Imrei Tzaddikim.
—o—
b) You shall number them by their hosts (1:3)
They counted, after all, by the half-shekels, and since the matter smelled of money there had to be two: "you and Aaron". Even Moses our Teacher wanted to have one more person beside him when he counted public money, so that no one should suspect him...
Tiferet Yehonatan.
—o—
c) Each one head of his fathers' house (1:4)
The well-known thinker and gaon Rabbi Moshe Chefetz once traded witticisms with a man of pedigree who boasted of his lineage at every opportunity. Rabbi Moshe told him:
— The difference between me and you is that with me a pedigree begins, and with you the pedigree of your family ends...
A person must strive to be "head of his fathers' house", the first to begin spinning a pedigree; but to enjoy a pedigree that others have woven is no great art...
Peninim Yekarim
—o—
d) The called of the congregation (1:16)
In fact it was the task of Moses our Teacher to appoint the heads of the tribes; he had, after all, been told: "And you shall seek out". But the Jews argued: if Moses appoints the princes, what do we need them for at all? They will in any case do whatever Moses wants... Therefore: "the called of the congregation" — the people elected them...
Tiferet Yehonatan.
—o—
e) Appoint the Levites (printed: 2:3)
A Masorah note:
"Appoint (hafked) the Levites"
"Set (hafked) a wicked man over him"
— "for no man is appointed leader of the community below unless he has been made wicked above": if one is appointed a parnas [community leader], it is proof that one has become wicked...
Baal HaTurim
Compiler's note: the saying cited is found in "Midrash Haser ve-Yater", Mainz, 5632 [1872].
—o—
f) The standard of the camp of Dan, to the north (2:25)
The north alludes to wealth ("gold comes out of the north"), because the North Pole is the darkest — the true symbol of wealth... The north wind, too, is stormy and unrestrained — the true symbol of unbridled wealth that wants only to swallow up and grab... That is why this was Dan's banner — Dan, "the rearguard of all the camps", the eternal gatherer of those who chase after money, money and more money... Of him it is also said "he leaps forth from Bashan" — the Bible-famous "cows of Bashan", meaning the magnates. —
Olelot Ephraim
—o—
Haftarah
g) And it shall be that in the place where it was said to them "You are not My people", it shall be said to them: "Children of the living God" (Hosea 2:1)
The prophet Hosea speaks of a period in which insolence and corruption reigned without limit among the people, and instead of calling them for it "You are not My people", they will yet be called, for their corruption, "children of the living God"; that is, they will yet be called righteous for their corruption... it will even be an honour...
Yeriot HaOhel.
—o—
h) You are not My people.
The Yalkut says that when God told Hosea that the Jews were sinning, Hosea said to Him: "Then exchange them for another people".
Is it possible that Hosea wanted to have the Jews exchanged?
— Hosea said to God: just try to exchange them for another people and You will see whether You make things better... Yes, then You would have seen that the worst among Jews is still better than the best gentile..
Or Yesharim (R' Moshe of Kobrin).
—o—
Avot
i) Eat bread with salt... and if you do so (6:4, printed 6:5)
A.
A very fine thing, this "eat bread with salt, drink water by measure and sleep on the ground" — but: "and if you do so" — that you yourself should act thus, not merely recommend it to the yeshiva students...
A popular saying.
B.
"And if you do so" — if you do it, if you run away from your comfort and eat bread with salt in order to be able to study Torah; if you do it — not when God does it... When one has nothing but bread and salt, it is no great feat not to eat delicacies... The real achievement is only when "happy are you in this world" and you leave everything in order to study Torah...
Maharam Schiff.
—o—
j) The Torah of Your mouth is better to me than thousands of gold and silver (6:10 as printed)
A Jewish woman comes to the Maggid of Kozienice with a request: since her child is dangerously ill, the Maggid should therefore pray for a complete recovery. The Maggid sees through the holy spirit that the child is lost, and, unable to get rid of the woman, tells her that if she brings him a thousand rendlekh [gold coins] the child will be helped. The pauper woman agrees at once; the Maggid is astonished.
A little while later the woman is back: she has even more than a thousand rendlekh — the Maggid gapes all the more. She takes out[?] of her kerchief a — — — Chumash!... "Is this not worth more than a thousand rendlekh, Rebbe?"
The Maggid had to keep his word... and he said: "Never has anyone defeated me except this woman."
Theatre Notes

„The Sacred Flame“, a play in 3 acts by Somerset Maugham, performed by the Vilna Troupe.
Maurice Tabret, a young airman, is paralysed in a crash and unable to live with his wife Stella.
For a few years his wife nurses him and is faithful to him, until her brother-in-law Colin Tabret arrives and a hot love develops between them, which goes as far as intimate relations...
The mother, Mrs. Tabret, tolerates these relations, because she, the experienced one, knows that when the „sacred flame“ flares up in two young bloods it is like a river that floods its banks, and every restraint is pointless. The happiness of the two young people, her children, is also dear to her. And so that her sick son may die with the illusion that his wife has remained faithful to him, she poisons him with a large dose of a narcotic.
The play, which has a somewhat sensational background, nevertheless touches on a deep human problem: the struggle between duty, logic and morality on one side and the power of sexual love on the other.
For five years Stella did everything possible to ease her husband's sufferings, and perhaps the situation would have lasted a long time yet, had not the young, healthy Colin come along, whom she even tries to push away, because she knows what it may lead to.
But what use are reason, morality and modesty, when the whole human being is then flooded by an erotic deluge, from which very rarely a „Noah“ is saved who manages to build an „ark“ and keep himself on the surface.
L. Potocka, Orleska, Goldenberg, Buzgan, Natan and Shigarin were all excellent; they stood at the height of their task. Their acting was a fine concert of words, which left a deep aesthetic impression.
A dissonance was brought in only by S. Kan, who as the lover („amant“) was very pale, without any expression, and disturbed the harmonious whole.
— — —
„The Black Ghetto“, a play in 7 scenes by Eugene[?] O'Neill.
A young American Negro falls in love with a white girl, who, however, will not hear of him. Only when she is seduced by a white Don Juan does she come to the Negro, who marries her.
The play expresses the tremendous racial antagonism that prevails between whites and blacks. It is a cry of protest, a spit in the face of the pseudo-American civilisation which tolerates such inhuman laws as do not allow Negroes to enter the society of whites.
Just as for Jews in the Middle Ages, there exists today a „black ghetto“ in the very heart of ultra-modern New York, and if someone wants to break out of there he is brutally pushed back in.
Orleska was splendid in her role; she surpassed herself. A tremendous impression was made by her monologues, which were performed with great artistry and deeply moved the audience.
Also good in their roles were: Buzgan, Weislitz, Katz and Shigarin.
The crowd scene was very successful and effective.
S. R.

The Imposing Lag ba-Omer Outing / A Performance for Children in Będzin / The „Gan Yeladim“ Reopens / Czeladź Already Has a „Rada Komisaryczna“ — the Jews Have Not a Single Representative / The „Upadłość“ of „Produkcja“ / Smallpox Vaccinations in Sosnowiec / Clash Between 2 Gabbaim

The Imposing Lag ba-Omer Outing
Lag ba-Omer, the festival of youth and spring with its traditional outings, went off very well in Będzin this year, so that our town has not seen for a long time such a successful national event as Sunday's outing to the woods of „Młynki“. This year, on the initiative of the Zagłębie district committees of „Maccabi“ and the K.K.L. [Jewish National Fund], all youth organisations and sports clubs arranged a general outing which Jewish Będzin will long remember.
Despite the uncertain weather and the distant place of the outing — 25 kilometres both ways — the „tiyul“ nevertheless drew up to 1.200 participants, apart from the hundreds of guests who did not join the procession.
At 7 in the morning the procession set off from the Hakoah ground. At the head of the procession, which is received with great enthusiasm by the assembled masses of people, march the orchestra and the board of „Hakoah“, all the „Maccabi“ clubs of Zagłębie with their blue-and-white flags, „Gordonia“, „Hashomer Hatzair“, „Hashomer Haleumi“, „Bruria“, „Herzliya“, „Betar“, „Hashachar“ and the Będzin gymnastics groups of „Hakoah“.
A particularly fine effect is made, thanks to the exemplary order, by the halutz youth in scout dress; „Gordonia“ and „Hashomer Hatzair“, which mobilised their members from the whole district for this year's Lag ba-Omer festivities.
On arriving in the forest the organisations rested, and each camp for itself put up field tents, made tea and enjoyed themselves heartily. Some of the entertainments that had been planned in the programme were disrupted by the rain, which appeared several times in the noon and evening hours. Despite the bad change in the weather the youth nevertheless carried on all the games and spent a whole day in a festive mood to Jewish music, hora dances and Eretz-Israel songs. „Gordonia“ also held several talks: „1,800 years since the Bar Kokhba uprising“ and „Yosef Chaim Brenner“ on the 10th yahrzeit of the tragically killed Hebrew poet.
At 8 in the evening the outing returned to town; the excursionists are awaited by thousands of curious people, who are inspired by the Zionist youth celebrating its festival. Then a very successful march-past takes place in the main streets, which makes an impression also on the non-Jewish public; all those assembled march under the national flag, and, singing various Hebrew songs, the very successful demonstration disperses on the Hakoah ground to the sounds of the Polish and Jewish anthems.
—o—
A Performance for Children in Będzin
Next Monday at 3 p.m. a performance for children will take place in Będzin. The rich programme will be performed by the pupils of the Jewish girls' gymnasium in Sosnowiec. As is known, the performance had an extraordinary moral success in Sosnowiec.
—o—
The „Gan Yeladim“ Reopens
As we have already written, the Hebrew Froebel school named „Gan Yeladim“ is being reopened in Będzin by the Zionist women's association „WIZO“.
The kindergarten, which will at last be housed in its own large, comfortable premises, will be staffed with first-class pedagogical personnel.
As we are informed, the news of the opening of the kindergarten has aroused great interest among parents who strive to give their children a Jewish national education.
—o—
Czeladź Already Has a „Rada Komisaryczna“ — the Jews Have Not a Single Representative
The Będzin starostwo has received a decree from the voivode that a „rada komisaryczna“ [appointed commissarial council] of 5 persons is to be nominated in Czeladź.
It is interesting that councillor Mr. Schweitzer, who went hand in hand with the „BB“ club [the pro-government Non-Partisan Bloc], was not nominated.
—o—
The „Upadłość“ of „Produkcja“
The mechanical bakery in Sosnowiec named „Produkcja“, founded two years ago, has, as the Polish press reports, gone bankrupt and is under „upadłość“ [bankruptcy proceedings].
—o—
Smallpox Vaccinations in Sosnowiec
The local magistrate announces that the free smallpox vaccination will be carried out from the 11th to the 30th of this month.
During this time the smallpox vaccinations will take place in the public elementary schools, and for adults at the outpatient clinic at Targowa 18, every day from 12.30 to 2.30.

Clash Between 2 Gabbaim
Last Sabbath the first clash over the kehilla elections took place in Old Sosnowiec, between the gabbaim of the synagogue and of the beit midrash.
The clash came about because the synagogue gabbai criticised the beit-midrash gabbai: why is he „catching souls“ for the elections with the help of a kiddush...
The Sad State of the Jewish Orphans' Homes. Danger that the Educational Homes Will Be Closed.

[Będzin — orphans, charity.]
The sad state of the orphans' homes, the so-called “ochronki” [shelters], has already reached the highest degree of collapse: because of the large debts the bakers, butchers and shopkeepers have stopped their credit. And if the Jewish public does not come to help, the “ochronki” are threatened with closure.
In connection with this, a tag sale organized by the Charity Society will take place next Tuesday.
It is to be hoped that the campaign will be properly supported, so as in this way[?] to rescue the important orphan institutions from collapse.
When the Secretary Got a “Shake”, the Little Wife Got a Divorce.

[Będzin — agunah affair, rabbinate.]
The story began as long as 3 years ago. A young man from Będzin married a girl from a small town, and after the “seven days of feasting” the young fellow vanished, and the little wife, who remained an agunah [a ‘chained’ deserted wife], went off to a job as a saleswoman in a shop in Dąbrowa.
Last Sabbath the wife happened to be in Będzin, and walking in the street she met her runaway “bird”, who, catching sight of her, tried to run away.
This time, however, he did not succeed, and he fell under the rule of the local Jewish porters, who took an interest in the fate of the wretched woman, and with the help of the porters the young man was taken to the rabbinate so that he should give a get [divorce].
The divorce, however, dragged on because of the price: the rabbinate demanded no less than 50 zł., and the young man did not want to give more than 25 zł. So that it nearly came to pass that the divorce would not take place.
Only when one of the porters started to “shake” the rabbinate's secretary and threatened further deeds was the divorce done for 25 zł.

[Będzin — monument, state ceremonies.]
This week the monument in honour of the fallen of the 11th[?] regiment was brought here; the monument is located in the barracks and will be finally unveiled on the 21st of June [czerwiec] of this year.

The budget commission, which is working out the draft of the new municipal budget, has decided that a kilowatt of electricity should cost only 40 gr. Whether the decision will be confirmed is a great doubt.

[Będzin — cantorate.]
The gabbaim of the “Ahavat Re'im” synagogue in Kraków invited the local cantor Mr. Żupowicz[?] several weeks ago to come to Kraków to lead the prayers for one Sabbath.

A Bear Tears Loose from Its Chain and Injures Several People.

[Czeladź — accident, circus.]
In Czeladź there is a travelling circus, which has its seat precisely at the liveliest spot, where the greatest traffic takes place.
Last Sunday, while the market was full of people, a bear tore itself out of its cage and went in among the crowd.
Naturally a great panic broke out. Finally, with the help of the police, they succeeded in calming the enraged beast.
Several people were injured.

The Majority of the Radomsko Hasidim Will Not Vote for the Agudah List

[Będzin — elections; Hasidim.] As is known, several Radomsko Hasidim who lean towards the "Agudah" [Agudat Israel] concluded a bloc with the "Agudah". Long-sought safe-breaker falls into police hands.

Information on reductions for the International Exhibition in Paris.
In response to the many enquiries from our readers regarding the reductions for the International Exhibition in Paris, we turned to the French consul in Katowice, from whom we received the following information.
Every individual who travels to the exhibition and buys a direct return railway ticket enjoys a reduction of 25 per cent.
Groups of 25 persons receive collective return tickets with a reduction of 33 per cent.
The tickets are valid for 30 days.
The reduced-rate visa, which costs only 2 zł., is given only to those who travel in order to take part in the exhibition.
The visa is valid for a whole month, there and back.
The above-mentioned reductions are granted on presentation of an identity card (legitymacja), which is issued at the French consulate in Katowice at the price of 9 zł.

How Did the Election Campaign for the Kehillot in Zagłębie Look?

By the time our readers read these lines, the election campaign for the kehilla elections will already be over; yet it is worth giving a short overview of how the election campaign looked and what means were used in the election struggle — or, more correctly, in the frenzied dance of demons.
Not to mention the countless meetings which every party and tendency held with the participation of its imported "great men" — the streets were simply "flooded" with election "literature", in which one "told off" the other down to the seventh rib... and most probably this will be a wide field for the courts in Zagłębie...
In Będzin the "Agudah" began its fight on the Sabbath. On that day the "guardians of the faith" got "open eyes" and only then noticed the printing shops where work is done on the Sabbath; intending to strike "capital" from this for the election fight against the opposing lists, the "sharp ones" of the Ger shtibl went out into the street to check the "measures" of Jewishness. Because of this inspection it came to a brawl between the two sides, and the peacemaker was the police.
Likewise, some of the allied Sochaczew Hasidim, wishing to show their loyalty to the "Agudah", visited several Hasidic shtiblekh, bringing along the well-known sold souls, the whippersnapper [pętaki] "editors", to hold "speeches". Everywhere these creatures got the verdict they deserved, and to the sound of caterwauling they withdrew from the minyanim and shtiblekh.
The next day, Sunday, the "Agudah" distributed "election newspapers", their content — disgusting insults and attacks on those who figured on the Zionist list.
The "election newspapers" and similar materials were, as always, distributed by the "young army", the pupils of the "Yesodei Torah cheder".
The Zionist list issued a large illustrated poster, in whose content the honour of the Ger court was also touched upon. To this, however, the authorities did not agree, and the posters were taken down; only when the non-kosher words had been struck out were the posters permitted to be distributed.
Of the other tendencies, the two artisans' groups especially "distinguished" themselves. In their innumerable "publications" one honoured the other with no mean portions, and each "proved" that "I am the one" — we are the true artisans...
The small traders worked quietly, among their own members, and did not even reply to the "Agudah"'s pamphlet addressed against them...
From Monday evening on, the town was "illuminated" by the light-advertisements for various lists.
In Sosnowiec the election fight was fiercer than anywhere else, because around the fight for the kehilla there was reflected at the same time the fight over the rabbinical seat, between the Englardists [supporters of Rabbi Englard] and the Mizrachists...
On Friday at twilight an election appeal of the Englardists was distributed, which likened the "Mizrachi" to the underworld; to this "Mizrachi" replied that the "underworld" in fact belongs to the Englardists. But taking into consideration the content of both "appeals", one's face turns red with shame, seeing how far "the means sanctify the end"..
For list number 6 ("Mizrachi"–Zionists) an election agitation was conducted in the European manner: hundreds of school youth demonstrated with balloons and little flags in their hands, calling on fathers and brothers to vote for list 6.
Grandiose meetings of all tendencies were held. The meetings passed off quietly; only the meeting of the "Agudah" had no luck — at that meeting "egg explosions" occurred once again. Rumour has it that the eggs were still left over from the budget session during Chol HaMoed...
The sum total is that if we Jews had used so much initiative and energy for the benefit of other important purposes, we would have gained a great deal from it...
In Dąbrowa it did not come to any serious clashes. In the synagogue a quarrel even broke out on the Sabbath, but it soon grew quiet.
The whole fight consisted only in distributing appeals in which "the cards were laid open" about the activity of the kehilla representatives up to now.
The "Bund", which officially did not take part in the elections, distributed an appeal to its comrades that they should prepare for the "burial" of the old, mouldy, fascist kehillot,
Derekh Eretz and Reverence

(After the election tumult. — The fragmentation and lawlessness on the election front. — What now?)
Well, now one can at last breathe freely: the election tumult is over, the fair is over, everything is over that deafens and intoxicates [printed "פערשפורט"] the naive voter, the honest and upright Jewish citizen, the member of the Jewish kehilla.
Now it already belongs to the past — the tripping-up of one party by another, of one chair-grabber by the next. The intriguers and the little flattery-figures can now rest after the hard, toilsome work in which they so distinguished themselves on the way to the kehilla elections. Various, various types and specimens, original and peculiar individuals, showed themselves on the surface of public life and announced to the Jewish people that we are fortunate, because they have taken upon themselves the power to become our spokesmen, our representatives.
And the political maturity of these candidates — well, may God not punish us for the words and for the sins we commit with the pen. With one interesting episode we had the opportunity to become acquainted. A Jew, a householder, a Hasid — and as for travelling, you understand, he travels to the Rebbe. But enormous sympathies he has for the "Mizrachi"; only that does not matter: if the "Agudah" will do him a "favour" and pay the widow of the deceased melamed the sum which he honestly earned in the cheder "Yesodei HaTorah", he certainly agrees to offer himself up as a sacrifice and to figure on the Agudah list, although he is far from its ideals, from its conduct, from its arguments and from the whole political machination. It goes without saying that at the very first step the Jew was already cheated, but that does not belong to the matter, that interests us little; for us only this is interesting and characteristic — in what manner and by what ways people approached the elections. The community, the representation, the spokesmanship, the responsibility toward the public were placed as the last item on the agenda; the votes of the electors were first of all sold for a mess of pottage, the private little "favour" was set higher than the interests of the community. Well, can the simple, honest voter know what is going on behind his back? How his vote is being sold? What deals are being made with his voice?
There is maturity for you, there is consciousness, there is understanding and orientation for the common good, there is how people understand what it means to be represented, what it means to represent this or that class, this or another tendency.
And if one thinks that by chance there happened to be one man who is poorly oriented in public problems, one is greatly mistaken; it was only by chance that one man told, in all his naivety, how they wanted to cheat him — but of such specimens we have a full 75 per cent and perhaps even more, and unfortunately we notice them among all strata, among national, democratic and even left-wing elements alike. It is rare that they are consistent and walk along a well-trodden line.
We understand that the kehilla representation must be made up of the most varied tendencies and that a fruitful activity must be conducted for the benefit of all strata of the population, but every tendency must after all have its programme, its marked-out line, its "ani ma'amin" [credo]; just as one cannot be more papal than the Pope, so one must not dance "kadosh" before everyone.
On the election front people went with the slogan: because you want to bury me, I will bury you; because you want to see my downfall, I will fight not to let you up onto the kehilla chair. Usually it is said that these aspirations last only until the elections, and afterwards, when it is all over, there, in the kehilla room, one sets about productive work and knows that one bears important tasks for the common good and that Jewish public life is waiting for them to be solved. Usually that is what is said, usually that is how it is understood, and usually that is how it ought to be — but why fool ourselves, why play "blinde vize" [apparently: a blindfold game, make-believe], when one knows that it is not so, when one knows that as it was before the elections so it will be afterwards too. We would not wish to be false prophets and say that the activity in the kehilla will be a continuation of the election battle. Would that it not be so, would that we do not return to the bitter experience within the walls of the kehillas.
True, before the elections every tendency preached very nicely its programme, its demands, for which it would fight; but afterwards one sees one of two things: either they will go on tearing at each other for all the world, one will spite the other; or — and this will be in the best case — they will sit it out entirely, so that the whole activity of the kehilla will be paralysed. As soon as they are assured of the chairs they will be able to sleep peacefully at home; they will even forget that one is a parnas and must come to a meeting once in a while. And here the question arises: can one really go on along these paths? May one be so apathetic toward our communal problems? May we tolerate every lawlessness? Can we then afford such luxuries? After all, the Jewish kehilla system costs the Jewish population so much money that we have the right to demand that it be what it ought to be, that which one could and should have made of it.
Do our representatives not sin against themselves and against the Jewish people when they enter the Jewish kehilla and do nothing for the Jewish people? Is it then permitted to them to put us in such an unpleasant situation? In such an ugly position? Are we not humiliated in the eyes of others when they see what a face our institutions have, in which all strata of the population are represented?
When we draw a parallel — how the election campaign looks, what "salvations and consolations" the candidates promise us if only we send them into the gmina [kehilla], what they will make of it, to what a high level they will bring it; when we listen to each party's programme we have the sure consciousness that these people will represent us properly. But comes a day after the elections and we are beside ourselves; only then do we see that these people have no notion of what kehilla affairs, kehilla problems, kehilla interests are, and then we are disappointed. It gives the impression that they did know something, did understand something; only, hardly have they been assured of the chair when they have time enough to occupy themselves with the questions: when they have time, when they are in the mood and well disposed, then they will be able to amuse themselves. A parnas, a dozór [kehilla board member], they hold, can occupy himself with the question when his heart is at ease; one need not exert oneself; an amusement — by all means, but not, heaven forbid, to be tied to it as if one had been hired for it. Such a Jew makes light of kehilla affairs altogether; he says to himself: well, it does not give me a livelihood yet, so I have time to think it over, and when I have the possibility I will come. Such talk you could hear from the former parnasim. Now it is the same again: if they do not behave with more attentiveness, with more regard and respect for Jewish prestige, it will most likely be brought to the same state — which really must not be allowed.
We must not allow the kehilla representatives to make light of our kehilla system, because with the making light[?] of our kehillas our kehilla interests are automatically degraded, and that we must not allow; to that we must react properly, because merely to make a toy, an amusement-corner, of Jewish self-government is certainly permitted to no one. Therefore it would be important in the first place to give a lesson to all those who have now entered the Jewish kehilla as representatives: let them be told that they should behave with full seriousness and respect toward all our problems and painful questions, because as representatives of the Jewish kehillas — they must not forget — they guard the honour of Israel, the honour of the nation, which must be reckoned with on every occasion.
Fragmented, torn, lawlessly and without any respect whatsoever, people went to elect a Jewish representation; let us see to it that the fault is repaired by giving ourselves an account of how much shame and humiliation this has brought us in the eyes of others, so that the stain be wiped away by demanding of our representations that first of all they enter the kehillas with derekh eretz [respect] and reverence, and that along that path they go step by step.
Selekt.

The Future... (A Fantastic Picture)

[Story — a fantastic vision.] By B[?]. A. Wajnman.

A terrible, dark night enveloped mountain and valley. Masses of darkness raged like a hurricane in the invisible infinity, accompanied by tremendous thunderclaps and blinding flashes of lightning, which cut into space at intervals. The Almighty — in the circle of His retinue — sits on the Throne of Glory, deep in thought. His heart is heavy and sorrowful, as it were. Once again those times have drawn near — those times of the Flood and of the Dispersion [the generation of the Tower of Babel]...

A glance! And the angel — who is in charge of the earth with all the "vidmung"[?] [unclear word; apparently: everything] that is upon it — appeared and took his place before the Throne of Glory, folding his mighty wings...

— What is the news on earth? the Creator asked quietly,
— Bad!! the angel answered curtly.
— Is my cup of suffering full yet? the Almighty asked the seraph hovering in the heavenly space.
— It will not be long before the cup is full to the brim, the angel answered, casting a glance as he spoke at the cup standing nearby, in which a kind of liquid had been gradually filling up more and more...
— Go down to the earth and look at it one last time! came the command.
The angel who is in charge of the earth vanished and quickly returned, silent, and in dread took his place before the Creator.
— What is the news? the Creator asked sadly. Tell!!
I have circled the whole planet — the angel began — I looked for a human being and did not find one; I met many 2-legged ones, but they are beasts, not human beings possessing the image of God... The whole earth is one great prison-labyrinth and the people are one great family of poison-mixers...

— And the woman, whom I gave to man as a helper? What is she called?
— Eve! — the angel broke in — she used to be called, but today her names are various, and she is dissolute...
— It was not such a woman that I created — said the Creator in despair, and quietly, with his last hope, asked:
— And the children?

— The children? the angel answered — just like the parents! Ever since they divided the globe among themselves, there stretches one long chain[?] of hatred and distrust from land to land, from people to people; rivers of blood pour without cease; man is turned into a beast; the greatest cruelties are committed in the name of God, in the name of justice; and the deeper the rivers of blood and tears become, the more there drown in them the noble divine feelings, the sublime divine truth...
And in the end new misfortunes have been added.
— Which?
— A flood of parties, which have descended[?] upon the children of men... Every party has leaders who promise to bring salvation to mankind, and hypocrites they are, these "providers", who trample your divine word underfoot...
— Thousands of human years — the angel went on — have passed since you, great Creator, said: Thou shalt not kill!! And the so-called pursuers of peace have now begun to drill in and expound the "Thou shalt not kill"; they hold meetings, they promise to realise the prophet's "and they shall beat their swords into ploughshares", but on the quiet they are preparing an even crueller slaughter, they are preparing means of annihilation in order to turn everything into a state of chaos and void...
— Has anything remained untouched by the filthy hands of him whom I once called man? the Creator asked.

— Almost nothing!! the angel answered resolutely; all pure sanctities have been struck to the ground. The tents of Shem are locked... The mountains of Zion are soaked with the blood of martyrs... and... and...
— Enough!!! the Almighty cut him short in pain. And, full[?] of sorrow, he turned to the angel hovering in space: Is my cup of suffering full now?
— Full now! the seraph snapped in despair...

And the Creator, as it were, rested his head on his hands; he let fall a tear, which dropped into the cup of suffering... at which[?] the whole heavenly retinue shuddered terribly...

And the sky grew still darker, with a darkness that could be felt, and a deluge poured down on God's earth...
— — — — —
The angels of destruction whispered meanwhile: That is what you are worth...
