A Letter from Milówka

The health resort of Milówka, which lies more than 500 metres above sea level in the mountains of the Western Beskids, has already earned itself a name among the thousands of guests who in recent years have found a place of rest here.
This is, incidentally, no wonder, since Milówka, which lies in the Żywiec region in the splendid valley of the „Soła“ (452 m above sea level), is surrounded on all sides by a chain of mountains called the „Western Beskids“. The mountains — „Prusów“ (1009 m), „Sucha Góra“ (1162 m), „Barania Góra“ (1214 m), etc. — attract almost daily thousands of tourists from every corner of Poland.
Among the regular summer guests one notices for the most part a majority of the working intelligentsia, who — after a hard year of work — find here, in the lap of God-blessed nature and the fir forests, the rest they badly need. Thus student colonies come here from Kraków, Warsaw, etc., which stay here until after the holidays. There are also many summer visitors [?] from Zagłębie, mostly from Będzin and Sosnowiec.
The few dozen Jewish families who live here permanently have their own synagogue and maintain a rabbi and a shochet. Lodgings at a price of 40—70 zł a month can be had in the little town or in the surrounding peasant cottages.
There are also several Jewish boarding houses, among which the well-known Goldberg boarding house stands out, with clean, bright, sunny, comfortable rooms.
A branch of the Bielitz „Maccabi“.
Last week a branch of the Bielitz „Maccabi“ was founded here, with its own sports ground; it numbers some thirty-odd members. The dentist Kinstler was elected chairman and Mr. Tobias secretary. The association has an advantage: holding a „Maccabi“ certificate one can enjoy a 25 percent railway discount and cross the Czech border without any difficulty.
S. S.

The Czeladź Jewish Carter and His „Kochanka“

Czeladź is boiling like a kettle. Young and old are talking about the „romance“ of the Jewish carter Mr. S., who abandoned his wife and children and went off to his Christian „kochanka“ [mistress]. When his wife went there, to the „romantic little house“, Mr. S. attacked her and beat her murderously.
The local moreh-tzedek Lewental took an interest in the matter; last Sabbath he came to the craftsmen's minyan and admonished the faithful husband and father for his „fine“ deeds.
— Will the rabbi's intervention achieve anything? — That the near future will show...
The „Red Rooster“ in Gołonóg

From an unknown cause a fire broke out in a small house in Gołonóg. The fire spread with lightning speed and engulfed the neighbouring peasant buildings. Thanks to energetic rescue efforts the fire was checked. 6 houses, 10 barns and 6 stables were burnt down.
From Sport

„Garbarnia“, Kraków — „Hakoach“ 1:2.
The Będzin „Hakoach“ is making efforts to bring in [?] the best teams, so as to give its players good training for the coming championship matches. This time we again [?] saw [?] a Kraków team. True, the guests did not come in their representative line-up; three players came from the first team.
„Garbarnia“ proved to be a technically well-schooled side [drużyna], but it lacks [?], namely [?], finishing [?]. „Hakoach“ again failed to use its chances to beat the guests. The attack played without a plan and therefore lost. Even a penalty was not converted (Gutman). Already in the first minutes the guests succeeded in scoring the first goal through Biskup. „Garbarnia“ keeps playing the whole time, yet fails to score further goals [?]. After the change of ends the Będzin side takes the initiative; a series of promising situations are squandered by the „Hakoach“ forwards. Only in the 16th minute does Jankielewicz succeed in scoring the equaliser. A few minutes later Gutman shoots a penalty out [?]. In the 34th minute the referee awards a free kick and Ska [?] Reszowski [?] shoots in unstoppably. Neuberg, the Rosen brothers and Jankielewicz played well. Among the guests the backs, the centre-half and the inside forwards stood out. Referee Mr. Mazur [?] very good.
—o—
Zagłębie representative team vs. Königshütte 1:5 (1:3).
The representatives of Zagłębie gained a deserved victory over the city side of Königshütte. The guests proved to be very poorly schooled technicians, whereas Przybyłek, Tabiczhart [?] and Banaszyk [?] of the home team played excellently. The backs Kapała and Czepla [?] and the „Hakoach“ goalkeeper Neuberg also held up very well. The guests had their best players in Michalski [?] and the very nimble wings. Already the first minutes bring a goal for Zagłębie, scored by Tabiczhart [?]. The home side's attacks bring disorientation into the opponents' ranks. The consequence is the second goal for Zagłębie, scored by Przybyłek. The guests recover a little; Neuberg, who catches the balls with great assurance, has several fine moments. The initiative passes again to the Zagłębie players, who score the third goal through Banaszyk [?]. A minute before the interval the inside-right of the Königshütte team shoots in unstoppably from three metres. Half-time 1:3 in favour of Zagłębie. After the change of ends the home side neglects the wings; Königshütte exploits this, but without success. Soon they again have their say and Banaszyk [?] shoots the fourth goal. The Silesians try hard to hold the result, but Przybyłek succeeds in shooting the fifth and last goal for Zagłębie. In view of the constant superiority of the home side, the referee Mr. Mazur [?] breaks off [?] the interesting match. Spectators: over 2 thousand.

A Letter to the Editor.
Dear Mr. Editor!
I ask you to give me space in your esteemed newspaper for the following statement, for which I thank you in advance.
Because the decision of the Zionist committee in Dąbrowa regarding the election of board members in the Dąbrowa kehilla is not in accordance with the slogan „strictly along the Zionist line“, with which we went to the kehilla elections and according to which we must also act in future, I declare that I can no longer carry out the office of parnas. I therefore lay down my mandates both as parnas and as a member of the Zionist committee in Dąbrowa.
As regards the reasons which moved the above-mentioned committee to such a „decision“, this is not the place to uncover what went on behind the scenes. In spite of everything, I promise to carry out the decision.
Respectfully,
Jechiel Damb.
The Most Topical Economic Questions

(Expenditures in the economy at critical moments. — What is new with the tenants' question [„lokatorn“, from Polish lokatorzy — tenants]?)
That the economic situation in the country is bad, that the situation is quite a tense one — this we all know, all citizens can confirm it, because all of us carry the burden on our shoulders. But that is not what this is about; granted that things are bad — that is indeed bitter, and one must seek advice on how, and by what means, the unwanted, the dangerous, the unbearable can be improved; for as long as nothing at all is done about it, there are the surest chances that it will get even worse. And why should we fool ourselves — we see plainly that nothing is being done, and these are indeed the consequences: it keeps getting worse and worse.
But apparently even doing nothing in the face of the dangerous situation is not enough either, and with a light conscience people help to aggravate the situation.
Thus we see that in discussing the new budget for the town of Będzin, efforts are made even to devise fresh taxes; thus the investment tax, from which we had already been freed, has risen again like the resurrection of the dead, and precisely now it has been found necessary to burden the town's inhabitants with it.
It is characteristic how the tax question is trivialised: people reckon that if the fee for bringing goods in by rail is increased, that means it costs nobody anything. Is it then not obvious that the merchant must add this expense to all his expenses? And once that is so, the products must surely become dearer — and who pays then, individuals or the community? Does not the whole population bear the burden? Does one not in this way make life harder for the broadest strata of the population? What is this game of looking with closed eyes for? Is it a healthy phenomenon? Does it not mean, in this way, fooling oneself? Misleading oneself? Making things harder for oneself?
Or take, for example, the tenants' question, that so painful matter which, unfortunately, has to this day still not been solved among us and, regrettably, is still stuck at a dead point — and „in the high windows“ it is discovered that precisely now is the time for the question to be solved, that precisely now is the time to raise the rent. Now, when people refrain from renting flats in new houses because they are not able to pay the high rent (tsinzh), and when a large percentage of the population cannot even pay the rent in the old houses, which by the way is not high — precisely at such a time they want to set about solving the question, and consequently raise the price of flats and shop premises.
It goes without saying that for a country it is no trifle to leave the painful question unsolved; one cannot, after all, always find oneself in such a difficult situation that the question is not solved. True, in the end the most varied means must be applied so that fresh flats are built and new houses put up; but one must not forget that such a thing is very sensitive and demands enormous forces — not from individuals but from the community. And therefore what can be achieved by raising the rent of the average and poor citizen precisely in such hard times, when he has no possibility of existing under the conditions prevailing until now? Or, for example, what can be achieved by raising the tax on unbuilt plots? Will the owner of the plot thereby be forced to build a house? One must, after all, be consistent, level-headed. Is it not enough that the owner of the plot is not given the possibility to build — must he in addition be punished for it with an increased tax? Upon my life [„k'lebn“], such tactics, such a way of acting, are incomprehensible. On the contrary, let the owners of the plots be given the possibility to build, and we shall see what a building movement will start in the country. On the other hand it is incomprehensible to go about with the opinion that, because the landlord will want to spare himself paying the tax on the unbuilt plot, he will see to achieving what he cannot attain — these are simply absurdities, fantasies.
But be that as it may, one thing can be established: the rent for dwellings will certainly be raised. Were we not in such hard living conditions, it would already have been an accomplished fact; only thanks to the prevailing conditions does the matter still drag on. But in the end we must get used to the thought that everyone will pay more rent, and therefore very much to the point is the national conference of the tenants' associations, which takes place next Sunday in Warsaw.
Before the government raises the rent it is important that it should hear what the people say, what the citizens who are members of the tenants' associations say. The tenants' association must, after all, be the only institution that will not let the citizen be harmed[?] [„bevelhn“] so long as he cannot obtain a dwelling on normal terms; and therefore on Sunday the mighty voice of all the tenants' associations must be heard, as many delegates as possible must be represented in Warsaw, and their voice [printed „sht-m“] must resound as mightily as possible in the decisive circles.
The government wants to solve the tenants' question, a question that is so urgently necessary and truly a first-class need — and who if not a government should be able to solve such a matter? But one thing must not be forgotten: that this can by no means be done on the weak shoulders of the citizens, at a time when they find themselves in a period of crisis and have a hard struggle for their everyday living conditions.
It is high time for the government to begin creating realities in the field of building dwellings for the citizens; but at the same time one must not forget that the citizens must not be harmed[?] [„bevelht“] here.
The tenants' associations must guard the interests of the tenants; care must be taken that the broad strata of the population do not suffer here, because in that case it would be catastrophic for the citizens of the country. For let us suppose: as soon as dwellings are raised and shop premises become dearer, it is obvious that on the one hand the tenant will not be able to keep up with it, and on the other hand it will have to make all kinds of goods dearer. Must one not render an account of all this? Must one not foresee in good time all that may come of it?
Yes, for people who are not responsible for their deeds — for what will later arise from them — for them it makes no difference, they certainly do not analyse it. But have irresponsibilities led only a little to the prevailing catastrophes? Have the country and its citizens suffered only a little because of the deeds of irresponsible people? Because of the lawlessness of all sorts of „individuums“? That should, after all, have taught a lesson to the economic leadership not to allow any more lawlessness, which has become free and unbridled[?] [„frak un fray“] in all areas of economic life.
It is, after all, no secret to anyone any more that irresponsibility and lawlessness have made a heap of ruins of the whole economic system in Poland, and therefore a sacred duty lies first of all upon the tenants' associations: that in the question of dwellings they should not let the matter come to a state of irresponsible deeds.
R. Lft.[?]
The New Contribution

[Zagłębie — municipality and taxes; article.]
What were the new registration books [„meldungs-bikher“, residents' registration books, księgi meldunkowe] needed for?
A book with a whole bundle of assorted papers and little papers, in which one cannot find one's way, as in the tangle of a labyrinth.
What were they needed for?
Here people talked about abolishing the passport system, about increasing the citizen's freedom of movement; the new registration system apparently goes in the opposite direction: it binds the citizen hand and foot, so that he should feel in his own flat as in a hotel, where one must keep an eye on every „guest“, with all his general and special distinguishing marks.
But the worst and the most absurd thing about it is that the new decree squeezes fresh millions out of the population.
True, the money stays at home: paper factories, printers, bookbinders, new municipal (magistrate) officials get work; but the work is unproductive, and the money after all comes mostly out of poor pockets.
The decree originates, true, from Warsaw, but as is reported, other towns managed to beg their way out and postpone it for a year; our magistrates, however, are obedient children: Warsaw has only to give a peep, and at once they say „we will do and we will obey“ [na'aseh ve-nishma]; they do not even try to beg off.
They were told to make new registration books — so they grabbed and made them, and extracted from the impoverished population new, bloody thousands of „gulden“ [złoty]!
And what is quite comical is that for the time being nobody knows how to fill in all the dozens of headings. The books lie in the houses and people look at them the way hens look at human beings.
No, it is no wisdom at all to frighten the population and to lay heavy contributions upon it: greater wisdom would have been to obtain [„oystsufiln“ as printed], where necessary, the cancellation or the postponement of the decree.
That our magistrates did not do.
Feige Ratze in Krynica

[Humorous feuilleton — Sosnowiec and Krynica.] By Y. Oberzhanek [J. Oberżanek?].
What do you say about my Feigele [little bird; pet form of the name Feige]? A Feigele, a real Feigele! Others say she is no little bird at all but a whole bird — a „ptaszek“, they call it.
So my Feigele is a healthy one. If not for the „napady“ [fits, attacks] — and „fits“ she gets twice a year: the first „fit“ she gets in May, when the summer sun shows itself, and the second „fit“ she gets around Hanukkah.
What my Feigele suffers from — may I know as little of evil [i.e. I have no idea]; I only know that she is „pod nadzorem“ [under the supervision] of a doctor:
My Feigele picked herself a doctor — a young fellow with a black „grzywa“ [mane], with a pair of big eyes, with pressed trousers, always with a smoothly shaven „trombe“ [mug]. Well, is it any wonder that when my Feigele catches sight of him she gets a „podwyższona temperatura“ [raised temperature]?...
I shout at her: Feigele, what good is such a doctor to you, because of whom you get a high temperature? Are there too few old doctors here in Sosnowiec?
Says she: no, the young doctor already knows her organism; she has no „zaufanie“ [trust] in any other doctor. No other doctor will „dogodzić“ [satisfy] her the way the young doctor does.
Well — never mind, I think to myself: if she has no „trust“ in any other doctor, if only the chum with the black mane can „satisfy“ her — it can't be helped anyway.
So the young doctor really is a regular member of the household with me. And since lately my Feigele gets „fits“ very often, he keeps „zbadać“-ing [examining] her all the time, taps and listens, holds a piece of chalk and draws. Her shoulders look like a map: little stripes and little dots, little circles and little sticks.
I ask the fellow: panie doktorze [doctor, sir], tell me, why do you listen so much?
I am listening, says he, whether the lungs live in peace with the heart...
And if they don't live in peace? I ask him — are you such a great peace-pursuer [„rodef-sholem-nik“], or what?
But that is not what I meant to tell you. I only want to draw the attention of other men who have wives who get „fits“ and have „trust“ in young doctors, so that they should not come to such an end as I have.
Hear a story:
A few weeks ago I notice that my Feigele is not herself. What does it mean: not herself? By day she is the same as always: paints herself and smears herself, smokes „papirosy“ [cigarettes] and „mutlt“ [?; probably: chatters] with the neighbour women. By day she is the same as always, but at night — at night she is not the same: she cannot fall asleep, tosses and moans [„stękać“], turns on the right side and on the left side. I want to sleep, my eyes are sticking together, and she wakes me:
Borukh Hersh, are you asleep?
The next day I come home — my Feigele lies in bed with a wet towel bound round her head, and the fellow with the black mane is doing a „zbadać“ [examination] on her, taps and listens. Listens and taps, looks into her eyes and counts her teeth, questions her about what sort of thoughts she had during the sleepless night, wicked thoughts or good thoughts.
— Your wife, he explains to me, suffers from a „rozstrój nerwowy“ [nervous disorder].
Where, I ask the „professor“ with the black mane, does my Feigele get this „strój“ from?
It comes, says he, from over-exertion.
So what, in your opinion, panie doktorze, must one do to drive away my wife's „strój“?
For this ailment, says he, there is one remedy: she must „używać“ [go in for] sport, walk in the mountains. She needs Krynica, he explains to me.
When I heard „Krynica“ I went cold. I understood that this smelled of „coarser things“: that out of my wife's „strój“ there would spring „stroje“ [outfits — a pun on strój] — Krynica outfits.
What I wished the doctor, that I will spare you. The main thing is that a week later my Feigele was in Krynica.
That too would not have been a great misfortune. Let her calm [„uspokoić“] her nerves. All the wives go to Krynica — why indeed should my bird not be in Krynica too? Why should she be worse than the „gegrivete“ [?] shoemakers' wives? Why Yente Brane the bagel-baker yes, and Feige Ratze no?
All that would not have been a misfortune either, if not for the business with the doctor. Hear a story:
Left alone at home with the four walls and with one „pokojówka“ [chambermaid], I felt that I too was beginning to get a „strój“. I didn't think long, left the four walls with the „pokojówka“ — and off to Krynica.
There I found my Feigele in such a „state“: no Jewess at all — a full-blown „sportowiec“ [sportswoman]: in white trousers, with a „mitz“ [cap] over her eyes, with a pair of tall sticks at her side. And someone is holding her tight under the arm, as if he were afraid that, God forbid, she might run away from him. And who do you think was the 2nd sportsman who held her so tight under the arm? — The doctor!... The fellow with the black mane, with the grey [„groye“ as printed; perhaps for „groyse“, big] eyes...
Only now did I understand why my Feigele got „fits“ so often, why the doctor tapped and listened so much at my wife's shoulders; the reason for my wife's new „strój“-sickness, and why the doctor told her to „używać“ sport and why to Krynica of all places...
And what else did I find out? I found out that the doctor who kept „examining“ my Feigele is, all in all, — a doctor — of philosophy... that he has as much to do with medicine as an Agudah man [Agudat Israel] with piety...
I have told you the story so that you should know to beware of a wife who has „fits“ and has „trust“ in a young doctor.
Luxury

[Essay — Society and economy: against luxury.] It is a fact that at every step in our sinful world one comes across phenomena which everyone knows are foolish, everyone knows are bad, and everyone sees the fatal consequences that come of them; nevertheless they take root [?] and people go on committing the same follies again and again.
One of the phenomena of this kind is L U X U R Y. Who among us, from the rich banker down almost to the poor porter, has not complained in his life about luxury? That is — the wish to outdo those around one with expensive clothes, expensive furs, diamonds, grandiose weddings, glittering balls, needless trips to expensive spas...
Who does not know the troubles, the countless bankruptcies, the numberless family tragedies, and finally the terrible want caused by chasing luxury beyond one's means? It has already gone so far that recently Hasidic rebbes and rabbis have declared war on extravagance in the circles of the Jewish middle class; especially in the present bitter times everyone groans about it and — people go on doing the same.
And how many pens have already been broken over this question, how much ink has already been spilled among all nations, and among Jews too, from the prophet Isaiah down to the most recent times — and it has led to nothing. On the contrary, luxury, especially among Jews, keeps growing bigger and bigger.
The first bearers of luxury have always been the rich, the magnates; pride, which is rooted in all people, drives them to place themselves above everyone around them. And to achieve that they build themselves great palaces, dress in velvet and silk, in expensive furs, adorn themselves with diamonds and brilliants, spend a lot of money on expensive furniture, on splendid balls, on automobiles. The same pride also drives the people of the middle class to imitate this, although it is entirely beyond their means; and after the middle class the poor dance along, and so it turns out that the daughter of a poor broker, who runs about all day like a poisoned mouse until God helps him and he puts a wall together with a wall [i.e. clinches a deal] and barely earns a few groszy for a living, — she too wants to keep pace with the daughter of the rich manufacturer... From this come all the troubles, the bankruptcies and the whole poverty.
In the present bitter crisis, when all bridges are collapsing, the ordinary, "all-year" [?] Jew, the Jew of the middle class, must take himself firmly in hand and overcome within himself the empty pride of dancing after the rich. The magnates always have money, and not only may they spend it on luxury — on the contrary, it is desirable that they pursue luxury as much as possible, for, just as everything in the world has its good side and its bad side, so it is with luxury. Luxury moves all the wheels of the economy and of everything that goes on in the world.
So when one speaks of the harmfulness of luxury, one must remember that what is bad is that the poorer people and the middle class, who are extremely [?] pressed for money, who flay the skin off themselves, who quite often save the bite from their mouths, borrow other people's money — that they too enter into races with the rich. In the chase after the same garments and furs as the rich, they too hold rich balls, rich weddings, like those...
It is this that must be fought! One must endeavour to make the poor and those of the middle class understand that rich clothes, brilliants and even rich weddings are an extravagance, a harmful thing; one must never look at the fact that the other fellow goes about in gold, diamonds, brilliants and costly clothes: either he is richer than I — he may allow himself that; or he is a foolish spendthrift, a reckless braggart — and in both cases I need not imitate him...
I know that there are many people who understand this and would like to behave so; the empty pride rooted in people, to show off as rich before those around them, and the foolish, a thousand times foolish shame which almost everyone feels when those around do not count them as rich — this does not let them do what reason dictates.
They lack the courage to come out against public opinion. They are poor in courage to stand up to the pride that is rooted in people, and this leads to people being afraid of people. People do whatever is possible so that people should say... or should not say...
And yet there is only one remedy for it: to found an association that would come out with the slogan "Abolish luxury!"
The word "association" may perhaps strengthen the weak characters with regard to public opinion. They will no longer be afraid that people might say of them that they are not rich... and they will be able to do what their reason dictates to them.
Now, when the crisis is so great, is the most suitable time to create such an association. People with initiative must take it up.
Yaakov Kohen.
Dozór Yes — Dozór No

[Satirical feuilleton — kehilla board elections.] Monologue of a chairman who was a member of the community board ("dozór") for one day and night. Retold by Ben Amotz.
The Aguda! Who doesn't know the "Aguda" [Agudath Israel]? A party which "hates" with utter hatred all those who do not pray in the Gerer shtibl...
We have already more than once had plenty to sing and tell about the "Aguda". We had rabbinical elections — the Aguda; the gmina [municipal council] — the Aguda; and today I cannot show myself in the street because of the dozór seat which the Aguda promised me...
Who could have imagined that from this mandate I would have so much heart-pounding? As you see me, I never thought much of the whole business at all; what do I need a town full of enemies for? What for get into people's mouths? What kind of honour is it to be a dozór in these times?...
But when a misfortune is fated, it comes right into the house; the "fine Jews" came to me and talked me into it, that I deserve to be a leader in Israel — why not? Just a plain gabbai? Well, I thought to myself, what can be bad about it? Maybe even a bit of honour too, and what Jew doesn't want a bit of honour? Really, is it so bad to sit a few years in the gmina? Let everyone address me as "Panie Dozór"...
Well, is it a crime that I wanted to become a dozór? Incidentally, I only wanted to spite [?] my enemies...
But to be a dozór for one day and night — that I would not wish on my worst enemies. And here is how I was a dozór for one day and night.
On the night of 20 to 21 May I, like all the other candidates, had a "night of vigil"; I didn't sleep the whole night, only received the reports from the gmina. I was even feverish with fright, I had a "premonition" that I would get no joy from "Szmedrysz" [?].
In the morning, when I saw that "Szmedrysz" had "betrayed" me [Polish zdradził], that I hadn't got through, I said: Well, so what, "lo fildalti" [?, mock-Hebrew], and wiped my mouth as if nothing had ever happened.
Already over 2 weeks had passed, I had almost forgotten the whole business, when suddenly the door of my flat opens and in hastily comes a whole gang of Jews, old and young, all with cheerful faces, and they thrust their "little paws" ["fiftlekh", ?] at me.
— Mazel tov! Mazel tov! [?"rzent"] a dozór...
— Huh?... A dream!
From the election-makers I learn that I am a dozór. In the count — they say — there had been a "mistake"; we brought over our Reb Leibele of Łódź, who only then showed in black and white that — I am a dozór!
And I really was a dozór. Here I get an invitation to a meeting, to which I went and made myself heard too, banged on the table so there should be hush and quiet, so that something could be done — a dozór's doing, what else?...
But hardly had I looked around, who I am and what I am — bang! Again an "official communiqué" that —
— I'm already no longer a dozór!...
Finished being dozór, finished the mazel tov, finished the revenge on the enemies, finished the honour. Yes, a town of begrudgers, may they — God forbid — become...

[Będzin — accident.] On Sielecka Street in Będzin a deep canal has been dug for several days. A child aged 3, who was playing with sand, got in there. At that moment a lump of earth broke loose and covered the child. The child was taken out already dead.
Oneg Shabbat

[Weekly Torah portion — Oneg Shabbat.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes around this week’s portion
Collected and styled by Y. Y.
Parashat Korach
The Portion.
a) “And Korah took” (16:1).
A.
“This portion is well expounded” — Rashi.
The Gemara says: “The sons of Korah did not die” — this means the fruits, Korah’s traits, did not disappear. In those days there were various customs, habits and lusts which are incomprehensible to us and of which no trace has long remained, such as the lust to worship idols, which was once a simple, passionate lust. But one old custom did remain from those years — an incomprehensible yet passionate lust: strife. Korah’s spirit lives!
— This is what Rashi remarks: “This portion is well expounded” (yes, in the present tense) — the portion of strife is always, at all times, well expounded. An eternal problem...
Birkhot Tov.
B
“And Korah took — he took a bad bargain for himself” — Midrash.
Korah was a shrewd Jew, a great sage and a great rich man, a personality; but he made himself such an ugly name that today any scoundrel [lada łajdak] who stirs up strife against a great man is called “Korah”... This bad bargain Korah made: that all of today’s quarrel-mongers are compared to him, of whom he is surely ashamed...
Tiferet Yehonatan.
b) Dathan and Abiram (16:1).
The two perpetual intriguers. Everywhere they sow strife and hatred. One is “D-T-N”: he does everything in the name of religion (dat); in the name of Torah-loyalty he utters forbidden things against all true leaders of the people. The other is “A-B-I-R-A-M”: he is of noble lineage (avi ram — “my father is exalted”); he comes from great ancestry, and this entitles him to lead his “holy flock” by the nose and wage war against the true Moses...
Yalkut Margaliyot.
c) “And they rose up before Moses” (16:2).
First the verse speaks of Korah and of Dathan and Abiram, and when it then tells about the 250 Jews who took part in the strife, it interrupts in the middle with the verse “And they rose up before Moses”, because —
in a quarrel only either a great rich man who asks no one, or a great pauper who has nothing to lose, gets involved... The middling person always stands aside. Korah the great rich man and Dathan and Abiram (as the Midrash says) the paupers — they led the strife, but the 250 men were merely dragged along...
Machazeh Avraham.
d) “Is it but a small thing unto you that [the God of Israel] has separated you...” (16:9).
A squire (porets) divided his estates among many stewards, who managed 2 or 3 estates each. One of them got only a single estate. He comes to complain before the squire that he was given so little. Hearing this, the squire takes away from him his single estate as well.
— Why do I deserve this? — asks the steward.
— Not only do you not give me another estate, you take my only one away too?
— Because you are a thief; otherwise why would you be such a fool as to want more estates to manage and to bring more work upon yourself? You must be stealing and licking off a good bone...
That is what Moses asked Korah’s congregation: “Is it but a small thing unto you that he has separated” etc.? You have too little work as servants of the Tent of Meeting, “and you seek the priesthood also”? You want something more to manage? Ah, you surely don’t mean the Haggadah but the kneidlach...
Ohel Yaakov.
e) Korah and his congregation.
In Avot Korah’s strife is called “the dispute of Korah and all his congregation”. Did Korah then quarrel with the congregation? It should surely say “the dispute of Korah and Moses”.
Yes — the quarrel-mongers also tear at one another enough among themselves; they too have no peace among themselves. Only when it is a matter of opposing Moses are they all one... “Korah and all his congregation”: Korah and his own congregation do not live in peace among themselves either...
Noam Elimelech.
f) “And [the earth] swallowed them... and all their goods” (16:32).
What sin did Korah’s property [majątek] commit?
— Because all his insolence and his nerve to incite came only from his wealth... Were it not for his money he would not have waged such a quarrel...
And why did the sons of Korah not die?
— Because they took no inheritance, and so they were already as dead: “a pauper is accounted as dead”...
Asam be-shem [?].
Haftarah.
g) “For the Lord will not forsake His people for His great name’s sake.”
The Midrash (Ruth) distinguishes: in exile God does not forsake us “for His great name’s sake”, and in the Land of Israel He did not forsake us because “the Lord will not forsake His people, neither will He abandon His inheritance”.
That is: in the Land of Israel we were “His people” — His people He did not forsake, as a father does not forsake his child; nowadays He does not forsake us “for His great name’s sake”, so that people should not talk... and so a few bones are tossed to us out of pity...
Kokhav mi-Yaakov.
Avot.
h) “Who is wise? — He who learns from every man” (4:1).
Why does the folk saying go: “Every fool has his own sense”?
— Because a wise man learns from everyone and does not rely only on his own sense, whereas the fool holds fast only to his own foolish sense — he is the cleverest of all... He has only his own sense.
Botzina de-Nehora.
What's New in Zagłębie? — Będzin: A Representative of the Starostwo at a Session of the Kehilla Council

[Head of the local section; Będzin — kehilla.]
What's New in Zagłębie?
(Date boxes: Friday, 4 Tammuz 5691 — piątek 19 czerwca 1931 [Friday, 19 June 1931].)
Będzin
A Representative of the Starostwo at a Session of the Kehilla Council.
For lack of a quorum the session did not take place
This week we again had a "sensation". The previous allocation of the parnasim [kehilla board members] was changed once again. The new allocation again turned out unfavourable for the Zionist list, which lost 2 mandates, which were allotted 1 to list 8 (Hitachdut) and 1 to list 1 (Mordechai Dafner).
On the Agudah list only the persons were changed: instead of Messrs. M. L. Silberfreund and Y. M. Ehrlich, Y. Welgryn[?] and Mr. Y. A. Landau came in again.
On the strength of this fresh "victory" the kehilla council was summoned to a session, which was to take place on Tuesday evening.
At the session, according to the "strategic plans" of the "Agudah", only a mere commission was to be elected, which would conduct the elections to the board.
The crush to get into the session hall was very strong; getting inside smacked of broken limbs, but the "work" was in vain — the session did not take place.
Those who came to the session were the Agudah parnasim and their[?] allies, together a number of 8.
A surprise for everyone was the appearance of the representative of the Starostwo, Referent Mr. Mandyszewski[?], accompanied by 2 policemen, who, at the demand of the representative of the authorities, removed the "gallery" [the public] from the session hall. Only the parnasim and the representatives of the press were left in the hall.
As soon as the kehilla president Mr. A. And[?] the 'sick' husband at first pretended not to know and did not want to believe what 'mouths' were saying; he naively believed in his faithful wife, who, by the way, is a very decent woman, runs a decent household on little money and, above all, has presented him with 3 lovely children.
Only when people took him — the husband, that is — by the arm and led him to the 'romantic spot' where his 'woman of valour' was merrily spending her time, did he finally open his eyes, and then — vanished altogether...
When the 'secret' came out, relatives on both sides began to take an interest in the tangled affair, which has already found its echo before the rabbinate. Witnesses are being summoned, people question and investigate; the little wife denies it 'stone and bone', screams that she owes God nothing but her soul [i.e. is wholly innocent]; the husband, she says, has abandoned her and her children to their fate.
The rabbinate first of all ordered that the husband's family should support the children.

A Very Important Ruling of the Supreme Tribunal — Concerning Income Tax (podatek dochodowy)

The new ruling of the Supreme Administrative Tribunal [Najwyższy Trybunał Administracyjny] on the assessment of income tax (podatek dochodowy) is of unusually great importance for all merchants.
For merchants who keep no trade books, the most painful question is that the income tax is assessed higher than what they declare in the tax return (zeznanie).
All disputes and differences of opinion over income tax always revolve around the question: when does the tax authority have the right to assess the income higher than stated in the return, and when does it have no right to do so.
Until now the tax authority has taken the position that as soon as the return is questioned (kwestionowane) by a questioning notice sent to the taxpayer, the tax authority has a free hand and no longer needs to take the return into account at all.
Quite differently the Supreme Administrative Tribunal has recently ruled, in the case heard on 17 December 1930, under number 28 - 4511.
The Tribunal ruled that the tax authority may assess the income tax higher than the return only if the questioning queries were not answered satisfactorily, so that according to the authority's materials the income was indeed higher on the grounds of the questioning points.
The tax authority, however, may not assess a higher income than stated in the return by relying on other facts, not those stated in the questioning notice.
This very point of the ruling is of enormous importance for all merchants, because very often the higher assessment is made precisely on the basis of other grounds, not those stated in the questioning notice.
We shall give the following example here, so that every taxpayer may know when he can rely on this important ruling.
For instance, the tax office (urząd) stated in the questioning notice that according to the office's information the income from sugar was higher — not 2 per cent as declared, but 4 per cent, and therefore the income was higher. There was nothing more in the questioning notice. But later they assessed the turnover of sugar higher, and they also increased the assessment according to the turnover and income of the other goods kept in the business.
This too is unlawful in the sense of the aforementioned ruling of the Supreme Administrative Tribunal. For if only the size of the profit on sugar was questioned, it was not permitted to assess the sugar turnover higher, nor to increase the turnover (obrót) and income of the remaining goods.
The income-tax assessment may be raised above the return only on the point that is touched upon in the questioning notice.
And even this can happen only when the taxpayer has not fully removed the tax authority's doubts with his reply.
Ad. B. S.

"Ma Yafit" or Provocation?

[Będzin — kehilla; polemical article.] At the constituent session of the newly elected Będzin kehilla council, which took place in the presence of the vice-starosta [deputy district head], the following sad fact occurred:
After taking over the chair as the elected president, I began, as a matter of course, to conduct the session in the Yiddish language — but here the leader of the "Agudah" [Agudas Yisroel], the parnas Rinski, called upon me to conduct the session exclusively in the Polish language.
Well, a question arises, first of all a question of principle: must we Jews ourselves demand of ourselves that in our purely Jewish institutions our sessions be conducted in the Polish language? We Jews, who have been waging a struggle of many years for the equal rights of our languages, even in the municipal and state institutions — shall they themselves renounce their rights [sic] in their own autonomous institutions?
Then I wish to put a second, purely formal and logical question: how does Mr. Rinski dare — you, who cannot yourself pronounce a single word of Polish — to demand that a session be conducted in Polish, thereby exposing yourself to public ridicule, and thereby you weaken the prestige of Jewish autonomy?
The sad fact becomes still more vexing when we recall that the initiative comes from those elements who wage an embittered struggle for the kehilla to be a purely religious institution, and that for that purpose the sadly notorious Paragraph 20 was created, so that the "sinners" should not weaken the religious character of the kehilla.
And now the main question arises: what is the Agudah after with its clumsy proposal — perhaps only to find favour in the eyes of the squire [porets], who was present at the session, or did they simply mean thereby to provoke the newly elected kehilla leadership? If that is your aim, you have certainly not hit the mark with it, for such Jesuitical tricks have only a contemptible and repellent effect. This was proved to us by the last kehilla elections; here too the "Agudah" made use of all sorts of electoral machinations, beginning with par. 20 and the "famous" sermon from the Sejm rostrum by the notorious insolent fellow from Łódź, to the effect that communist cells [jaczejki] sit in the Jewish kehillas — but the "Agudah" received from Jewish Będzin the verdict it deserved: the Jewish masses showed that they are politically mature enough and understand where the truth is and where the lie is, and they gave a proud and courageous answer by voting for national Jewry. Now, too, the Jewish masses will not let themselves be spat in the face by such people, who in their whole essence are exactly the opposite of what they preach.
Jewish Będzin will understand that the "Agudah's" proposal to conduct the session in the Jewish kehilla in Polish means either singing "Ma Yafit" or provoking — as if to say "we are the loyal citizens"...
Yitzhak Wygodzki.

What's New in Upper Silesia?

[Upper Silesia — news.] Soviet trade mission places orders for millions of złoty.
As the Katowice press reports, the Soviet trade mission, which recently stayed in Upper Silesia, has placed large orders at the local ironworks.
The orders amount to several million złoty.
For a union of the N.P.R. [Narodowa Partia Robotnicza, National Workers' Party] with the Chadeks [Christian Democrats].
On Sunday a convention of the N.P.R. in Upper Silesia took place in Katowice. Several Sejm deputies also took part in the convention.
The main item of the convention was the union of the N.P.R. with the Ch. D. [Christian Democracy].
The proposal was accepted in principle.
One year in prison for killing a man.
The Katowice district court sentenced a certain Pluty Alojzy [Alojzy Pluty?] to one year in prison for killing a member of the Powstańcy [the Silesian Insurgents' organization].
Suicide of 3 unemployed men.
In Katowice 3 unemployed men decided to commit suicide. For this purpose they dug a deep pit in a coal mine, where the air was filled with gases. Then they lit a match, which caused an explosion, and all of them were burnt to cinders.
Catastrophe while trying to avoid an accident.
Outside Katowice the engineer Wilk, travelling in a car that he was driving himself, saw a drunkard lying on the highway. Wishing to save the drunkard from an accident, he swerved the car, but at that moment the car overturned, and the engineer's wife and a child, who were in the car, were thrown out onto the pavement and severely injured.
Death of an unemployed man [headline: "mord" — murder; the item itself describes a suicide].
At the freight station in Katowice an unemployed man threw himself under a train, which cut off the suicide's head.
Brawl during a match.
On Sunday a brawl broke out during a match at a sports ground in Katowice. A number of players were injured.
Dąbrowa

[Dąbrowa — local news; a swindle, Betar.] A "trading house" with little peppercorns
Into the colonial-goods [grocery] shop of Mr. L. Rechnic in Dąbrowa [Górnicza] came a Christian who introduced himself as the owner of a trading house in Königshütte [Królewska Huta, today Chorzów] and asked for an order.
Mr. Rechnic, seeing that the prices of the colonial goods offered were affordable, placed a trial order for the sum of 80[?] złoty.
A few days later Mr. Rechnic received a notice from the post office that the order was ready to be collected.
When Mr. Rechnic brought home the goods he had redeemed, only then did it become clear that he had fallen victim to a swindler. In the parcel of goods there were a few small packets of pepper and more such "bargains"...
The Rechnic family went off to Königshütte, where, after much searching, they finally found the "trading house"...
Rechnic reported the swindle to the police, but there it was explained to him that the proprietor of that "trading house" is mentally ill...
From Betar.
The local Betar, which has already existed for 2 years, arranged in the hall of "Maccabi" a propaganda lecture with the participation of the comrades of Brit HaTzohar [the Union of Zionist Revisionists] in Będzin, Langfus and Jaskierowicz, who spoke on the topic "The present situation in Zionism". A provisional committee was elected, consisting of: A. Sztajnberg (chairman), Jehuda Unger (secretary), Ranter (treasurer).
At the lecture 25 comrades declared their adherence, and we are embarking on a broad, wide-ranging activity for the Revisionist idea.
Olkusz

[Olkusz — local news; and Będzin — sport and youth.] A terrible storm.
On Sunday before dawn a terrible storm passed over here [Olkusz], accompanied by heavy thunder and lightning, which caused great damage. In the village of Kroczyce a thunderbolt struck the house of Michał Jędryk, who was severely injured together with his under-age boy. The house was completely burnt down.
—o—
Excursion of Będzin's Hakoach to Oświęcim.
In connection with the 10th anniversary of the Jewish sports club Kadimah in Oświęcim, which takes place on Sunday the 28th of this month, the Będzin "Hakoach" is organizing a larger excursion, and they will at the same time take part in the jubilee celebration.
—o—
Summer colony of "Sinai".
The youth organization "Sinai" in Będzin is organizing a summer colony for its members in Daytshe ["Dajcze" — probably the village of Niemce near Dąbrowa, today Ostrowy Górnicze; identification uncertain].
Next Wednesday almost all the members from Będzin leave for the colony, as well as a large number of members of the newly founded "Sinai" organization in Sosnowiec.
Where Is One to Get the Rent Money?

[Poland — economy and taxes; opinion.] Where is one to get the rent money? That is the question one hears in the street of late. With everything else one can somehow manage: one eats, or one doesn't eat; one has a garment made, or one doesn't. But rent — there no expedient helps, that one simply has to pay; so where is one to get it? It appears that in the "high windows" [the authorities] too, where no rent is paid, they have realised this, and they want to squeeze out of the public, by way of the rent, the few groszy they need.
With the taxes things are tight: however much one squeezes the public, it always finds a way out and does not pay. If a monopoly is put on liquor, it drinks no liquor. A monopoly on tobacco — it does not smoke. Even a tax on trade is not safe either: a man closes the shop and does not pay. But there is one thing he cannot renounce: a dwelling. That he must have, and if he cannot do without it, then he has indeed been seized by his weak side. If he cannot do without it, let him pay — and pay he will. And therefore this very point can be exploited and the public squeezed: raise the rent to double, and perhaps to even more. Never mind — rent has to be paid.
That, it seems, is how those who are planning to raise the rent think. Where the tenant will get the money to pay, they do not ask. He will have to pay. If he does not pay, he will be put out of the dwelling. If the landlord does not want to put him out, the landlord will pay. Roughly so do they reason there in the high windows, and they are apparently very pleased with the idea.
Yes, the landlord will have to pay — that is where the nail is lodged, that is what it is all about. It follows that the new decree affects the landlords more than the tenants. They, the landlords, will have to become the bailiffs; they will have to collect the tax from the tenants (lit. "neighbours") and hand it in at the cashier's office. For his trouble he [the landlord] will receive nothing at all; he will be an unpaid servant, and on top of that the business will cost him very dear.
For one must not fool oneself: at the present day there are already thirty per cent of tenants who do not pay their rent regularly. With a doubling of the rent it will come out, at the least, to as many again, i.e. 60 per cent of the tenants will be in arrears with the rent. Since the tax office will not want to know about that and will demand of the landlord that he pay what is due from his house, such a man will either pay or throw the tenants out; both possibilities, however, are impossible.
A landlord rightly remarked to me that the affair may lead to our reaching in Poland the same result as in Vienna, where 80 per cent of all houses have passed into the hands of the city. There the Socialist municipality (magistrat) introduced an original kind of tenant protection. The landlord was indeed not allowed to take more than the dwelling had cost before the war, but he was allowed to take it only in pre-war currency, i.e. he received as good as nothing. With that money he had to maintain the house. The municipality laid upon the tenants a dwelling tax such that it amounted to as much as the dwelling really ought to cost. The upshot was that only the municipality had an income, and the landlord became an unpaid guardian of the municipality's revenues. This policy led to the owners barely managing to rid themselves of the houses, and everything passed to the municipality.
I do not know whether that is bad; perhaps it is actually good. But one should call the child by its name and not play hide-and-seek. Moreover, the matter ought to concern, first of all, the landlords and not the tenants, because it is the landlords who will be dunned. The tenants need not be so very afraid, for a whole world will not, after all, be turned out of its dwellings.
Where is one to get the rent money? — thousands of people ask today, and find no answer. Will it be easier when they ask: where is one to get the dwelling tax? Will the public sooner have the means to pay? There are many things happening among us that we do not understand. Least of all, however, do we understand those who sit there and think up such projects: do they really not know, do they not feel what is going on among us? Or perhaps they pretend not to know, as that peasant says: if there is no liquor, let us at least talk about liquor; if there are no taxes, let us at least talk about taxes!...
Sh. Y. Stupnicki.
A Terrible Jewish Murder in Jędrzejów — The President of the Kehilla Is Killed in the Middle of the Market

[Jędrzejów — murder; kehilla.] A terrible Jewish murder in Jędrzejów.
The president of the kehilla is killed in the middle of the market.
From Jędrzejów they write to us:
On Sunday morning a terrible murder occurred here, committed by one Jew against another.
The course of the murder is as follows:
In the middle of the market a quarrel broke out among several Jews who are partners in the buses that run on the Jędrzejów—Kielce and Jędrzejów—Kraków line.
A partner in that business was also Mr Meir Lewin, an artisan by trade. The quarrel took on serious forms, and from words they passed to deeds.
At that moment Meir was informed that his partner Hershl Bornsztajn was fighting with the other partners. When Meir heard this, he snatched a knife from the kitchen, with which he rushed to the spot where the brawl was taking place.
When Mr Bornsztajn saw Meir with the knife in his hand, he held him back, and between them a struggle with knives ensued. The result was a terrible one: Lewin fell dead on the spot.
The murdered man had been elected a few weeks ago, thanks to the majority of the artisans' parnasim [board members], as president of the kehilla in Jędrzejów.
The murder has shaken the whole town. Thousands of people took part in the funeral, which was held on the same day.
A wife with 6 children have been left orphaned.
The murderer has been arrested.
The fate of dozens of families depends on the existence of “Beit Lechem”.

[Będzin — charity and institutions.] (On the meeting of “Beit Lechem”.)
A few weeks ago the general meeting of the “Beit Lechem” society in Będzin took place. Because of the small number of those attending, the item “elections” was not held.
Several weeks have passed; the number of recipients grows every week and the income becomes smaller and smaller, because the old board is not active and there is not yet a new one, so that the dozens of recipients who, thanks to “Beit Lechem”, do not have spoiled Sabbaths and holidays — are left abandoned...
So then, next Monday the 29th, at 4 in the afternoon, the continuation of the meeting will take place at the “Merchants' Association” [Sochrim-Farein], at which a board must be elected that will carry on the activity, will go on running this institution that is so necessary at the present time. If the required number of members does not come, the institution will be closed, and the whole responsibility falls on the Jewish population of Będzin.
In the name of the board
A. D.[?] Balimowski,
Sh. Lewkowicz.
A badge sale for the benefit of three institutions.

[Będzin — charity and institutions.] On Thursday, the 2nd of July [lipiec], a badge sale [flag day] is being arranged by the “Linat HaCholim” society in Będzin.
“Linat HaCholim” with its “children” — the maternity institution and the “Moshav Zkenim” [old-age home] — has not arranged any fund-raising event whatsoever in the course of 3 years, in comparison with other philanthropic institutions; but the situation is so critical that the board has changed its system of silence kept until now and organised a badge sale.
Let everyone therefore remember that the badge sale is for 3 institutions, and not get off with idle excuses [shehi pehi].
A fire in Wolbrom.
[Wolbrom — fire.] On Saturday night a fire broke out on Listopad Street in Wolbrom. 2 houses went up in smoke. Several poor Jewish families have been left without a roof.
The Będzin “Gordonia” youth goes out to the countryside.

[Będzin — youth movements.] Next Thursday the first group of participants leaves Zagłębie for the summer colony [summer camp] that the pioneering youth organisation “Gordonia” is arranging in the village of Nickulina, which lies in the Beskid region.
The regional leadership [Hanhaga HaGlilit] has already appointed the directors and also made the last preparations for this year's colonies, which will begin on the second of July and last until the end of August.
The first colony, in which over 40 people will take part, will be under the medical supervision of the esteemed Rajcza[?] doctor, Mr. Frischer.
