Help Yourselves! (On the Export Project for the Chałupniks)

[Zagłębie — Economy; crafts, cooperatives and export.] 1.
Following on from the points made in the last article about the hard situation of the Jewish chałupniks [chałupnicy — small home-based craftsmen working for merchants] — especially on the question of finding a sales market abroad for our local ready-made products (clothing and leather) — it will be, we believe, particularly important to mention a few facts and observations which throw a clear light on the considerable export possibilities in the sense of one-hundred-percent self-help on the foundations of sound cooperation, for the happiness and well-being of thousands of impoverished, hard-working Jewish families in our region.
But there is one great obstacle, which lies like a stumbling block on the road to the realisation of every large and important action in the ranks of the Jewish petty bourgeoisie. What is lacking is the strong initiative, the energetic hand that would organise and conduct a great action with a sense of responsibility and give it an appropriate direction, adapted to the trading and working conditions concerned, even on our own home market. At the very top, naturally, stands the question of o r g a n i s a t i o n — one of the hardest and most thankless efforts in the process of realising all our aspirations.
The concept of organisation has lately become altogether very delicate with us, rubbery, relative — it can be stretched and developed so long until it — melts away [?]... It will be quite enough if we turn back a few pages in the very latest history of Jewish public life in Poland for us to become great unbelievers in the possibility of larger Jewish cooperative enterprises existing, whether for raw materials or for finished production. We have, unfortunately, far too little routine [experience] and understanding for what we usually mean by the concept of c o o p e r a t i o n (jointly owned, collective enterprises with limited liability and binding discipline).
2.
Some time ago the writer of these lines presented to the then existing Supreme Council of the Jewish artisans' associations in Zagłębie a detailed project for exporting clothing and footwear to such countries with which we are without the slightest doubt able to compete (especially with our enormously cheap labour force); it also indicated the way of reaching agreement, and in general of making contact, on this whole important matter with the appropriate bodies abroad.
Under the said project a central purchasing office for Zagłębie was to be created (incidentally, the plan covered only Zagłębie), and all operations were to be carried out through the "Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego" in Katowice.
At the time, representatives of the administrative and industrial authorities took an interest in the project, to such an extent that the instructor of the guild corporations in the Kielce voivodeship, Dr. Wojtowicz [?], referred the matter to the Ministry, recognising it (the project) as a first and important step in the sense of self-help for the chałupniks and small traders themselves, and at the same time as an export experiment from a purely economic [?] standpoint. Full support was thus promised by the relevant government bodies; all that was needed was to take the first step...
The management of the Kielce Chamber of Crafts and the chairman of the executive of the Central Jewish Artisans' Union in Poland, Mr. Ch. Rasner [Chaim Rasner], also took a positive attitude to the question, and incidentally, some time later, at a plenary session of the Kielce Chamber of Crafts, a similar [?] step was taken regarding shoe export.
But — everywhere that same accursed "but"! But there, unfortunately, it remained — and hush-hush... The public goes on [doubtful word] in a thoroughly Jewish manner...
I recall the sarcastic remarks of certain "connoisseurs", that it is plain folly to think that any of us would be able to compete with the Czech "Baťa" or with German industry, which flood the entire world market with the cheapest ready-made clothing and shoe products. No amount of explanation helped then, but "what reason does not accomplish, time will" — and Białystok will prove it. Białystok and other textile-manufacturing centres [doubtful word] in Poland have found a sales market for ready-made clothing in the very heart of world industry, in the centre of the greatest textile industries in the whole world, in the land of millions of unemployed — in London and in Manchester...
Our project embraces a much broader programme of work and development, and with proper organisation there is a colossally rich field and favourable prospects for accomplishing very great things.
3.
It is, it seems, clear and plain that with the coming winter an enormous crisis begins in the ranks of the chałupniks. The last season stood under the sign of the general stagnation and unemployment in the country. Apart from that, the internal competition from the younger, newly arisen chałupniks (tailors and shoemakers especially) has brought the situation of the Jewish tailors and shoemakers in Zagłębie to the very last limits of the struggle for existence.
We do not want to say that it will get even worse — do not open your mouth to Satan! — but it is lamentable enough as it is now. Let at least now the strong initiative of s e l f - h e l p arise. Nobody will help us if we do not help ourselves. Let the quarrels among the chałupniks stop for a while. Not with shouting and not with outcries will the heavy wagon and the emaciated nags of work and bread be pushed forward even half an arshin. Only with joint effort and good will shall a real way out of the hard situation be found after all, namely: in the organisation of small-scale export, which in this case is also of great importance for the store-owner [magaziner — the merchant who commissions the work]. This is a common interest which must be exploited jointly. Let the initiative only come, let only the first steps be taken; courage, energy and good will — these are the preconditions for every self-help action.
There is now a favourable moment to make use of the holidays — so let someone be found among the store-owners or among the chałupniks who will call a large (joint) conference in Zagłębie, which will acquaint itself in detail with the whole project (in a newspaper article it is somewhat difficult) — and the way out will surely be found.
A. Gancwajch [?]
The Consequences of Placing a Sequestration on Rent for the Landlord's Debt

[Law — Housing and attachments; legal advice for tenants.] There are many landlords who owe taxes or other debts. Usually, in such cases, a sequestration [sekwestr] is placed on the rent payable by the tenants [lokatorzy].
Some landlords, however, will not hear of any [doubtful word] and go on demanding rent. The tenants affected are then bewildered and cannot by any means decide what to do: if they pay the sequestrator or the bailiff [komornik], they will "anger" the landlord. If, on the other hand, they pay the landlord, they fear that the executor [bailiff] will take away the last bit of their poor belongings.
It must therefore be stated clearly that merely on the strength of a so-called notice alone the bailiff or sequestrator has no right yet to carry out a seizure [zajęcie] and auction [licytacja] at the tenant's.
If a tenant does not comply with the provisions of the notice ("zapowiedzenie") and pays the landlord after all, the enforcement authority can for the time being do nothing more than draw up a report, and on that basis the court later imposes a fine on the guilty tenant.
Likewise a fine threatens in the case where he refuses [?] altogether to accept the notice or gives false particulars concerning the rent owed.
It must of course also be added that besides the threatened fines such a tenant also bears responsibility for the sum withheld with him; but this sum too can be claimed only by judicial means.
Letters from Home

[Będzin — satirical feuilleton; the year 5691 in review.] My friend Reb Shloyme, may his light shine.
Before we add up the total and close the debit and credit of the old, already passing year, I would like to have one more talk with you, as with a true close friend.
And in that "chat" we will indeed take a last look at the old year and "audit" its bundle of luggage that it is taking along with it...
As is the way of the world, when New Year's Eve comes people air everything bad and lament the old year, while they do not spare compliments for the new guest, the new year...
We want to be an exception in this respect; we will see the old year off with "cheerful" faces, because in our opinion the old year 5691 left the whole world, and us Jews in particular, a great many "good" things: it finally "solved" the problem of good and bad, "uprooted" the perpetual hatred, the bitter envy between the nations, and gave proper expression to
— "a trouble shared is half a consolation"...
Let us not fool ourselves, Reb Shloyme, and take a look at how things now stand in every state: even rich, golden America, which was the provider[?] of the whole world, the land that said "the silver is mine and the gold is mine," already lies under the heavy burden too, under the national plague called — crisis. True, the crisis-disease has gripped Europe for a number of years already, but never before was its face so conspicuous as in the year 5691.
Yes, Reb Shloyme, so it is, and if you are not a firm believer in what we have shown you, we will try to give some living facts proving that the year 5691 brought a great deal of "good" in all fields, cultural as well as economic.
Let us go in order:
In former years, in a city like Będzin you could count on your fingers the firms that bore the title:
"Company with limited liability"...
Real aristocrats they were — what more is there to say? "G.m.b.H."?
And today, just stroll past the lane "Zhimne D..." [?] — you can see on almost every sign of every shop a large inscription:
— "Spółka z ogr. odp." [limited company]...
Yes, there are no more big and small merchants; they are all equal to me — equal paupers, equal deliberate bankrupts, equal grabbers — "and we became paupers together"...
The merchant world in general rose to a high "level" last year: the ever-existing term of abuse has been[?] abolished — bankrupt! bankruptnik! — a word it was a disgrace to let out of one's mouth. If it ever happened that a merchant went bankrupt, he fled at midnight to distant parts, wandered off to where the black pepper grows, but the stain on the family remained forever.
But today — what a delight! A merchant takes "parcels" [goods on credit] on Sunday, and the next day he says like a gentleman:
— "I am suspending payments"...
Not a little did 5691 do for culture. In this year great "cultural values" were created. The Yiddish word has been greatly "elevated"; the formerly "good" Yiddish press has capitulated to the command of the hour. The columns of the Yiddish press no longer deal with the old "outlived" articles about culture, art and other such "nonsense." Today the world is open, and everything that is done in the innermost chambers, in the kitchens and in the merry little houses must be made public for "the broad strata of the Jewish popular masses"...
The year 5691 tore the locks off the secret houses, off the hidden places to which only the bourgeoisie, the sons-in-law on board [kest] and the only sons had access; a time has come when the poorest child, scarcely owning five groszy, buys a newspaper from which he draws "spiritual nourishment"...
A great "victory" did the past year win over the Jewish communities. Already years ago we had no great joy from the life of our kehillas. Ever since we were blessed with the thirty-six righteous men, the Jewish communities began to sink and gradually lost the ground of their existence. It is possible that the death-throes of the kehillas would have lasted a very long time yet, but then came the year 5691, the year that could prove that in Jesuit Spain churches would be burned [the Spanish church burnings of May 1931] — and it put an end to kehilla life... There is no longer anyone to speak of, anyone to criticise; those who still supposedly stand at the helm of the present kehillas are "studying" the Mishnah:
— "while his dead lies before him"...
In the religious field, too, a great deal of positive work was created during the year. As in all the Jewish Diaspora, special committees of "Shomrei ha-Torah ve-ha-Dat" [Guardians of the Torah and Faith] were founded in Zagłębie too, which display strong activity in the field of education. Above all, the committee is "active" in the public elementary schools [szkoły powszechne], out of which (naturally, before the committees were created) generations of ignoramuses grew.. The Talmud Torahs were reorganised this year and placed on "healthy foundations," spiritually as well as materially.
The work of the above-mentioned committees was very hard, not only internally; they, the "Guardians of the Torah," also had to wage a hard struggle externally... Little was lacking, and the Talmud Torahs would, God forbid, have fallen into the hands of the sinners, of those "who want the Talmud Torah children to learn Chumash without the [?]"... But they did not succeed: with united forces the spiritual leaders went out to battle and won a "victory"...
The kashrut matter has, thank God, been "regulated." It is already "clear" which butchers are trusted for kashrut and which are not. On the other hand, the sausage question has not yet been regulated. "Kraków wasn't built in a day either"; one surely cannot settle such a "weighty matter" in the course of a few years... Slowly, slowly they will also establish the "diagnosis" of the "kosher sausages"...
Public life "pulsated" strongly this year. The feeling of unity made itself felt at every step; everywhere the defenders stood on guard and defended the interests of
— their pockets and...
— — — — —
I hear a knock at the door.
— Please, come in.
Before my eyes appears a radiant figure, wearing a golden crown on its head. From its courteous bow before me I see that on the top of the crown a "B" [ב, numeral 2] is engraved...
At once I realise that this is surely the new year 5692, and I welcome it with the verse:
— "Blessed are you in your coming!" May the "B," the first letter of Bereshit, bring a new, happy epoch for all Israel — so wishes your friend
Ben Amrak[?].
'Doom-Mongers Will Be Thrown Out' (From Our Leipzig Correspondent)

[Leipzig — economy; the international fair; letter from our correspondent.] "Doom-mongers (Miesmacher) will be thrown out" — such a poster has been pasted up in all the Leipzig fair halls. In Germany "Miesmacher" is the name for all those men [?] who talk themselves into believing, and want to persuade others too, that things are bad and can no longer get any better...
Doom-mongers have no place at the Leipzig Fair, the place where the whole German and the leading world industry have come together to show what they have achieved lately. All doom-mongers must fall silent when they enter one of the great fair palaces and behold the great creation of world industry.
The Leipzig Fair now has about seven thousand exhibitors, who have brought everything the human mind can devise. And although the times are bad and the people have no money to buy, the biggest and the smallest things, cheaper and dearer goods, are being produced here, and people wait until the time comes when these things can be sold and will find their buyers.
Doom-mongers will be thrown out...
— — —
When you enter one of the fair palaces, a kind of melancholy comes over you when you see how many thousands and tens of thousands of things are being made, and one manufacturer stands next to another, one competitor next to the other, and one product is laid out next to the next, nearly all with the same face, and the manufacturer and his neighbour look at you with greedy eyes:
Perhaps you will buy something? Perhaps you will pay money and order something? Perhaps thanks to you there will be some work to do?..
And it seems to you that behind him stand the hundreds and thousands of workers whom he employs, or could have employed, begging you:
Give us work, so that we can provide for our wives and children [?] as before...
And behind them, it seems, stand the children — tens of thousands, hundreds of thousands and millions of hungry children, looking at you with innocent childish eyes and begging you:
Buy something, so that we may for once drink warm milk or eat a piece of meat, and not always cabbage and cabbage...
And you look on and cannot help, and a kind of melancholy comes over you and you become a doom-monger, one of those who have already despaired of better times and want to persuade others too that there is nothing to hope for from better times...
— — —
"Doom-mongers will be thrown out." This had to be written up in all the fair halls; it is a kind of poison, cocaine, which serves to numb oneself and tear oneself out of despair.
Had the German working people fallen into despair, the whole industry, with all the technology that has conquered the world, would have fallen silent. Everything would have come to a standstill and the working nerve of life that still holds up the whole edifice would have stopped beating. It would have come to a catastrophe such as world history has never known to this day.
No, doom-mongers are not needed here...
— — —
Among the national exhibitions of individual countries, Spain, the new republic, has now come for the first time. One may regard the "new Spanish masters" as one likes, but one must admit that the new government is making an effort to do something.
What have they not brought to the Leipzig Fair? Real royal delicacies... fruit and wine, iron and porcelain, fabrics and silk, lead and furniture, and everything has its own Spanish note, which cannot be denied — it comes from a country we do not even know...
And looking at all these precious goods which the newest competitor has brought to Leipzig, to the greatest world market, our heart rejoices and we say rightly:
"Doom-mongers will be thrown out."
Z. Haber.
A Little Feuilleton: On Rosh Hashanah It Is Written

[Feuilleton — Rosh Hashanah; the press.] On Rosh Hashanah it is written...
Does it not look like an agreement between above and below, between heaven and earth?
We here, on the sinful earth, write all year round: one whiles away [?] his days and writes for the editorial wastebasket, one reckons up his debts and writes them on the wall, one writes anonymous letters, one writes appeals, and one writes up other people's belongings for distraint..
This we do all year; we don't spare ink, we pour out whole buckets — and when Rosh Hashanah comes we lay down our pens and begin to pour out tears: one prays for himself and one for others, one for health and one for a livelihood, one for long life and one for forgiveness...
But they, the angels in heaven, do otherwise: all year they do not dip a pen into the inkwell — why should they write, when the writing writes itself! That is what makes them angels after all — "the ledger is open and the hand writes." But when Rosh Hashanah comes, "and the angels hasten" — they snatch our pens and set to work...
All our sensational newspapers, which have lately sprung up like mushrooms after rain, are not capable of inventing in the course of a whole year such sensations as the angels create in the couple of days of Rosh Hashanah: who by beast... who by plague...
And precisely in this lies the difference between us and them — we write only what has been (what is yet to be we cannot know, after all), and they write what is yet to be — what is past does not interest them...
You will surely ask a question: since what has been does not interest them, what then do we have to fear? The answer is...
Anyway, the eve of Rosh Hashanah is no time to ask questions and give answers — we had better leave it for Passover, for the Seder...
Onkelos [?].

Dvoyre Yakhet Goes on Strike Against the Lord of the Universe...

By Y. Oberzhanek [J. Oberżanek?].
I am, after all, not born today and not born yesterday; I have been through strikes before — political strikes, economic strikes and protest strikes. But a strike against the Lord of the Universe I am hearing of for the first time — and who, do you think, is on strike against the Lord of the Universe?
— My Dvoyre Yakhet.
You think my Dvoyre Yakhet is, God forbid, a Bundist, or a socialist, heaven forbid? Oh, where did you get that idea? She is as far[?] from socialism as a politician is from honesty...
So how does she suddenly come to strikes, and against the Lord of the Universe at that? The excuse is: — fashions!
Listen, Jews: whoever thought up fashions, may he never get out of the „Seym"[?]... They thought up a fashion for spas. Suddenly all the women became „ailing" — each one suffers from a different malady. They all travel for a „cure" to Szczawnica, to Sopot, to Krynica; and when one goes to the spas one takes along bathing „spodenki" [shorts], and when one comes back from such a „cure", it comes out on the husband's head.
My Dvoyre Yakhet, too, once tasted the taste of the „bathing spodenki", and about those „spodenki" I can sing and tell to this very day...
Well, what connection do the „bathing spodenki" have with my wife's strike? There is a connection, and quite a big one, as you will soon hear.
Every year at this time, the week before Rosh Hashanah, we — I and my wife — are very busy. My wife with the dressmaker and the milliner, and I with looking for „seats" [in the synagogue]. My wife had a task: in the women's synagogue she was to „reign" [królować] with her toilette, so that the women would burst with „envy" [zazdrość] and the men would tear their eyes out; and I had a second task — to find „comfortable [wygodne] seats".
What my Dvoyre Yakhet meant by „comfortable" I already knew: close to the men's synagogue, so that on an „occasion" [okazja] she could catch a „glance", and during the „interval" [antrakt] between Shacharit and Musaf she could cast an „eye" — at the cantor; and the cantor too had to be a „[—]"[?], a „personage" [osoba] before God and men...
When Rosh Hashanah used to come, that was indeed my task: to find for my Dvoyre Yakhet a „seat" with all the enumerated „comforts" [wygody]. If Dvoyre Yakhet had all the „comforts", the women burst with vexation and „envy" — and all was well; if not, if, heaven forbid, another Jewish woman turned up in the women's synagogue with a finer[?] „seat", I was not sure of my life...
This year I ask my wife: Dvoyre Yakhet, what about „seats"? It is already the eve of Rosh Hashanah — where will we pray this year?
Mine does not answer. And when Dvoyre Yakhet is silent, the best thing is to be silent too, and so I was silent.
Next day I say again: Dvoyre Yakhet, you've forgotten where you stand — Rosh Hashanah is approaching — we must give a thought to „seats"!
Mine is silent again.
Then I understood that this silence was not smooth, that it was a calm before a storm. I did not think long and hired two „seats" — of course, with all the necessary „comforts".
Dvoyre Yakhet, I say to her — you can wish me mazel tov.
— What's the mazel tov?
— I have hired, with good luck, „seats" — once-in-a-lifetime „seats", right at the front; the very „cream" [śmietanka] will be praying there.
— Who asked you? — she came out with her tongue — who needs seats, when this year I am not going to synagogue.
— Dvoyrele, Yakhetshi, are you joking? What do you mean, you won't go to synagogue? What Jewish daughter does not go to pray on Rosh Hashanah?
— Harsh Makhl [Hersh-Mekhl]! — she banged on the table — if I say not going, it will be not going; I've prayed enough, understood?
— Dvoyre Yakhet, have you, God forbid, gone out of your mind? The greatest „progressives" [postępowa], the greatest Sabbath-desecrators and treyf-eaters tremble on Rosh Hashanah before the Day of Judgement. When the fish in the water tremble, you want to sit at home?!... Nothing else but that someone has put a spell on you...
What use are stories[?] to you — I talked, I shouted, I got angry, and she stuck to her own: she is not going.
When I saw[?] that anger did not help, I changed my tone: Dvoyreshi, I begged her, explain the reasoning to me; you're no fool — why did you go to synagogue for twenty whole years, and precisely this year you have become so terribly „progressive"?...
Only then did she come out with the real talk:
— Listen to me, Harsh Makhl — she said — all those years, when I went to synagogue on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, it was understandable — I had something to pray for. I prayed that the Lord of the Universe should forgive me my sins that I had sinned all year long. Not only I — every Jewish woman who weeps and pours tears on the pages of the machzor has something to weep about... No Jewish woman weeps just like that, for pleasure... When you see a Jewish woman beating her heart at „Al Chet", she has something to beat it for — a Jewish woman does not beat her breast for nothing...
Now I ask you: what do I need to go to synagogue for this year? All those years, when every summer I travelled once to Sopot, once to Krynica — after such a „cure" I truly had to go to synagogue and cry my heart out, beg the Lord of the Universe to forgive me my sins that I had sinned „wilfully" and „unwittingly". After three months of „plaża" [the beach] I truly had to beat my heart „Al Chet"; but now? When the whole summer I have grown black and gloomy in Będzin, when the whole summer I haven't seen any beach before my eyes — I feel pure as a dove...
That is one thing. And secondly — what did you want, that I should go to synagogue in last year's „rag" while Yellow Beyle will go in a brand-new silk dress fresh off the needle, and I will burst watching? No, that she won't live to see from me!...
Well — I say — and therefore?
— Therefore — she says — if the Lord of the Universe could look on while Feygl the fishwife and the fat baker's wife „had a good time" [bawiły się] in Krynica, and I lay in chopped-up troubles up in the attic [górka]; if Yellow Beyle must have new silk dresses with „aganki"[?], and I must watch it and be crushed — if the Lord of the Universe wants it so, then this year I am not going to synagogue... No, no, I am not going...
Why should I drag it out for you? I tried with good and with bad, I spoke Turkish and Greek — nothing helped; she stuck to her own: she is on strike against the Lord of the Universe, and that's that...
And what is all this because of? Because of fashions. Had my Dvoyre Yakhet never tasted the taste of the Sopot and Krynica „bathing spodenki", she would have had no complaints against the Lord of the Universe this year...
I have heard of various strikes — political strikes, economic strikes — but a strike against the Lord of the Universe I am hearing of now for the first time...

The Year 5691 in Jewish Life.
(A Brief Summing-Up)

[Survey — the year in review.] Harder than in any other year, it falls to us this time to sum up Jewish life in the whole world in the just-ended year 5691. The present [?] summing-up, the balance-sheet of the past 12 months, is far more frightening than in the last hard post-war years. Never yet has the situation of the Jews everywhere, in every corner of the earth, been so grave and so cruel as in the year 5691.
The grey storm-clouds that have hovered long, long over Jewish heads will by no means withdraw; not a single ray of light will show itself in our life of exile — on the contrary: life grows harder and harder from one time to the next. The world economic crisis, raging with such danger, has struck first of all the Jewish people, which is losing the ground and the hold beneath its feet.
There is no country, apart from a few individual smaller states, where our situation could be secure. All the rights of equality that we fought for and won at all the peace and minorities congresses, all the constitutions and free civil laws that were guaranteed to us at all international forums — have remained merely historical documents, but without value; no nation has set about honestly and sincerely realising the promises given, so that all the decrees, outrages, pogroms, lawlessness, restrictions and economic oppression go on being continued year in, year out.
In Soviet Russia the Jewish situation and living conditions have not improved at all. The October Revolution shattered not only the Tsarist regime but also the life of three-million-strong Russian Jewry. The new economic arrangements of the Soviet government have declassed the Jew and driven him out of the Russian shtetl and village, turning him into a "lishenets" (one without rights), into a deproletarianised inhabitant whom nobody defends and who is hunted. The new five-year plan, the "Pyatiletka", which was to strengthen the threatened economic positions in the U.S.S.R., has given the Russian Jew nothing at all.
The G.P.U. continues its work, and its agents diligently use violent means against those who carry in their hearts the faith in national liberation, throwing them into the damp [?] prisons and deporting the Jewish martyrs to the wildest regions of Turkestan and to icy Siberia.
In Spain a revolution of the state took place a few months ago, which has also brought a change in the attitude of the Spaniards towards the Jewish people. Spain has at last thrown off the monarchy, driven King Alfonso out of the country, and on the ruins of despotism a free republic has been established.
The new Spanish government wishes to free itself of the former sins with regard to Jews, turning with an appeal to the Jewish people that it should consent to return to Spain.
In Germany, where Hitler's men were victorious at the last Reichstag elections, the life of the Jews there has worsened. The anti-Jewish outrages of the German "patriots" continue. The economic crisis that devours and oppresses the German people has not spared German Jewry either, which is living through terrible days.
Salonica (Greece), the former city of the great sages of Israel, was this year turned into a city of slaughter, incited by the Jew-hating press, which accused Greek Jewry of betraying the fatherland. Angen [?] the Greeks of Salonica fell upon the Jewish quarters, robbing and shedding the blood of dozens of Jewish souls. The Greek government — as always in such cases — did not react at once and did not suppress the first symptoms of the pogrom, and did not protect its threatened citizens at the proper time, but arrived with military help only after the pogrom. To this day — several months after the events — those guilty of the pogrom have not yet been punished, and the Jewish pogrom victims have not yet recovered from their painful wounds. Although the Greek Prime Minister, Venizelos, expressed to the sufferers his sympathy in their grief.. the Salonica pogrom will remain forever a stain on the history of the Greek people.
Mexico (America) too has favoured us with a pogrom. And as it seems, antisemitism is also penetrating into the land of Columbus. In general the position of the Jews in the United States has lately worsened.
The world crisis has also found its way across the sea; unemployment and the catastrophic economic situation are felt by American Jewry too, which for many years supported with a generous hand all the most important national, cultural and philanthropic institutions of the European Jews.
Here with us in Poland the Jewish situation has not changed for the better; on the contrary — it has worsened. The government treats "simultaneously" [probably a misprint for "indifferently"] the needs of its Jewish citizens, who are struggling hard for their subsistence.
Tens of thousands of Jews go about in Poland without employment and work, being forced to depend on the help and support of others. Lawlessness has remained in force, and no relief whatever has been granted in this respect. In the universities and even in the state secondary schools the Jew still has no foothold, and the government institutions are still closed to [?] the Jew.
The elections to the Sejm gave the three-million-strong Polish Jewry an unfavourable result, carrying through all in all only a few deputies. The small Jewish representation in the Polish parliament makes it harder to defend our just interests. The "Agudah" went to the elections on its own and, by its independent candidacy, wrecked many Jewish mandates. This wild, irresponsible Agudist deed was rewarded by the appropriate factors with the well-known Paragraph 20, which was exploited at the kehilla elections that took place not [?] long ago in Congress Poland.
In the cultural field we unfortunately cannot record anything positive. Our school organisations, which were created with so much toil and sacrifice, are wrestling with great material difficulties that threaten their existence. The new school year 1931-32 has opened, and tens of thousands of Jewish children have remained at home, outside school, without education, without an educator and without a teacher.
The only Hebrew newspaper of the Diaspora, "Ha-Tsefirah", which had reappeared after many years' interruption, could not keep itself going and had to close. On the other hand the Jewish street has been flooded with a mass of cheap trash newspapers, which demoralise the Jewish reader and which bear witness to the spiritual Jewish decline.
The general crisis has also had a bad effect on the Jewish book market, so that Jewish publishing is going through critical days. There is no interest in the book and in Yiddish literature, which naturally makes life hard for our writers.
Eretz Israel too has not escaped the bad economic situation. Private capital has begun to flow less to Eretz Israel; the national funds could not cover all the needs of colonisation, causing a certain unemployment in the country, on account of which the gates of Eretz Israel were this year closed to a workers' immigration (aliyah).
The political situation was quite a hard one this year. The Mandatory went on restricting our rights to Eretz Israel, narrowing with his own hands the obligations he had given us in 1917; the various "White Papers", the restrictions on land purchase in Eretz Israel, the negative answer to the demand for certificates for halutzim, the non-employment of Jewish workers in government enterprises, the appointment of a new High Commissioner for Eretz Israel without consultation with the Zionist Executive, and many other wrongs have undermined our trust in the English government, which resigned not long ago.
The latest political events in Great Britain give hope and faith that favourable changes will now set in in England's attitude to the Mandate, to Palestine policy and to the Jewish National Home.
— —
In Basel the 17th Zionist Congress took place, which unfortunately did not bring the desired outcome. Instead of dealing with the most important current problems, the Congress devoted its best time to an unhealthy debate about the final aim of Zionism. Dr. Weizmann stepped down from the presidency of the Zionist World Organisation, and in his place Nahum Sokolow was elected.
The Jewish Agency too, which had for the time being done little for the upbuilding of Eretz Israel, was reorganised and activated. But again the Agency was dealt a painful blow: the first appointed president of the Agency, Mr. Frankel of New York, died suddenly in Paris, without having managed to carry out the office and mission he had taken upon himself in Basel.
— —
We now stand on the threshold of the new year with full confidence that the year 5692 will be a year of happiness and contentment.
Matek Hampel.
In Honour of Rosh Hashanah

Little Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes. Collected[?] by Y. Y.

"Happy is the people that know the trumpet-sound" (Ashrei ha-am yod'ei teru'ah).
The shofar performs the same function as a preacher of reproof (mokhiach): it calls to repentance, and therefore there are many comparisons between the shofar and the preacher of morals:
a. First: "A shofar that was overlaid with gold is unfit (pasul)." If the preacher covers up for the men of gold, if he flatters and avoids rebuking the wealthy, he is unfit.
b. There is a special rule that a shofar must not be multi-coloured [misprinted]. The preachers too are often multi-coloured. "Once a man comes to depend on other people, his face changes into many colours" [printed "lebrat" for "lebriyot"]. The communal functionary often changes his face into various colours. Now he smiles at one man, and behind his back he twists his face at him. Sometimes a flattering little smile to this one and sometimes to his opponent — either way, a face rich in colours.
c. Into the shofar one blows through a little hole, and it comes out through a big hole. Moral preaching has the same fate: in one ear and out the other... But little goes in, through a small crack, and it goes out through a wide hole... — Olelot Efrayim.
• • •
A rabbi once takes up the shofar to blow, and it won't go — Satan has got inside it. There is no choice; one has to turn to a householder, a somewhat frivolous fellow, who can also blow — and with him it goes as smooth as butter...
After the prayers the householder says to the rabbi: Do you know, Rebbe, what happened? When Satan came and wanted to get into my shofar, I said: Listen here, you — all year long I obey you, so you might obey me at least once a year... — Folk saying.
• • •
We Jews plead, at the Judgement in Heaven, that we are confused in exile, that our troubles bewilder us, and therefore we do not fulfil our duties towards God. But Satan argues: duties are duties, that is no excuse...
On Rosh Hashanah, when the shofar is blown, Satan becomes confused ("in order to confound Satan") and cannot carry out his mission of accusation. So he sees for himself that when one is bewildered one cannot fulfil one's duties... — Rabbi Simcha Bunem of Przysucha.

"And Thou art faithful to revive the dead."
A rabbi once noticed a householder weeping bitterly during the Days of Awe as he said in the Shemoneh Esreh: "And Thou art faithful to revive the dead," and asked him the reason.
The man pours out his bitter heart to the rabbi: I have — he says — four sons, great good-for-nothings, and I know that soon I shall die and they will squander[?] my whole estate; and here the prayer speaks of the resurrection of the dead — I am afraid that when I rise at the resurrection, not a trace will be left of my fortune, and what shall I do then? Go begging from house to house?...
— Don't be afraid, — the rabbi reassures him — if you have four such sons, you will not rise at the resurrection at all...

"Man's origin is from dust and his end is to dust; at the peril of his life he earns his bread."
The soul and the body of man belong to two separate elements, and therefore their sources of nourishment are different as well. The body, as "its origin is from dust", should draw its livelihood from working the soil, from physical occupation; the soul, on the other hand, as a spiritual being, should be nourished by spiritual, higher food. Thus indeed was the Jew of old, when he was in his own homeland.
Today the roles have been reversed. The Jewish body is only a spiritual being... whereas his soul — "with his soul he earns his bread": the soul works for bread... Not the body works for a living; rather the head schemes for a living... — Ohel Yaakov [printed "Ihel Yaakov"].

"And because of our sins we were exiled from our land."
Not "because of our sins" (chatoteinu, plural), but "because of our sin" (chata'einu): because of our single sin — because of groundless hatred we were driven from our land. So the remedy for groundless hatred must indeed be: groundless love, unity not for the sake of politics... — Yalkut Margaliyot.
• • •
Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berdychiv once said this on Rosh Hashanah:
Master of the Universe! There are six hundred thousand Jewish souls, and the Torah has as many letters. If one erases[?] and separates a Jewish soul from the community, it is as if one erased a letter from the Torah, which is a grave prohibition. That is when it is one Torah joined together; but when the Torah is divided into separate books (chumashim), one may already erase... it loses the holiness of a Torah scroll. If Jews are divided, they too lose their holiness...

"And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and took bread and a bottle of water, and gave it unto Hagar" (for the first day).
The Midrash says about this: from here it follows that Abraham's household members were generous.
How does that follow?
Abraham gave Hagar bread and water, no more, because — Rashi remarks — he already then bore a hatred toward Ishmael, the "wild man". And why — one asks — did Abraham have[?] to give Hagar the bread himself? Could he not have told a member of his household to do it?
It is precisely from this that the Midrash infers that Abraham's household were generous: Abraham was afraid that they would give Ishmael all sorts of good things, so he himself gave only[?] bread and water... — Lev Yehudah.

"For now I know that thou fearest God" (for the second day).
Abraham showed such heroism and was willing to slaughter his only son for God, and yet the angel said of him: "Now I know that thou fearest God" — at this minute I know that you are pious; a minute later I no longer know... "Do not trust in yourself." — Yitav Lev.

"Only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard" (for the first day).
The Rebbe Reb Baruch of Medzhybizh said about those who shout during prayer: See the difference between a wick of wool and a wick of flax. The candle with a cheap flaxen wick sputters and crackles, whereas the candle with the better woollen wick burns quietly and modestly... — Botzina de-Nehora.

"The Lord killeth and maketh alive; the Lord maketh poor and maketh rich" (ibid.).
It is one and the same: "killeth and maketh alive" and "maketh poor and maketh rich", because a poor man is likened to a dead one... — Remazei Rokeach.

"As a calf untrained" (for the second day).
An ox — if one shouts at it[?] or it feels a stick — at once finds the straight path. A calf, however, you may beat it, and it dances and hops along all the crooked ways. So are we, the children of Ephraim... — Sha'ar Bat Rabbim.
Sugar.

[Article — economy and health; the price of sugar in Poland.] By S. Rotenberg.
For quite some time an agitation has been conducted here, with the help of colossal advertising, to increase the consumption of sugar.
— "Sugar strengthens, sugar gives strength" — such and similar slogans anyone can notice on the most varied posters in railway stations, trains, post offices; in a word, in every public place of every town and shtetl in Poland.
Never before has such a large-scale advertising campaign been conducted here as is being done for sugar.
Brochures are printed, it is advertised in the entire press; even in the smallest little papers of the most out-of-the-way provincial shtetls notices appear from time to time about the necessity of consuming as much sugar as possible.
Millions are spent for this purpose. People are lectured, statistical figures are cited, the calorie value of sugar is calculated, endorsements ("haskamot") by medical authorities are printed, confirming that sugar possesses great nutritional value and is necessary for health.
But is this the way that leads to an increase in sugar consumption?
We permit ourselves to doubt it, because it is not with the help of advertisements that sugar consumption will increase. After all, this is not some article that still has to be introduced and needs advertising. Advertising sugar and demonstrating that it is necessary for health is exactly as clever as advertising bread. It would occur to no one to agitate that people should eat bread, because that is self-evident, because it is a product that a healthy organism demands of its own accord, without advertising.
Poland, with its 76 sugar factories ("cukrownie"), takes fourth place in European sugar production, and in spite of that sugar costs more than twice as much here as in other countries.
Only here can such curiosities occur: that sugar is exported abroad by illegal means and later smuggled back into Poland and sold considerably cheaper than the normal price.
Parallel with the sugar agitation a struggle is being waged against the illegal trade in saccharine, which is smuggled in from abroad in large quantities. Rewards are even set for informing on saccharine dealers.
All this would be superfluous if sugar became cheaper, because nobody uses saccharine (except diabetics) because he likes its taste better than sugar, but simply because he is not in a position to buy sugar and is therefore forced to deceive himself at the expense of his health.
The great mass in Poland is badly impoverished, and that is the reason why the annual average consumption of sugar here amounts to 12 kilos per head, while in little Denmark it is a whole 47 kilos.
The high price of sugar also causes the poor strata to be unable to afford fruit, which we have here in great abundance and cheaply and which is of colossal importance for the nourishment of the people.
What has long been understood in Western Europe, people here unfortunately refuse to grasp. There they know how to appreciate properly the importance of sugar and fruit for health. These articles are cheap there and therefore accessible also to the poorer strata.
Here, however, people know how to import from abroad, for heavy millions, cosmetic articles, while such vitamin-rich fruits as oranges and bananas, which are called "the fruit of the future", are regarded here as a luxury.
That is why there are so many rachitic children in Poland, because they get too little sugar and vitamin-rich fruit.
The task of the government must be to reduce the price of sugar and at the same time to abolish the high duty on southern fruits. That is the only means of improving the health of the people, which here limps badly.
On one very widespread poster a woman is printed holding a child by the hand, and one reads the slogan: "Mother, do not begrudge your child sugar."
Every time I happen to look at this poster I think to myself that one more slogan is missing there, namely the cry of protest that the woman — more correctly, the millions of poor women in Poland — would have uttered: "Make sugar cheaper, and we will not need to begrudge it to our children."
One Must Not Keep Silent!

[Będzin — Jewish education; article.] A year ago, in a series of articles, we drew attention to the sad phenomenon that the leading Jewish public circles relate with such criminal indifference to the question of the Jewish upbringing and education of the thousands of children who attend the state elementary schools, where they are condemned to ignorance (am-haaratzut) and national annihilation.
Unfortunately our voice remained a voice crying in the wilderness. One must marvel and be astonished at how there is never a lack here of people, time, energy and money too when it is a matter of elections, running around, squabbles and all sorts of intrigues, and how all these necessities are lacking when it is a matter of creating truly great things, which are absolutely and urgently necessary for maintaining our national existence but demand calm, quiet, systematic and unceasing work...
But we must not reckon with the temporary indifference of our "patented" communal workers and wait with folded hands until their sleeping conscience (they probably still have such a thing) forces them one day to open wide their glued-shut eyes, in order to see what has happened in the course of the years they spent on grabbing seats and fighting over seats. Again and again the ugly wounds must be uncovered, so that people may see them and remember them, so that they will not recall them only when it is already too late and too difficult to stand up against the danger.
And the danger is truly great, horrible and terrifying. In our town alone, in Będzin, about two thousand five hundred children (among them also about 800 boys) are being educated in the state elementary schools, where they receive a careful and good education in the Polish language, Polish history and general subjects; at their disposal stand well-equipped and richly stocked children's libraries, rooms of teaching aids, etc. Only the Jewish subjects are not cultivated there. The Polish state, which maintains these schools, cannot and need not take any interest in them, when Jewish society itself takes no interest in them (it does unfortunately happen quite often that even in schools maintained directly with Jewish money these subjects are pushed aside, hidden away and neglected).
Two meagre hours a week are sacrificed there to the so-called religious instruction in the Polish language, which in the best case cannot give more than a little something. While the child receives clear and distinct knowledge of Polish culture and history, thanks to the fact that these subjects occupy the central place in the curriculum and much time and attention is devoted to them by the competent factors, he receives foggy and blurred notions of Jewish culture and the Jewish past. The trouble is often increased by the fact that many parents hand over their children, in the hours free from school lessons, into the hands of various ignorant melamdim and belfers (teachers' assistants), who are not capable of revealing to the child the beautiful and sublime in Judaism, the truly great and stirring, which awakens in the heart a warm feeling of love, pride, courage and readiness to sacrifice oneself for the people and its holy things, but only force the children into mechanical "ivri-reading" (rote reading of Hebrew), a thing which is a true torment for a child and which may awaken in him only a feeling of aversion and unwillingness and take away from him forever the desire to get to the content of this foreign and incomprehensible "ivri".
And the results of this dreadful and criminal neglect, unfortunately, our kehilla administrators are incapable of seeing and of appreciating properly. It grows pitch-dark before one's eyes and deeply sad in one's heart when one remembers them. The truth must be told: if things go on like this, we will within a short time be left here in Congress Poland in general, and in our corner in particular, entirely without readers of Hebrew literature and press... And great becomes the vexation when one considers the matter and it becomes clear that with small money means, only with great love and much self-sacrifice, one could achieve a great deal, a very great deal in this field and considerably weaken the force of the blows dealt to us by the assimilation policy that the Polish government conducts towards us with the silent consent of Jewish society.
But about the means which we are able, and also obliged, to adopt in order to weaken this danger and remove it almost entirely — in a second article.
A. Z. Borensztajn [?].
What's New in Zagłębie? — Będzin: A Cruel Deed by a Local Merchant and House-Owner

[Head of the local page; Będzin — crime, community.]
What's New in Zagłębie?
(Date boxes: Friday, 29 / 29 Elul 5691 — piątek 11 września 1931 [Friday, 11 September 1931].)
Będzin
A cruel deed by a local merchant and house-owner.
He lured a young Hasidic man to his place and beat him within an inch of his life
In the course of the week people from all strata of the local Jewish population have been turning to us and telling us about the cruel deeds of Mr. Lejtenberg and his son against Mr. Eliezer Kachan, a grandson of the author of "Tiferet Shlomo", of blessed memory.
We received various details from each of them, but we regarded the whole affair very sceptically; it was simply impossible to believe that lawlessness had already risen to such a level that among our brethren, the children of Israel, deeds were already happening of the kind we had always recorded of non-Jews. But it is, alas, a sad truth, and of the unbelievable we were finally convinced by the beaten man himself, the young Hasid Eliezer Kachan.
And here is what he relates:
"In the house of Pinchas Meir Lejtenberg lives a poor, sick widow, who lives there in the worst conditions. Her livelihood is selling herring, but the landlord wanted with all his might to evict the poor widow.
The widow turned to a number of people, and [?] to Mr. Eliezer Kachan, asking him to intervene with Mr. Lejtenberg so that the persecution against her would stop.
Mr. Kachan, together with Mr. Alter Yaakov Widman, did indeed intervene with the landlord and asked him to withdraw the lawsuit against the widow, but they achieved nothing. On the contrary, Kachan got 'a reward for his trouble' and went away 'thrashed', with nothing.
With that the first act ended.
The second act began last week: a rumour spread in town that Lejtenberg had gone bankrupt, as is 'the way of the world'. Various opinions were voiced about the bankruptcy; amid such a 'commotion' [?] stood Mr. Kachan too, who said:
'Lejtenberg ought to be taught some manners for such a malicious bankruptcy'...
The news reached Lejtenberg, who apparently became very angry about it and decided to take revenge on Eliezer Kachan.
The revenge took place in the following way:
On Thursday evening, when Kachan was sitting and studying, Lejtenberg's son came in and said with an innocent expression:
'Daddy asked that you come to him, because they want to settle things at last with the tenant (lokatorka), with the widow'...
Kachan, without the slightest suspicion that the invitation was veiled in bad intentions, closed the Gemara and went off to finish the matter he had begun in his time — to do a kindness for an unfortunate widow.
'They let me in — says Mr. Kachan — through a half-open door of Lejtenberg's shop; to my question: "Why into the shop of all places?" — the messenger answered that "everyone, the wife too, is in the shop"...
Mr. Lejtenberg led Kachan into a half-dark little room and said to him:
— "What do you think, should I stop the lawsuits against the Jewess?"
— Certainly, a very right thing; how long is the term?
But as soon as I had uttered the words — Mr. Kachan starts to weep — Lejtenberg and his son began to beat me within an inch of my life; after the cruel blows one of Lejtenberg's sons, holding a piece of iron in his hand, threatened me:
— "If you raise a cry in the street, you'll be killed"...
I carried out the "order" as required, went home and poured out my bitter heart before my wife and children.'
With that the 2nd act ended.
The third act was already 'played' in the Skierniewice shtibl before Kabbalat Shabbat. This act is already a bloody one — here knives were already at work, and the epilogue will take place in court.
For Kabbalat Shabbat Kachan's son Yechezkel went to the Skierniewice shtibl, where he wanted to make public the deed of Mr. Lejtenberg, who is also one of the Skierniewice Hasidim.
But as soon as Kachan's son stood up to pray, Lejtenberg came up to him and ordered him to leave the shtibl.
At the moment when Kachan's son said:
— "Perhaps you want to kill me too, like my father?" — he was attacked by Lejtenberg's sons, and one of them stabbed him in the head with a knife, inflicting a dangerous wound.
When the crowd saw that Kachan's son was covered in blood, an alarm was raised, upon which the police came and took both sides to the commissariat, where a report was drawn up.
The deed has aroused great indignation in town; it is an unheard-of thing that people who pass themselves off as merchants and house-owners should be capable of such brutal deeds.
The Dozors [Kehilla Board Members] for Savings.

[Będzin — kehilla.] It is a well-known matter that the situation of the local Jewish community (gmina) is a critical one. The treasury is empty, the debts grow larger from day to day, and there is no way out.
So the wise men of the kehilla began to think how to improve the situation. After long deliberations they came to an agreement that savings must be made.
The first cut was introduced in the synagogue, namely, that at Minchah and Maariv not 4 candles should be lit, as until now, but only 2...
Well, never mind — we have no right to speak out against the dozors, especially when it is a matter of reducing the deficit of the gmina; but one must surely be consistent: if savings, then why did they have to hire a cantor (ba'al tefillah) from outside for the High Holidays (Yamim Noraim) and pay him a sum of 750 zł.?
A Butcher Dunks a Ne'eman in the Slaughterhouse.

[Będzin — slaughterhouse.] In the local slaughterhouse an incident occurred last week which shows how far lawlessness has already gone.
Between the ne'eman (kashrut supervisor) Shalom Baruch Lewowicz and a certain butcher a quarrel arose because the ne'eman did not want to put his stamp on calves slaughtered elsewhere. For this the butcher grabbed Lewowicz and threw him into a large, huge cauldron of water in which the entrails of the cattle are washed...
Lewowicz was barely pulled out of that swamp alive, and it took a long time until he came to himself...
Fruit from Będzin for the Będzin Society in New York

[Będzin — Linat Holim.] Last week Mrs. Szwajcer, who is one of the most active workers in the Będzin Society (Verein) in New York, travelled back to America.
At her request photographs were taken of the old men and old women, which she took with her for the above-mentioned society.
As a token of gratitude to the society, which from time to time remembers the "Linat Holim", fruit growing in the garden of the "Linat Holim" was sent along with her.
Jewish Religious Instruction Abolished in the State Elementary Schools.

[Będzin–Sosnowiec — education.] In elementary school (folks-shul) number 8 in Będzin and in several elementary schools in Sosnowiec the teaching of Jewish religious subjects has been abolished. On account of this outrageous injustice (crying to heaven) and burning question, the gmina delegated Messrs. Wygodzki and Goldsztajn to the school inspector in Sosnowiec, who declared that the number of hours of Jewish religious instruction had been reduced in the present school year by 30 per cent, and that changing this lies within the competence of the School Board (Kuratorium) in Cracow. On Tuesday the same delegation turned to the Kuratorium in Cracow, which in turn declared that changing the matter lies in the hands of the Ministry of Education.
It is therefore a sacred duty of Jewish Zagłębie, to whom Jewish education is dear to its heart, to react as sharply as possible to this burning and painful question.
The Municipal Bath-House Is Already Operating.

[Będzin — municipality.] The municipal bath-house, which on account of renovation had not been operating for several weeks, has been open again since yesterday.
For convenience the official hours have been extended. The establishment is open until 10 in the evening.
The Magistrate Cuts the Jewish Subsidies

[Będzin — municipality.] On the basis of a circular (okólnik) from the Ministry, the temporary commissioner has once again cut the municipal budget by a sum of 70 thousand zł. Of this sum the first to be sacrificed (the kapparah) were the subsidies for Jewish schools and for the orphanage.
At the meeting of the council of commissioners Mr. Rechnic came out against this kind of action, and after a longer discussion the plan of cuts was changed as follows: for the orphanage, 3 thousand zł. less than the preliminary sum; each school, 500 zł. less; the subsidy for the chadarim unchanged.
Thursday the 17th of This Month — Tag Sale for the "Linat Holim"

[Będzin — Linat Holim.] After a pause of 3 years the "Linat Holim" society, because of its difficult situation, has also been compelled to hold a tag sale.
The tag sale was actually supposed to take place in the month of czerwiec (June); owing to various circumstances beyond its control the date was postponed, and it takes place next Thursday, the 17th of this month.
In this connection it is important to note that the "Linat Holim" also maintains the institutions: the "Moshav Zekenim" (old-age home), and an institution for poor women in childbirth. Let everyone who buys the tag take into account that the coin dropped in is a support for three living institutions.

Sosnowiec — Instead of a divorce he handed her 10 groszy..

[Sosnowiec — section head; divorce and agunah; followed by four items: eviction, vows for the free-loan fund, Prof. Messing, Revisionist conference.] Our town is boiling over the story that happened this week.
About 7 years ago Rywka Aszpic and Iszkl [?] Szyfman got acquainted here. Both professional beggars, they set up a wedding canopy according to the Law of Moses and Israel at Mandżewska [probably Modrzejowska Street] 22.
After the “honeymoon” the couple separated, and neither had any news of the other.
Last Tuesday the couple met again in Sosnowiec and after a short exchange of words came to an agreement — to divorce.
No sooner said than done: they went to the Będzin rabbinate to obtain a get. On entering the rabbinate the runaway husband asked that a get be given to his wife, whom he had finally found in Sosnowiec after 7 years.
But up there the young man's words were not taken seriously at all; they only explained to him:
— That costs 60 złoty.
The couple began to cry and shout: How can it be? We are poor, and if we don't divorce the wife will again remain a living agunah. But it did not help at all, and the decision was not changed.
— “If you don't have 60 złoty, then go and do what you like”...
On leaving the rabbinate the man said to his little wife:
— “Listen, so that you don't remain an agunah — since I don't have 60 złoty, I give you before witnesses 10 groszy; let that be instead of a get. I forgive you, and you are free according to the Law of Moses and Israel”...
—o—

Vows for the free-loan fund
Year in, year out, the vows made on being called to the Torah from Rosh Hashanah until after Sukkot are designated for the Gemilut Chesed (free-loan) fund. But one must bear in mind that the more the crisis deepens, the more urgent the institution becomes, sustaining hundreds of souls from ruin; therefore the vow campaign must not be petty in character — everyone is obliged to support the institution, which plays an enormous role at the present moment.

[Law — House-owners.] Legal instructions for house-owners.
Every landlord is obliged under the stamp law to issue without fail a receipt from a receipt book (kwitariusz) for every rent collected.
Giving a receipt not from a receipt book, as well as not giving any receipts at all for collected rent, is punishable by a fine. Such cases have already occurred in Będzin.
A receipt for rent paid serves as proof that the previous rent has already been paid.
The landlord is obliged to keep the receipt books for a full five years and to show them on every demand of officials of the Treasury (Skarb). Failure to show the receipt books for the last five years is punishable by a fine.

A Man Wanted to Poison His Own Wife

A short time ago the following sensational trial took place at the Sosnowiec District Court.
In the dock sat 28-year-old Stanisław Bachenek, who was accused of wanting to poison his wife and his 2-year-old child by pouring arsenic powder into the soup at lunch.
The defendant was defended by the Jewish advocate Dr. Kowalski, who showed that the evidence was not clear and that the wife was hysterically ill. The court took no notice of this and sentenced the accused to 15 years' imprisonment and the loss of all civil rights.
This week the case was heard at the Warsaw Court of Appeal. Advocate Kowalski again appeared for the defence, and through his pleading he succeeded in convincing the judges who had already handed down the verdict, and the defendant was fully acquitted.

Everyone Must Share the Hardship

(A word about school fees.)
The school year has already begun. People are already buying books, as far as each can afford; the teachers are already studying with the pupils with real relish — but the fathers' faces grow worried and troubled, and the question arises: where does one get the school fees from, where does one get money to pay the school.
School fees have not become cheaper in any school at all.
One might ask: why? After all, everything has become cheaper, and wages too have become cheaper everywhere. But there is a just answer to that: the number of children in the schools has fallen by at least 25 per cent, so that the schools' income has shrunk by 25 per cent, and the expenses cannot by any means be cut without it turning out to the detriment of the pupils; on the contrary, pedagogy has not stood still, there are new achievements and methods, for which new equipment must be used, and that costs a lot of money.
This is indeed the worst kind of judgment — when both sides are right. What does one do, then, when it is nearly impossible for the children's parents to pay the expensive school fees? There is one way out. The school managements must show understanding and, as far as at all possible, ease the parents' worry in paying school fees. The school managements must collect the school fees in the smallest instalments, so long as the necessary sum can be paid off over the year. The managements must be very careful about sending children home for non-payment of school fees, and must first use all other means.
In such extraordinarily hard times everyone must share the hardship.
Y. D.
How Did the Rosh Hashanah Days Pass?

The weather suited the times: cold, rainy and gloomy at heart. The houses of prayer were packed with worshippers, people prayed fervently; the crisis grows from day to day and not a ray of improvement is to be seen.
In the Będzin synagogue the cantor prayed somewhat weakly on the first day, but on the second day he "captivated"[?] the congregation.
Sermons before the blowing of the shofar were given by the rabbi, by the Musaf leader at the artisans' [synagogue], and by the newly engaged director of the "Mizrachi" school, Mr. Gotesdiner, who in fine thoughts developed the meaning of the Rosh Hashanah haftarot — and what the education of Jewish daughters looks like in the present generation.
Nowhere did it come to any "clashes" — apparently people are becoming "more serious"; only in the synagogue a small incident occurred between holders of seat rights over a "seat".
This year on Rosh Hashanah a minyan of the rabbi's own followers was organised in the rabbi's flat. On the second day the shofar-blower, also one of the rabbi's followers, went on strike and would not come for Musaf. Various interventions were of no avail: once the shofar-blower has said "nie pójdę"[?] [Polish: "I won't go"], no "power" in the world will help.
Thanks to the "strike" the minyan broke up, and the worshippers went off to the shtiblekh and to the synagogue.
— — —
In Sosnowiec too both days of Rosh Hashanah passed peacefully. In the streets a festive mood was created by the large number of Hasidim, mostly from Galicia, who had come for the holiday to the Radomsko Rebbe and strolled about freely in their Sabbath clothes.
In the town synagogue, before the blowing of the shofar, Rabbi Hager delivered a sermon rich in content, interwoven with fine sayings of the sages. The sermon also mentioned the loss of the long-serving shofar prompter Wolfson, of blessed memory, whose memory was honoured by the worshippers.
Cantor Mr. Lejchter, accompanied by a choir, prayed very beautifully.
The Whole Town Takes Up the Wrong Done to a Deceived Wife

In the town of Pilica a young man who did not live in domestic peace deceived his wife in the following way:
On the night of Rosh Hashanah, while his wife was asleep, the young fellow packed up the few things that belonged to him. When his wife, waking from sleep, asked him what he was doing, the husband answered her that there was a fire not far from their house and he was packing up the household things. Meanwhile he went out of the house with the few things and vanished.
The young wife, seeing that she had been deceived, decided to take revenge on her husband. The revenge consisted in this: the next morning she went to the synagogue where her husband was praying and gave him a "ceremonious reception". She would not leave the synagogue until her husband was removed from the synagogue by the worshippers.
The expelled man then went to the beit midrash, but from there too he was sent away, and the poor young fellow had to sit shut in at his parents'.

The Rabbi of Będzin to the Jewish Population

To the honourable inhabitants of our town, may God protect them.
Because I am not entirely well, it is hard for me this year to deliver a sermon in the synagogue on Shabbat Shuva; but my heart nevertheless streams out to you with loyalty and love, and I therefore ask you earnestly to repent. One must repent for the sins between man and God (bein adam la-Makom) — between man and the Blessed Name — and between man and his fellow (bein adam la-chavero) — between man and man. Fulfil what is written in this week's portion: „Give ear, O heavens“ etc., and „let the earth hear“ etc. The main things between man and God are the initials of SHaMaYIM (heavens): Shabbat, Ma'akhalot (foods), Yir'at shamayim (fear of Heaven), Mikva'ot (ritual baths). To keep the Sabbath, to beware of forbidden foods, to obey the rabbinical court in matters of kashrut, to have fear of Heaven, which is the foundation of the Torah and the commandments, and to safeguard the mikvaot, the purity of the family.
The main things between man and his fellow are the initials of ERETZ (earth): Achdut (unity), Rachmanut (compassion), Tzedakah (charity). All should be united, there should be no quarrels and no division between one and another; to have compassion on everyone, to put oneself in the other's situation and take him into consideration[?]. To give charity, to be helpful and to support the needy and all institutions.
I ask the town's forgiveness very much that I shall not deliver a sermon. I also ask forgiveness of the synagogue worshippers that on the coming Yom Kippur I shall not pray in the synagogue, because I am not entirely well; but I pray together with the whole town, and I hope that we shall all obtain by our prayers a good year.
I wish you a good, bright, joyful year, a final sealing for good, blessing and success, health, plenty and contentment.
As the soul of one who loves you forever.
Day 4[?] (Wednesday) of Ha'azinu, „bkh״l“[?] 5692, Będzin.
Chanoch Tzvi HaKohen Levin, head of the rabbinical court of this holy community.

Max Aronowicz

Max Aronowicz is no longer alive! How hard it is to bring these few words to one's lips before the people who lived with him, before the people who worked with him and knew him.
No, it is impossible to believe that the young, likeable Max Aronowicz has closed his eyes forever and sealed his lips for good.
To our young readers the name is unfamiliar, because it is already 12 years since the deceased left Będzin, but the older readers still remember him well. They remember his fine articles, his sharp-witted sketches and his courageous public stands, through which he more than once won himself a name among all strata of the Jewish population.
Max Aronowicz had always belonged to the left wing; he was a socialist through and through, and yet how often he gave his all for the Jewish community, how he loved everything that bore a Jewish character. He was proud when he succeeded in raising the Jewish merchant to a higher level; his face shone with joy when he saw that he was managing to uplift the artisans thanks to his lectures, for whom he sacrificed no little time and effort.
In the golden era of "Hazamir", when that institution held first place in the field of music and song, Max made his way in and began to sow seeds of culture there. Max used to say: everything that penetrates Jewish life — the whole movement, the way of life — in whatever direction it may be turned, one must see to it that it is all bound up with and polished by culture. "We must," he said more than once, "first of all have cultured people, intelligent and conscious idealists[?], and then a Jewish life with a kernel will crystallise. With [unclear word, "khashmen" — perhaps "cantors"] we will always manage, but with Zamir-tsars we will never get far."
Starting from this standpoint, a reading room was founded at "Hazamir", where[?] Jewish life began to pulse. Who does not remember the Saturday-evening "box evenings" [evenings answering questions from a question box] and lectures, in which all strata of the Jewish population took a lively part.
What problems were not discussed at the box evenings! About every newly published book people voiced their opinions there and debated. Over a topical article in the newspaper, passionate discussions often dragged on.
Besides the box evenings and literary conversations about current affairs, lectures were held every week on the loftiest problems, such as: philosophy, natural science, hygiene, medicine. People talked about art and about theatre, about gods and idols, about philosophers and poets, and everything bore such a serious character, such a profound engagement.
Who stood at the head of this engagement? Thanks to whom were the rooms of the then "Hazamir" filled with guests from the whole surrounding area? Everyone remembers that the first place was then taken by Max Aronowicz.
Although in 1905 Max was a member of the S.S. [Zionist-Socialists] and later went over to the "Bund", he could not shut himself up in the narrow frames of party-ism. The general Jewish situation interested him exceptionally, and to improve the lot of the sufferer he was capable of sacrificing himself.
He spoke of the Jewish renaissance with shining eyes. When an important Jewish book appeared he was beside himself with joy; it was a holiday in his home then.
During the editorial meetings that regularly took place with comrade Aronowicz before the war and during the war, he was more than once happy when he saw that the sky was beginning to clear and that salvation would come also to the oppressed, suffering peoples standing on the eve of their liberation. At such a moment it seemed that he grew taller with joy, and his face glowed with happiness.
— —
For the last 12 years the deceased lived in Brussels, and from then on he broke off his collaboration with our newspaper, owing to the circumstances in which he found himself. But the distance did not estrange him; on the contrary, he longed even more for his former home, for the Jewish life of old.
His frequent heartfelt letters were one long chain of laments, in which he complained of European coldness; one heard in them nothing but a strong longing for the old Jewish milieu, where the Jewish pulse beats so intensely.
His heart ached; he suffered much from having been thrown far away from Jewish life, from the Jewish book, from the Jewish press.
Now, at the open grave, it is very hard to enumerate the virtues of a person and the loss of a dear comrade. One cannot sit down with a calm conscience to enumerate the virtues and assess the loss at such a time[?], when the pain itself is only just stirring, when the grief has struck us too, together with his family.
L. Szpigelman.
