The culmination point — On the secret liquidation of the municipal Talmud Torah and the creation on its ruins of the “Ezrat Bnei Aniyim”

On the secret liquidation of the municipal Talmud Torah and the creation on its ruins of the “Ezrat Bnei Aniyim” [Aid for the Children of the Poor].
So, it seems, they have decided among themselves that everything connected with Torah must be taken into their lap, that the monopoly on Torah must be clamped into their hands at any price. The Agudah people [Agudat Israel] have settled among themselves, as it turns out, that here no one is to be let near, that Torah is entirely in their domain, and that as soon as anyone wants to do something in this field, it must not be possible to do it without their consent.
The notice about the Będzin “Talmud Torah” that was printed last Friday aroused much bitterness in town, so much so that respected householders asked at the editorial office whether it really fully matched reality, as the fact had been presented by us, and they expressed themselves in the sharpest words, saying that one must react as strongly as possible to lawlessness of this kind. What does it mean — a naive Jew asked — how may one want to destroy and disrupt a Jewish Talmud Torah, where several hundred children from the poorest strata of the population study? May one really be so selfishly disposed that, because it suits the party better that Będzin should have no Talmud Torah, one should want to wipe it out entirely and not leave a bone of it? And they, the “Torah-faithful”, those who always speak in the name of God and His beloved Name, do not dip their hand into cold water [do not lift a finger]. With such a light conscience they wanted to destroy and remove such a popular institution, which has existed for so long with its old traditions; and when others wanted to touch it, to make it into a decent institution, they shouted: away with you, sinners, from the holy institution, which for us is a relic! So they, then, may do with their holiness whatever they like? Wreck it and trample underfoot all their sacred things? Are they really permitted, systematically, consciously, with a certain order and calculation, to erase such an institution, which has existed since ancient years in every town and shtetl? Need one really give no account to anybody for such deeds? Is it already permitted to do to “the greater part of the people in number and in substance” whatever they please and whatever serves them, so that they may strengthen their party seats?
Such questions a Jew sets himself to ask, and he wants an answer to them.
And truly it was hard to understand these people. One could never have imagined that they would have the nerve to consciously break up such an institution. We used always to complain to the heads of the Talmud Torah: why do they leave the institution in such a sad state, why do they not bring it out of the deep mud into which they themselves led it? We had heard, after all, that they are afraid of the modern Jews, of the “apikorsim” [heretics], that they would turn the Talmud Torah into a school, that they would reform it — and so we said: do as you understand, do what you want, only introduce a little more order, call a general meeting — so we argued — only do something, introduce order, let it be according to your method, according to your system, but let the town know that the money is used for this purpose. But they would not hear of that either; every means was used so that people should not understand what was being said, and when Hasidic people came, who could not be suspected of introducing “heretical reforms”, it was quite a hard piece of work until they could be shown the other side of the door; but they achieved their aim, and the “dangerous elements” were removed.
Of course we could not grasp what kind of witchcraft wheel was turning here: others, who hold a certificate of kashrut, were not allowed to dip their hand into cold water, while they themselves shook off all activity. Only now does it emerge how much the leading elements were interested that the institution should breathe out its soul one by one, slowly, so that no one should even know when and how it happened.
Now that the Agudah has founded at its cheder its own Talmud Torah under the name “Ezrat Bnei Aniyim”, the blister has been pierced and the secret has come out. They tried to set up a little shop of their own, with whose merit they will go to the public for money, and the old Talmud Torah will in this way collapse. For they themselves will do nothing; on the contrary, they will do just enough for it to be destroyed; and others, of course, as always, will not be let near, so that in time the “sinners” will have nothing to take over, and they themselves will hold such a little shop in their own pocket.
And people complain that they have done nothing — only now does one see what sort of “wire-pulling” was conducted there.
Had they not intended to liquidate the Talmud Torah, firstly they would not have let everything go to ruin while others were not allowed near, and secondly they would surely not have suddenly founded an “Ezrat Bnei Aniyim” society; for we know very well how strict the money question is in the cheder “Yesodei HaTorah”, where for the sake of a few złoty no leniency [?] whatsoever is known, but the child is simply sent home, whoever it may be.
That is how great the dose of lawlessness is nowadays in the public sense. Otherwise one would surely have to bear responsibility for the deeds. Otherwise one would surely have to reckon with a whole town of people and render them an account.
Jewish money, after all, does not come so easily into the pockets that the community should exploit the individual so mercilessly. Is it any wonder, then, that people have no trust in certain types of public workers, when things come to unheard-of deeds? When people allow themselves everything in the world and need give no account to anybody? The question therefore arises: can and must such functionaries in communal affairs not be punished? Should they not be asked by society: by what right do you defile public activity and mask your deeds from the broad public? Can everything, always, remain ownerless? Must the Jewish community tolerate this? Will we get far with such masked activity, which brings so much vulgarity and disregard into all strata of the population?
Everything must surely have a limit. Every matter must surely be brought to the culmination point!
Has the culmination point not yet arrived?
R. Let.
A Little Feuilleton — Joking in the Tax Office.

[Feuilleton — taxes.] In the corridor of the tax office, by the door of the naczelnik [head of office], stands a quite sizeable "kolejka" [queue]:
One comes to get his debt split into instalments; a second tries to plead for a bit of a prolongation of a "zaliczka" [advance payment]; a third already has a slip saying that on such-and-such a day his belongings will be sold, so he hopes to cry away the decree; and so on, a fourth, a fifth, a tenth — whenever you come into the tax office you will always find the "kolejka" by the door.
And were it not for the single official sitting in the waiting room, one might imagine that we were in the Land of Israel. The whole queue consists almost entirely of the "national minority" [of] our brethren the Children of Israel, and only rarely, very rarely, does a Christian stray in, as a token.
Jews stand there for hours on end in dire troubles [lit. "chopped troubles"]. And as is the Jewish way — they crack jokes.
One tells the following story:
At an acquaintance of his they took and carried out everything that was in the flat: a sideboard, a table, chairs, everything; so they now live there like the Chinese: they sit on the ground, legs crossed under them, and sitting on the floor they eat and drink and even receive guests... So when a sequestrator came there — they saw in him their revenge: the floor, surely, he won't carry away...
A second chimes in:
An acquaintance of mine arranged things even more cleverly. He took two legs off the table and nailed it firmly with one side to the wall; instead of chairs there are special benches fastened to the floor; and from the sideboard they removed the lower panels altogether and walled it in so deep into the wall that only the little doors stick out: now they will at most have to carry away the whole room.
Meanwhile, as one stands thus in the queue and waits, in comes one single Christian, takes off his coat at leisure, announces himself to the official, and the official lets him in out of turn.
The Jews shake their heads and one of them remarks:
— If I took off my coat too, perhaps they would let me in out of turn as well.
— We Jews don't need to undress here — comes the answer at once — us Jews they stripped stark naked here long ago.
D—l.

The terrible Friday night in Wolbrom.
[Wolbrom — disaster.] We are written to from Wolbrom: last Friday night was a very terrible one for the local Jewish population.
In the middle of the night dozens of people suddenly fainted, and all the local doctors and feldshers [medical orderlies] were called out to them.
Not all of those who fainted were revived, however; 2 people, healthy by nature, died during the night.
The dead are: a brother-in-law and a sister-in-law...
The sad event has caused deep mourning here.
M. L.
The Sunny Autumn.

[Essay — reflection.] (A mood.) By Chaim Horodyc.
People are frightened at the arrival of this year's winter, which moves closer with every day and is already almost on the threshold.
A nervous mood hangs in the air and keeps people in tension and trembling. It is approaching, it is coming — a hard winter, a cold winter...
And above this restless, sickly mood, high above it, hangs a bright, laughing sun and shines with boundless gaiety and friendliness over the world.
It has been autumn for more than a month. The summer of the calendar has long since passed into history. And the sun has still remained summery and playful, only with more charm and grace: it does not burn and does not exhaust, but warms and caresses, cheers and consoles.
The sun does not always go by the calendar, and still less does it care about economic crises or psychological depressions; it is always merry and gay, bright and radiant. And it is not stingy with its riches. It pours them out over the world and penetrates wherever it can reach.
We figured out hundreds of years ago that in truth the sun never stops laughing and shining. If people are robbed of its gifts and suffer from clouds and cold, it is entirely the fault of the earth, which turns on its axis and at times blocks the sun's way to people.
And people are cursed in that they cannot imitate the sun and always laugh and be merry. When clouds cover the sun, man becomes frightened and gloomy. And even when the sun still shines in all its splendour and will not give up its positions, man too often becomes frightened and worried that any moment now the clouds will move in and a hard, cold winter will arrive...
* * *
The sunny autumn does not have in it the creative power and blossoming force of a sunny spring. Despite the light and warmth, the leaves wither and turn yellow, fall down and are trampled.
Whoever visited a little wood in this sunny autumn could see it far more clearly and better than one sees it in town.
The trees of a forest in a valley bear witness to the great change in nature. The stones and rocks remain untouched, the flowing streams carry on with their eternal work, but the trees are orphaned and their heads go bald. The withered leaves lie strewn on the paths and announce the tidings of their destruction.
And the laughing sun looks down from above and can do nothing at all to help the torn-off leaves. But it has a hopeful message of comfort for the strong trees that stand firm and hold on with their roots deep in the earth. The turning of the globe will not harm them. It will turn back with its face to the sun, and the time of blossoming will come again, and the crown will again adorn the heads of the trees.
The essential part, the substance of the thing, remains and comes back to itself; only what is on the surface disappears, the adornment of the thing. Leaves bloom, leaves wither, but a deep-rooted strong tree goes on standing patiently and waits until the spring sun returns and renews its strength to adorn it again with fresh green blossoms.
* * *
"For man is like the tree of the field," we were taught thousands of years ago.
The same laws of nature apply to people as to trees.
Leaves bloom and leaves wither, they come and they fall; there is a time of spring and a time of autumn — the strong tree stands and waits for the next spring.
The sunny autumn is a comfort to man as it is to the tree. The sun strains its last strength to warm and smile before it is hidden for a while, in order to come back afterwards with more freshness and strength. The clouds cannot rule forever, and the way to light cannot always be blocked.
Man is both happier than the tree and unhappier. Happier because he can think and reckon and come to the conclusion that after clouds comes the sun and after darkness comes light.
Unhappier because he has feelings and nerves and can become frightened even when the sun laughs and shines, consoles and caresses; man can draw his own clouds over himself.
There are strong and weak people, just as there are strong and weak trees.
The sunny autumn...
For one it is a comfort, for another a terror...
Perhaps Now Is the Right Moment?

[Polish universities — antisemitism; Jewish education.] The whole of Jewish society is now alarmed by the events taking place at the Polish universities. The antisemitic agitation against the Jewish student youth repeats itself year after year. Formerly it was said that Jews could have no access to laboratory work in the prosectorium [dissecting room] of the medical faculty, because they, the Jews, do not supply any Jewish corpses. The Jews for their part put forward the following argument against this: first, it is not the duty of the students to procure corpses for the university; second, the Jewish religion does not differ in this respect from all other religions, which are opposed to the dissection of the dead, yet for scientific purposes an exception is made everywhere; third, the government can best regulate the matter by legal means. This was also demanded by the Jewish „Koło“ [parliamentary club] in the Sejm. The government, however, is in no hurry to issue such a law.
One success the agitators have already achieved: the introduction of a numerus clausus for Jews precisely at the medical faculty. The number of Jews admitted to study medicine is minimal; the same is true of the study of dentistry and pharmacy.
Basically, even a child now understands that the tragic [printed „כראגישער“] struggle taking place at the universities is not a struggle about the dead but a struggle against the living. The point is not to admit the Jewish youth to any studies whatsoever at the university and in this way to prevent Jews from being able to practise free professions, such as being employed as lawyers, doctors, engineers, teachers etc. What is being waged here is no struggle of ideas, but a purely economic struggle.
We Jews must oppose with the utmost energy not only the barbaric methods with which the struggle is waged, but the struggle itself. In Poland we are citizens with equal rights, and as such we demand the fullest equality of rights in all fields.
But do we understand our own interest, do we understand the danger that threatens us? Do we know [printed „to know“] that we ourselves do ourselves more harm than the clubs [pałki] of the hooligan Polish youth [?] — this we do not understand; for this most of us have not grown up — not only the ordinary Jew, but even the Jewish academic youth does not understand it; and when it does understand where its greatest danger lies, it displays such indifference that it is quite impossible to understand.
What future has our Jewish academic youth that studies philosophy? Where will the whole mass of Jewish teachers find employment? Perhaps in the state schools? No, we can forget about that for the time being. Whatever regime may rule, a right-wing or a left-wing one, an antisemitic or a philosemitic one — in this they are all agreed: that Jews may not be admitted to Polish government schools or private schools as teachers and educators. There remains, then, for the whole mass of future Jewish teachers just one field: Jewish schools, created with Jewish money.
Here, however, it must be said openly once and for all that we lose the right to demand equal rights when we ourselves undermine the foundations of our own existence. We have, for example, elementary schools for Jewish children in which there are no lessons on the Sabbath, only on Sunday. In such a school a Jewish teacher must as a matter of course be employed. But what do our „moshkes“ [assimilated Jews — a mocking term] do? They send their children precisely to non-Jewish elementary schools. In response the school inspector appoints non-Jewish teachers in Jewish schools. When we protest against this, he answers that the Jews do not want a Jewish school at all — the best proof, after all, is that in Sosnowiec they send their children en masse to non-Jewish schools.
We have no answer to that; it is indeed true, and it was precisely certified [„patented“] Zionists who were the first to send their children on the Sabbath to the gentile schools. They did not understand that they were committing not only a national crime, but were undermining the existence of the Jewish teacher. We have no answer when the Kuratorium [school-district board] points out to us that in fact the Jewish secondary schools have no right to exist. In Zagłębie, for example, where there are two Jewish secondary schools, we find up to one third Jewish pupils in non-Jewish secondary schools. Not, God forbid, in the government schools, of course, in which there is often not one single Jewish pupil.
The Polish school youth in Zagłębie, too, took clubs [?] in hand and wanted to drive Jewish pupils out of the Polish schools, but here we can be quite sure that no danger threatens us. Jewish pupils are not needed in the government schools, Jewish students are not needed at the university, but in private Polish secondary schools, where they form the material basis of the school, where for their own money one may spit in their faces, where without them the school could not exist — why should anyone want to be rid of them?
Perhaps now is the right moment for Jewish parents to understand that the same „pałkarze“ [club-wielders] who beat Jewish students at the university are preparing to educate their children; the present educators, too, did not do badly with the club as students. The Jewish acad[emic] youth must also understand that the club is not so dangerous for them as our home-grown „moshkes“: tempers at the universities will calm down, but our „moshkes“ will go on letting themselves be spat in the face for their own money. What then is the use of a Jewish student finishing his studies, when in any case he can do nothing with his diploma [„patent“]? X
Back to the Middle Ages (On the Latest Antisemitic Outbreaks)

[Poland — antisemitism; universities; opinion.] S. Rotenberg.
Like an ever-active volcano, in whose subterranean depths a fiery mass boils and seethes incessantly, and about which one can never be sure whether it will not suddenly begin to spew fiery lava and destroy everything around it that lives and blooms — so it is with the antisemitic disturbances: they, too, are prepared in a conspiratorial-treacherous manner and break out like a plague, like a black death, wreaking devastation in society. But what makes the hooligan excesses more dangerous than a volcanic eruption is the fact that to this day no seismograph has yet been invented that would react to antisemitic disturbances and make it possible to guard oneself against them.
It began in Kraków, then in Warsaw, Wilno, Lwów, and lately also in a whole series of towns and townlets antisemitic students and pupils have attacked their Jewish colleagues and beaten them until they bled, because of the unheard-of "Jewish chutzpah" of wanting to enjoy the light that the "Alma Mater" spreads.
Put out the electric lamps, remove for a while the latest technical achievements, and you will get a picture of the dark Middle Ages in every detail. Just as then the street boys and guild journeymen attacked, whenever they felt like it, the helpless, defenceless Jewish mass — so it is today too. Defenceless people are beaten and killed without a why and a wherefore [?], because of the one single "crime" expressed in the thirst of the Jewish youth for learning: an old, inborn, specifically Jewish "disease" which they will never be able to cure even with such "radical" remedies as pogroms.
Just as in the Middle Ages the black monks, with glazed eyes and a false prayer on their lips, called on the mob in the name of God to settle accounts with the "accursed", so today the antisemitic leaders call their youth into the churches, arrange "prayers" and call, in the name of the "pale Jew of Nazareth" who taught that if someone strikes you on the right cheek you should offer your left — to make pogroms on Jews.
Can the scientific and technical achievements our century boasts of serve as a sign of culture? By no means; otherwise such phenomena as brutal attacks on defenceless women and the throwing of infants out of their prams, as was the case in the Saxon Garden in Warsaw, would surely not have been possible in the age of radio and television.
What can one call such wild delusional deeds of the "noble" antisemitic "knights", who are supposed to be the guides, the future leaders of a people, if not barbaric vandalism? If in the very heart of Europe facts can occur nowadays that differ in no way from the deeds of the wild Huns and Vandals, then all the boasting of culture and civilisation is nothing more than make-up with which those people prettify their bestial faces — those who, after a bloody bit of work, come back into the university hall to hear lectures in jurisprudence, whose task is to train people who should stand on guard and protect society from injustices and hence from hooligan attacks by one part of society on the other.
"Brilliant" are the prospects of the Jewish student youth for the future.
What have we gained from the ghetto walls having been thrown down, if in fact they go on existing, with the difference that today they enclose the non-Jewish street and make it impossible for us to get in there?
Can a Jewish intellectual with a diploma, however able he may be, penetrate the ghetto walls that surround the state and municipal institutions? No! One can perhaps point to individual cases, but — exceptions confirm the rule — that is an old axiom.
And because of the "fantastic happiness" awaiting the Jewish youth in the future, they are not allowed to study. They are begrudged even "Torah for its own sake", because only lucky individuals will succeed in making of it "a spade to dig with". Various factors already take care of that. To protect themselves against Jewish competition, the antisemitic academics need not even resort to bloodshed; that is being done anyway by others, in a "humanitarian" way, in white gloves.
Are we going back to the Middle Ages? Possibly yes, who can tell; there are very many signs of it.
Just as in the life of an individual there is youth, middle age and old age, so it is with culture. It is quite possible that European culture has already reached its highest point and that it will go back and fall into a medieval sleep, and centuries will pass in darkness until new shoots of culture blossom again — not of some counterfeit pseudo-culture, but of a civilisation that will create the new society, where racial antagonisms will vanish, where social differences will be erased: a society in which we too, who were the first to infect the world with the microbe of freedom, will be able to take part as equals among equals and will strengthen the foundations of: light, freedom and labour.
Mother and Wife (A Gripping Novel of Jewish Life)

[Serial novel — fiction; final instalment.] S. Relkes [?].
My love for the young man grew stronger from day to day, all the words of love that I had read in the novels, where the happy and romantic meetings between a young couple in love in the forest are so beautifully described. The trees rustle, the water's waves whisper secrets [?] and murmur, and all of nature rejoices in their happiness.
David's mother heaves a heavy sigh and goes on telling:
I believed in him too much, I gave myself to him completely. I was his. Between heaven and earth he swore to me eternal and faithful love, and happy I felt in his strong arms.
But it did not last long before the shadow of happiness vanished, and I found [?] myself deceived, seduced, and in my heart a terrible secret lay hidden...
When the child was born later, only then did I feel my heavy misfortune. The child's father had disappeared, I did not know where he was, and wanting to save myself from what I had committed with such light-mindedness, and not wanting to bring disgrace and shame upon my grandfather, I carried the child away to a Christian nurse who lived not far from our shtetl, and the Christian woman, taking pity on my suffering, took the child in.
But in the shtetl a rumour spread that my grandfather, Reb Chaim, in order to cover every trace of his granddaughter's disgrace, had murdered the child.
On the strength of the rumours my grandfather was arrested by gendarmes, who put him in prison before Kol Nidre, from where he was released only at the end of Yom Kippur.
The illegitimate child the grandfather took into his home, where she did all the housework.
Years passed; the girl grew up as pretty as a picture. But the stain that [?] had lain on her from her birth remained all the same, and the inhabitants of the shtetl treated her with mockery and laughter.
This situation too came to an end: a rich uncle from America took the girl over there to himself and betrothed her to a nephew of his [?].
The young couple lived happily. Rachele was not only a beautiful woman but also a good housewife, and when her husband learnt that she was going to be a mother, his happiness was past belief.
But the happiness did not last long: the husband fell into a grave illness, which caused very much suffering to the family, and worse still was when cruel death destroyed the couple's nest.
A few months later I gave birth to a son, who indeed received his father's name.
"What name did the father have?" David asks his mother.
The mother turns pale, tears choke her, but at the moment when she has the possibility of telling the terrible secret she has been carrying for 22 years already, she controlled herself and cried out:
"David was the name of the father of my newborn son..."
"Mama!" With this word David fell upon his mother's neck and both burst into tears.
Sarahle too wept with them, because she understood that with her story David's mother had only meant to convince her son that he should not treat her — Sarahle, that is — the way Rachele's seducer had...
(The End).
R. Israel Moshe Weinreb

[Sosnowiec — obituary.] Moshe Feinkind.
(A few words over his open grave).
In memory of my dear friend.

That such an upright Zionist of the old guard as R. Israel Moshe Weinreb was would take leave of the world so quickly — that I did not expect, and perhaps no one around him expected it either.
With him one of the best sons has been torn from our loyal ranks, one of the most loyal active fighters for the holy idea of the revival of the people and the revival of the Land.
Whoever ever had the opportunity to work together with the great departed in the Zionist field must, willy-nilly, admit that like a "soldier on watch" he always stood ready to prove by deeds his loyalty and his devotion in serving Jewish interests in general and Zionism in particular.
Beyond his strength he sacrificed a great deal of money for Zionist purposes; beyond his strength he worked for the good of his people — something so deeply ingrained in his heart.
Sparing neither himself nor anyone else, R. Israel Moshe strove with all the impetus of his life to rebuild the old homeland of the Jewish people wandering in exile, and he gave his children, his only son, a religious and national education, leading them on the path he himself had walked.
R. Israel Moshe Weinreb (misprinted "Teinreb") could be seen at the Zionist congresses held in Basel, The Hague, Hamburg etc. as delegate of the Zionists of Sosnowiec, where together with the late Weinberg and others he founded the Zionist association.
At the so historic Sixth Congress R. Israel Moshe Weinreb created the so-called Polish "Landsmanschaft", consisting of almost all the delegates of the Piotrków Governorate; this Landsmanschaft remained loyal to Dr. Herzl and did not join the opposition, which was then led against him by the so-called "Kharkovites" on the so stirring Uganda question.
And when in 1907, under hard conditions because of the "state of war" prevailing in Poland owing to the general revolutionary movement, an illegal gathering of Zionists took place in Piotrków, there too one sees the veteran Zionist "merchant" [sic; perhaps "seeker"] R. Israel Moshe Weinreb at that gathering as delegate of the Sosnowiec Zionists.
And disregarding the danger that then threatened all those present, he took part like a true soldier in the deliberations to the very end.
At that conference a governorate committee was created to animate and direct Zionist activity in the towns, and also the elections to the Duma.
And R. Israel Moshe Weinreb was elected a member of the committee.
In the year 1908 a Zionist rally of Upper Silesia took place in Katowice, at which it was decided, on the initiative of the writer of these lines, to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the "Hovevei Zion" conference in Katowice, and one of the organisers of that jubilee was indeed none other than the ever-energetic and self-sacrificing R. Israel Moshe Weinreb of blessed memory.
He interceded with the border authorities to obtain one-day free passes to Katowice for the Polish delegates, etc.
There was not a single Zionist institution in which the departed did not take part, both with money and in person.
One of the best Jewish representatives, a maskil [printed "mashpil"] of the old cut and a warm Jewish Zionist — this Sosnowiec has lost, and with it the Zionist ranks, which grow thinner every day of those heroes of the old loyal guard, among whom was also R. Israel Moshe Weinreb.
May the earth rest lightly on him, and may he dwell in the shadow of the Almighty.
The first clothing ceremony of the "Malbish Arumim" in Dąbrowa

[Dąbrowa — charity.] Last Sunday, thanks to the tireless work of several persons in Dąbrowa, some 50 poor Jewish children were clothed.
The humanitarian activity was carried out precisely at a time of terrible despair. A severe economic crisis among the Jewish masses — but the power of Jewish will, of Jewish compassion, did not wear out the board of the still very young society "Malbish Arumim" ("Clothing the Naked"), and beyond their means they managed to carry out the first act of their tasks.
The celebration had the character of a popular festivity. Young and old, men and women, got ready to take part in whatever way possible in the great mitzvah of clothing poor children.
The hall of the Dąbrowa Artisans' Association was packed full with men, women and children; the guests of honour too — the children who had received clothing — were not excused, because "it is their celebration, so they should be here"...
The first clothing was also "combined" with the official inauguration of the society itself. It will soon be a year since the society was founded and the official opening had not yet taken place; the board held back the celebration for a favourable occasion, and indeed lived to see that in Dąbrowa 50 children could be clothed from head to foot — and that is truly no small holiday...
The president, S. Zając, declares the celebration open and honours Mr. G. A. Gutman with cutting the ribbon.
The Sosnowiec cantor Mr. Leichter with his singing of "Ma Tovu", and he recites a memorial prayer (hazkarah) for Zelig Gutman, may he rest in peace.
Then the local rabbi, may he live long, speaks on the topic of the day, pointing out the important significance of clothing poor Talmud Torah boys, and he wishes the society further success.
Present in the hall by chance is the editor of the journal "Unzer Kultur" ("Our Culture"), Mr. Y. D. Weiss, who is given the floor. Mr. Weiss delivers a short but objectively constructed lecture, in which he shows the unfavourable situation of a person when he is naked — not only the body but also the soul...
Also speaking are Messrs. Lichtig, Cukrowski and the secretary, who gives the following report:
No monthly pledge has been collected from anyone to this day. The income over 10 months, amounting to about 1300 zł, was collected through one-time donations from various persons. This sum already includes the 300 zł from Mr. G. A. Gutman; from Mr. Israel Mordechai Złotnik 100 zł, from Mr. Yosil Kleiner 50 zł, the Women's Association 25 zł, and others.
The board, which works intensively, consists of Messrs. Shmuel Simcha Zając (president), Mendil Balicki (vice-president), Yitzchak Hirsch Rotsztajn (treasurer), Yitzchak Krauz (secretary), Isser Cukrowski (administrator), Wolf Finer, Meir Szpigelman, Parnas Eber [?] Kalisz, Israel Mordechai Złotnik, Aharon Lemkowicz and Hirschel Rybsztajn.
The society has also introduced a "Golden Book" in which the names of larger donors are recorded. On the spot several persons pledged a sum of 100 zł.
The cantor sings several numbers, and with the singing of the Polish and the Jewish anthems the celebration is closed.
Afterwards the board and the invited guests went to the apartment of Mr. Meir Szpigelman, where the so-called "banquet" took place.
The guests made do with little glasses of brandy and wished one another that at the second clothing things would be improved...
The "banquet" was concluded on a spiritual note, with a "Mekimi me-afar dal", beautifully performed by the cantor Mr. Leichter and his choir.

A lesson for adults.

An Old Bachelor Against the New Marriage Law.

Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion (Vayetzei)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Vayetzei
The Portion
—o—
a) "And Jacob went out from Beersheba" (Gen. 28:10)
"Rabbi Berechiah says: from the well of blessing." Midrash.
The seventh blessing with which Isaac blessed Jacob is: "Be lord over thy brother" [printed "chit"]. The seventh, that is, the most significant blessing. And when Esau too came to ask Isaac for blessings, he answered him: if Jacob is already going to be your lord, what good are the blessings to you? Everything you acquire will after all belong to him, the lord... "What a slave acquires, his master acquires." That is why Jacob fled from Hebron — because of the "Be'er Sheva" [pun: sheva = seven], the seventh blessing — so that Esau should not be able to claim regret over the blessing "Be lord over thy brother". Pnei Aryeh Zuta.
—o—
b) "And behold a ladder... ascending and descending on it" (Gen. 28:12)
"Sulam" (ladder) equals in gematria "mamon" (money) and "oni" (poverty). This ladder was shown to Jacob — a ladder on which those going up and those going down change places without cease, up and down... Baal ha-Turim.
—o—
c) "And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth" (Gen. 28:13 [as printed; the verse is 28:14])
1.
Everyone treads upon the earth, but all are buried in it and it covers them — these are the Jews... Tzror ha-Mor.
2.
Everyone treads upon the earth — but all live only from what the earth brings forth out of itself... — these are the Jews... Sefer ha-Brit.
—o—
d) "This is none other but the house of God" (Gen. 28:17)
The author of "Ha-Pardes" once came to a town. Coming into the beit midrash, he saw how rotten and dirty it was, the walls full of mould, the roof full of holes — in the Jewish manner. So he said to the householders: when our father Jacob saw "how dreadful is this place", how frightening and dangerous the place was, he understood that "this is none other but the house of God" — that it could be nothing else but, most probably, a synagogue or a beit midrash... Sha'ar Bat Rabim.
—o—
e) "It is better that I give her to thee than that I should give her to another man" (Gen. 29:19)
Laban knew that Rachel was a righteous woman, and if she married a sinful man she would make him pious. Likewise Jacob: if he married a wicked woman he would make her pious. So Laban thought to himself: it is better that the two of them marry each other, rather than that the pious should multiply in the world... Nifla'ot Hadashot.
—o—
f) "And the Lord saw that Leah was hated, and He opened her womb" (ibid., 31)
In a little town the authorities once appointed three parnassim [community heads]. Now a certain householder had a particular longing to be a parnas too, so he went off to the voivode to obtain a parnas's seat for himself. In the meantime it happened that a libel was concocted in the town and the parnassim were arrested as "zakladnikes" [Polish zakładnicy — hostages]. And when our householder brought the town authorities the voivode's order that he was appointed parnas in someone else's place, they promptly locked him up in jail and promptly released that ex-parnas...
The moral:
It was decreed by Providence that the matriarchs should be childless. The lot would have fallen on Leah, because she was Jacob's first wife; but since Jacob loved Rachel and made her the mistress of the house, the lot fell on her to be barren... Ohel Yaakov.
—o—
g) "And Jacob laid the rods" (Gen. 30:41)
"Whensoever the stronger cattle did conceive" — when the Jews ("Israel is a scattered sheep") get heated and rebel against one another, "Jacob laid the rods": Jacob pointed symbolically to the rods that will then be lashing down on Jewish heads. But "when the cattle were feeble" — when unity reigns among Jews — "he put them not in": the rods will have nothing to do. Olelot Efraim.
—o—
h) "Jacob hath taken away all that was our father's" (Gen. 31:1)
"Of all that was our father's" — from the very cunning and deceit that Laban possesses Jacob learned, and "hath he gotten all this glory", and he tricked Laban himself out of the property... Binah le-Itim.
—o—
"Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom" (Job 21 [as printed; the verse is Job 28:28])
To be crafty, a sharp operator, is actually easy: one can swindle, bluff and the like. But to be God-fearing and wise into the bargain, to act cleverly and shrewdly and honestly at the same time — that is already an art... Zecher Tzaddik.
—o—
i) "In that he told him not that he fled" (Gen. 31:20)
Jacob was preparing to flee from Laban. But he knew that Laban was a "sharp fellow" and would sniff it out, so he outsmarted him even more and kept saying all the time that he was running away. "Al bli" — for nothing — "he told him that he fled": he said that he was running away. Consequently Laban was no longer on his guard when he really did run away... Milin Yakirin.
—o—
j) "Wherefore didst thou flee secretly" (ibid., 27)
At Laban's, Jacob behaved like Laban's own kind — like a deceiver. Only now did Laban find out that Jacob was a tzaddik. So he argued with him: "Wherefore didst thou hide?" — why did you disguise yourself? Had I recognised that you are a tzaddik, "I might have sent thee away with mirth and with songs, with tabret and with harp" — I would have sent you off with drums and dances... Kedushat Levi.
—o—
The Haftarah
k) "Return, O Israel" (Hosea 14:2)
A law (Bava Metzia 29b): "If one finds books, he reads in them once in thirty days; and if he does not know how to read, he rolls them." —
Clearly: a book must be read, or at least leafed through. Otherwise it goes mouldy.
We have in the ark — the earth — the Book of Life, the book of our life. So one really must leaf through it often, air it out[?] and read it... Drashot El Ami.
—o—
l) "The ways of the Lord are right, and the just shall walk in them, but the transgressors shall stumble therein" (ibid., 10)
The wicked also perform mitzvot. The difference is only that "the just walk in them" — for the righteous the good is a matter of life, while "the wicked stumble in them" — the wicked sometimes come to grief even over a mitzvah... Petach ha-Sha'ar.
—o—
Rabbi Yechezkel Landau wrote in "Noda bi-Yehuda" a responsum against the Hasidim for their recitation of the "Le-shem Yichud". He ends the responsum with the words: "The righteous shall walk in them, and the Hasidim shall stumble therein."
When printing a second edition of "Noda bi-Yehuda", the printer, out of fear of the Hasidim, rewrote the verse as it stands in Hosea: "and the transgressors shall stumble therein."
Rabbi Shmuel Landau said to him: my father made out of (the word) "transgressors" — Hasidim, and you make out of (the word) Hasidim — "transgressors"...
—o—
To the query from Mr. Hirsch Niebielski [?] concerning the Baal ha-Turim on Chayei Sarah: "And he dwelt in the land of the South, and next to it: and Isaac went out to meditate in the field — an allusion to what they said: whoever wishes to become wise should go south", Mr. A. B. (Sosnowiec) replies that the Baal ha-Turim is clear enough: Isaac instituted the evening prayer (for which one surely needs supreme understanding, a higher wisdom) after arriving in the South. Hence[?] it follows that wisdom reigns in the South. Words of this kind are found plentifully in the Baal ha-Turim.
Why Has Yiddish Been Forgotten?

We have already mentioned that the present population census [„folks-tseylung“; the 1931 Polish census] has a political background. We have also hinted that in this policy what was meant first of all were the territorial minorities, and least of all was the Jewish non-territorial minority meant, which has no aspirations whatsoever that could be dangerous to the state.
But now it looks as though we Jews had been so little in mind that we were simply forgotten altogether. For the territorial minorities the census nevertheless provided the convenience of proper self-determination in their own language, while for the Jews, who in the state sense are quieter than water and lower than grass, such conditions were created as will hamper their self-determination and take away the possibility of giving the correct information.
No, this does not come from forgetting. It is the conspicuous tendency of assimilation that makes itself felt in various deeds of the Sanacja camp towards Jews. It is an explicit disregard of the language spoken by almost all the 3 million Jews in Poland, a large part of whom cannot make themselves well understood in any other language.
It is an unjust ignoring of the natural rights of the Jews.
But...
How has it happened that only now, at the eleventh hour [lit. „an hour before the call to synagogue“], do we come out with this complaint? And why did Wilno alone have to come out with a memorandum of protest, with the demand for a Jewish column in the forms? Why did our political representatives not make timely representations in the proper offices about correcting the error, and if their intervention had not helped, why did they not go out to the public with an alarm about it? Why has the Jewish public until now not even had an inkling of the whole matter?
Much ink was spilled over the omission of the column „nationality“; a formal protest about it was even lodged in the Sejm, so as to sing along in unison with all the other minorities. But about this wrong [?], which concerns Jews alone, the Jewish representatives kept a mouth full of water.
But the public must not pass over it in silence; we must with all our energy, even now, correct the error — introduce the Jewish column!
In any case, however, Jewish young people must place themselves en masse at the disposal of the authorities for the census, so as to have at least the certainty that orally one will be able to communicate with Jews in Yiddish.
It is a historic moment of the greatest importance, which must not be neglected.
P. K.
Synagogue Architecture.

By Moshe Poltrak.
Among all peoples and races one can study the development of architecture in connection with their historical fate. The periods of development or decline of architecture are thoroughly bound up with the development and decline of their national existence. Among the Jews, by contrast, the development of architecture is absolutely not bound up with their historical destiny. The Jews lack the foundations which among other peoples are the starting point for an evolution of architectural form — foundations that flow from the spirit and the intuition of the given people. Independently of this, however, we see how the Jews build steadily, and with a special piety, at all times (both in the days of the Temple and after the Destruction, in exile) synagogues, in which they express their reverence for the God of their fathers. And the architecture of these synagogues is interesting, for the creations of the human soul always remain a measure of its spiritual development and cultural level.
When we wish to treat our architecture (especially the synagogal one), we must regretfully state that it is not a reflection of our national soul but rather an exact picture of our peculiar situation among the nations of the world. We have never had a style of our own. Even the First Temple, so famous for its beauty, is not a Jewish creation, for it was designed and built by Phoenician architects. And when the Jewish communities later began to build synagogues in exile, they borrowed the forms of the local inhabitants. Of more significant buildings there is no question at all, because the medieval Jew, out of eternal fear for his tomorrow, did not have the courage to build such. These are the factors that partly explain to us why there is almost no trace of a Jewish architecture from post-Talmudic times. The excavations of ancient Jewish synagogues, on the other hand, carried out in Eretz Israel and its surroundings, bear witness to a strong influence of the late Roman-Greek style which was then used by the Romans in their buildings.
But it also happened in the course of Jewish wandering that the people lived together with the settled peoples, as for example with the Arabs and Moors in Spain. From the beginning of the Middle Ages until the discovery of America we find in architecture the influence of the Moorish-Arab style. This style suited the Jews and Arabs, who have similar religious-architectural restrictions; therefore they willingly used it. Thus there arose at that time the synagogue in Toledo, now the church El Transito, with a splendid hall of columns with Moorish-Arab arches [?]; the synagogue in Córdoba, built by the then well-known Jewish architect Yitzhak Mehab ibn Efraim; and the churches Santa Marja la Blanca in Toledo and the most beautiful church in Seville, Sant Bartolome, were built as synagogues.
In the Spanish-Jewish period (if one may call it so) there is indeed created the typically Jewish form of synagogue architecture which the Jews, like their language, took with them into the world after the expulsion from Spain. In all the countries of the Mediterranean where a Jewish foot was set, the so-called Spanish Jews built synagogues in the Moorish-Spanish form (one must distinguish the word form from style); to this day remnants of that time have survived. These are, in the north, the synagogues in Amsterdam and Rotterdam, as well as the Spanish synagogue in London; in the south, the synagogues in Livorno, Venice, Padua, Salonika and Smyrna. Among the most magnificent synagogues, however, are counted the synagogues in Aleppo and Damascus. For the most part the buildings are not made to a pattern [„shpalon-mesig“, i.e. to a stencil], but each of them has its own specific architecture. Inside they are decorated with marble tiles laid out in interesting ornaments. Very often we find whole walls of marble covered with verses from the Tanakh. In the middle of the synagogue stood an almemar [bimah], and around the walls chairs were set.
Special attention was given to the ritual objects, such as the menorah, kiddush cups and the eternal light.
The development of architecture went by other ways than with the Spanish Jews among the Jews who lived north of the Alps. This was caused by the Christian peoples among whom they settled in the ghetto. These Jews (the Ashkenazim) built the first ghetto synagogues. In the endlessly narrow little streets of the ghetto the Jews have to build their synagogues; because of this they cannot express themselves outwardly in architecture, all the more so as they fear the hostilely disposed Christian surroundings.
(To be concluded).
What's New in Zagłębie? — Będzin: Friday Is to Be the Second Market Day of the Week

[Head of the local page; Będzin — municipality, market days.]
What's New in Zagłębie?
(Date boxes: Friday, 10 Kislev 5692 — piątek 20 listopada 1931 [Friday, 20 November 1931].)
Będzin
Friday is to be the second market day of the week
Meeting of the Commissarial Council.
On Monday a meeting of the Commissarial Council took place under the chairmanship of Commissioner Mr. Rzeczkowski[?]. Among other things it also considered the question, raised in its time by the Merchants' Association, that 2 days in the week, Monday and Wednesday, should be the market days.
The starosta rejected the Monday date, on the grounds that on Mondays fairs take place in the neighbouring towns, and the question was referred to the Magistrat.
After a lengthy discussion it was decided that the second market day should be on Friday.
The meeting also dealt with the request of the bus owners concerning the designation of a bus station for them.
The matter was settled in this way: the buses running to Grodziec ("Groytse") and "Haikovits"[?] (probably Wojkowice) will have their station on Gzichowska Street, and (sic) the buses running to Czeladź — on Browarna Street.
A lengthy discussion was provoked by the proposal of Mr. Rzeczkowski that the auditing of the expenditures and revenues of the budgets for 1929 and '30 be entrusted to the inspector Mr. Janiczek, and that two aldermen (Ratmänner, ławnicy) be attached to him, who should serve only as observers..
It goes without saying that the proposal, which degrades the authority of the aldermen, aroused dissatisfaction, and after much debate the matter was postponed to the next meeting.
No Lessons at All Were Held in the Talmud Torah This Week, and the "Agudah" Is Creating a New "Torah Shop"..

[Będzin — education, Talmud Torah; Agudat Israel.]
As we have already reported, the situation in the local Talmud Torah is catastrophic. It has already gone so far that since Sunday the melamdim (teachers) have been on strike, and the hundreds of poor children are wandering about the streets.
It goes without saying that in such a situation an alarm should have been raised to the Jewish population by that "foe" [misprint for "side"], which proclaims at every step (and even more so at election time...) that they are the guardians of Torah and faith; they ought to have taken upon themselves the initiative that the neglect of Torah study of the children of the poor be ended as soon as possible. But we see quite the opposite: the "Shomrei-Torah-niks" are content that the Talmud Torah is being utterly ruined, so that the existence of their new "kreml" (little shop), named "Ezrat Yesodei Torah", should be secured... Instead of starting a campaign in the town for the Talmud Torah, they are agitating in the shtiblekh (Hasidic prayer houses) that everyone should pledge himself to the newly founded society "Ezrat Yesodei Torah".
The holy campaign is conducted precisely on the Sabbath. The agitators (active in this field are mostly the "patented" pentakes[?], the "editors" of the "Vayakhel-Pekudei") come into the shtiblekh, where they deliver sermons about "Ezrat Yesodei Torah"; the agitators are already provided with pledge slips filled out with the names of those who pray in that shtibl.
As we are told, the campaign is meeting strong resistance from the Hasidic public, which understands the intention of the "Agudah": that with their new shop they mean to harm the "Talmud Torah".
When the President Does Not Want...

[Będzin — Kehilla.]
At Tuesday's meeting of the kehilla board, board member (dozór) Liwer lodged a protest against the kehilla president, who disregards the wish of some of the members that the meetings be held on Sunday, but instead convenes the meetings at such times when some of the members are unable to come.
The president thought to himself, "What does Kraków care if Warsaw is angry?" — and the protest remained on paper.
The same fate befell the request of the local Jewish academics to the kehilla board that a protest be expressed in the name of the Jewish community against the anti-Jewish excesses.
— "If I want it so"...
First Entertainment Evening at the "WIZO".

[Będzin — women's organisations, WIZO.]
In the own premises of the local women's association "WIZO" the first entertainment evening took place last Tuesday. As usual, the programme began late, and it is no novelty that men are not punctual...
Also taking part in the evening was Mrs. Dr. Moszkowska of Kraków, who, after the greeting by Mrs. Ratner, delivered a lecture devoted to the upbringing of children. The lecturer shed light in a very interesting way on the psychological aspects of the child and its needs.
After the lecture the members spent time over a glass of tea. On the whole the first evening was a success.
Extraordinary General Meeting of "Hakoach".

[Będzin — sport, Hakoach; the Maccabiah.]
Because the board has tendered its resignation, an extraordinary general meeting will take place this Sabbath.
At the same time, the attention of the tourists who intend to take part in the Maccabiah, which takes place at the end of March in Eretz Israel, is drawn to the fact that they must register at Hakoach, where they will receive the appropriate information.
From the Będzin “Gordonia”

[Będzin — youth and Zionism.] At the last meeting of the “Gdud Magshimim” of the Będzin pioneering youth organisation “Gordonia”, the bloody antisemitic excesses in the university cities, as well as in Zagłębie, were discussed. Feelings of solidarity were expressed with the Jewish academics who suffered, while it was resolved at the same time that the Jewish youth will not let itself be insulted and beaten and will defend Jewish honour with dignity.
— This week a collective talk took place in “Gordonia”: “The problem of Jewish labour”, in connection with the latest clash between the Jewish workers and the colonists in the village [moshava] of Hadera.
— Tomorrow afternoon the first session just held of the General Federation of Labour in Eretz Israel will be discussed.
General Meeting of “He-Halutz”

[Będzin — Zionism.] On Saturday the general meeting of the Będzin “He-Halutz” took place under the chairmanship of Mr. T. Kokotek; over 100 members came to it. Reports on the activity were given by Messrs. Majerowicz, Frenkel and Miss Rotenberg. Taking part in the discussion were Messrs. R. Liwer, L. Kokotek, Anzelewicz, Szapira, Rus, Bojm and others.

“Rabbi Yehuda Halevi as a National Poet”

[Będzin — lectures.] This evening, at the close of the holy Sabbath, a lecture on the above-mentioned subject will be given at the “Mizrachi” premises by Dr. Avraham Natesdiner[?]. The lecture is a continuation of the series “Jewish Philosophy in the Middle Ages”. The subject of the lecture promises to be very interesting.
Small Traders Against the New Amendment to the Turnover Tax

[Będzin — economy and taxes.] The board of the Small Traders' Association together with all sections held a meeting at which the new amendment to the turnover tax was dealt with, which provides no relief whatsoever for the small trader. Mr. Gutensztajn reported on the question, pointing out that relief of one and a half percent of turnover will be received only by the merchants who keep bookkeeping ledgers. It was therefore resolved to send a resolution to the President of the Council of Ministers, to the Marshal of the Sejm and to the Minister of Finance, that the turnover-tax relief should also apply to the small traders, who are threatened with complete ruin.
At the meeting further questions concerning the improvement of the sad situation of the Jewish small traders were also discussed.
Messrs. Kugelman, Zawader and Hejda were delegated as representatives of the association to the committee for the support of the unemployed.
Sosnowiec — Meeting of the Kehilla Board

[Sosnowiec — community.] On Sunday the kehilla board held a meeting at which the further items of the new kehilla budget were discussed. It was also resolved to buy a plot of ground around the cemetery.
Resolution to Restructure the “Bank Kupiecki”

[Sosnowiec — economy.] Under the chairmanship of Mr. Lejzerowicz an extraordinary meeting took place on Sunday at the “Hotel Polski”, called by the commission for the restructuring of the “Bank Kupiecki” [Merchants' Bank].
On the agenda was: liquidation or continued existence. The auditor Mr. Szaszkes reported comprehensively on the question and appealed to the members to help restructure and rebuild the “Bank Kupiecki”.
After a lengthy discussion it was resolved to endeavour to revive the bank; for this purpose a commission was elected.
Customs Official Sentenced to Two Years in Prison

[Sosnowiec — courts.] In the month of sierpień [August] 1930 the investigation office in Sosnowiec received confidential information that abuses were being committed in the local customs office to the detriment of the State Treasury. On this basis an audit was carried out, which yielded surprising results. It turned out that the officials Walewski, Knapik and Kwiatkowski had, with the help of forged accounts, embezzled a sum of tens of thousands of złoty. The greatest guilt for the embezzlement is borne by Walewski, who appropriated a sum of nearly 50 thousand zł.
Last Monday the trial of the accused took place for the third time in the local district court. Before the court proceedings the defence submitted a motion that, on the basis of the amnesty, the charge against Knapik and Kwiatkowski be annulled.
The court withdrew for deliberation and then agreed to the defenders' motion.
After the hearing of the witnesses, who confirmed the charge against Walewski, the court sentenced him to two years in prison.

He got married "a little bit". — Jewish daughters, be careful! / The visit of Mrs. Widrowicz from Eretz Israel / Nechama, Kadish and Chash tonight in Sosnowiec / Meeting of jewellers and watchmakers / Bought "diamonds" / Theatre repertoire

[Lublin / Zagłębie — warning against a marriage swindler; followed by five short items: Sosnowiec, Będzin, theatre.]
Through the editorial office of the "Lubliner Tugblat" we have been asked to print the following notice:
The "hero" of the story is the 29-year-old Asher Fridman, a tall, blond young man; he comes from Kowel, and he also has family in Lublin. In his pocket he carries a get [bill of divorce]. He is, that is to say, a divorcé. And that is true — but it is also true that this divorcé has already managed to make many Jewish girls unhappy.
Wherever he comes, he succeeds, with the help of matchmakers, in making some Jewish daughter unhappy, from whom he takes the dowry and then vanishes.
On the 3rd of this month he got married in Lublin. Soon after the wedding, however, he declared that he had to travel to Warsaw to order a wagon of coal; he took 200 zł. and left.
Several days have passed and the man has not come back.
The young man carries a get about with him in his pocket and will probably try in Zagłębie too to let matches be proposed to him and have "a bit of" a wedding, in order to grab a little more money. So people should be careful, and wherever this person turns up he should be detained and the editorial office of the "Lubliner Tugblat" informed.
—o—
The visit of Mrs. Widrowicz from Eretz Israel
For a few days now the well-known women's leader, representative of the Head Directorate of the KKL [Jewish National Fund] in Jerusalem, Mrs. Lea Widrowicz [?], has been staying in Sosnowiec. Immediately after her arrival Mrs. Widrowicz set about organizing the work in connection with the 50th jubilee of the Hibbat Zion movement and 30 years of the Keren Kayemet. For this purpose a large academy [festive gathering] took place last Saturday evening in the "Angielski Hall", at which the distinguished guest spoke with a very substantial lecture about the work of construction in Eretz Israel, and about the era and the 50 years of "Hovat-Zion" [sic].
After the academy a glass of tea was held, at which those present had the opportunity to listen to an interesting conversation on how to unite [?] (perhaps: perpetuate) the era of the Hibbat Zion movement.
Thanks to her popularity the guest from Eretz Israel also succeeded in interesting a larger circle of women, with whose help she set about organizing the forthcoming large bazaar in Sosnowiec.

Nechama, Kadish and Chash tonight in Sosnowiec

Warsaw “Diamond Merchants”

[Będzin — crime.] They have come on a guest tour to Zagłębie. Be careful and do not buy any “bargains”.
It happened in Będzin on Małachowskiego Street.
The 65-year-old Nute Feiner was on his way to pay a bill of exchange of 300 zł. at the “Bank Polski”. As he was walking along Małachowskiego Street, a Christian came up to him and asked Feiner:
— “Gdzie tu jest polski sklep?” [Polish: Where is there a Polish shop here?]
Feiner, without the slightest suspicion that this naive question was drawing him into a swindlers’ net, answered the “Christian” that on Kołłątaja Street there are purely Polish shops. But when Feiner had gone a few steps further, he was stopped by a young man who pestered him to tell him what the Christian had wanted.
— He asked me — said Feiner — where there is a Polish shop.
— You hear, grandpa — the young man began — I am the son of a jeweller in Będzin; my father has a jewellery shop on Kołłątaja Street, and the Christian is a Russian; he has a diamond brooch for sale that is worth a lot of money, but my father dug in his heels and would not accept the price the Russian goy demanded; so I would ask you, grandpa, to buy the bargain on our behalf, and for your trouble you will get 25 zł.
The sweet little words began to work on Feiner; he approached the “diamond merchant” and began to negotiate the “deal”... But the “merchant” ostensibly pushed him away: I won’t sell it — he said — to a Jew, only to a Pole...
At that moment the “son of the Będzin jewellery merchant” came up; he helped persuade the Christian to sell the brooch after all to the old “Żyd”, because he is an honest man, and finally the “merchant” agreed to make the deal.
The gang went into the gateway of Winer’s house, and there the Christian showed the buyer a beautifully decorated “diamond brooch”, for which he asked 400 zł...
— Pay for now — the young man said to Feiner — I have only dollars on me and the Christian won’t take dollars; after paying we will go home and you will get your money back with 25 zł. profit.
Feiner would not agree to this proposal: I will give the złotys — he said — and you give me the dollars. Meanwhile F. noticed the young man getting “intimate” with his pockets, and so the deal fell through...
—o—
Anti-Jewish Excesses in Olkusz.
[Olkusz — antisemitism.] The local school youth of the gymnasium and the crafts school did not lag behind their hooligan comrades in other towns and attacked the Jewish pupils in the gymnasium and scrawled anti-Jewish slogans on the blackboards, benches and walls. On Monday evening, after a meeting, a band of school youth attacked Jewish passers-by and beat them with sticks. In many shops, and mostly in the back streets, as well as in the synagogue and the mikveh, the window panes were smashed. The panic was indescribable; the police were alerted and, with the commissioner at their head, quelled the disturbances. On Górnicza [?] Street a band of hooligans lay in wait at the crafts school for the Jewish pupils of the evening courses. The latter would not go home until the teacher (“professor”) brought police and the hooligans were dispersed. Many hooligans were arrested and released the next day. A certain Ezer Goldfeld was also arrested; he is accused of resisting the police.
On Tuesday morning a delegation consisting of the rabbi, A. Paluch and B. Weisslfisch presented itself to the starosta and reported the excesses that had taken place and asked for protection in future. The starosta answered the delegation: first of all, nobody was wounded. Secondly, the Jewish youth must not let itself be influenced by the communists. To Mr. Weisslfisch’s question whether, when attacked, one must just let it happen, the starosta gave no answer, but promised that the administrative authorities would not permit any disturbances whatsoever. A. B.

The Będzin Jewish Community Has Lost a Budget Payer.
[Będzin — kehilla.] There is in Będzin a “pan mecenas” [Polish: Mr. Advocate], a certain Mr. R. Already some time ago people murmured that the pan mecenas had left us and belonged to others now, not to Jews. But nobody knew anything certain about it.
This week the “secret” was revealed — by him himself, by the pan mecenas.
The community (gmina) in Będzin called on him to settle his debt for several years of community budget levy (etat).
And when the debtor had read the demand, he informed the community by telephone that they should no longer bother him about budget matters, because he no longer belongs to the Jewish people...
— A budget payer has been lost.

Tax Relief for Bakers.
[Taxes — artisans.] All bakers who have artisan cards will pay turnover tax of only one percent. This will take effect as of 1 January 1932. The bakery shops belonging to the baker will likewise pay one percent.
On the other hand, bakers who have no artisan cards will go on paying 2 percent.
The same relief is being introduced for other workshops producing foodstuffs that have artisan cards.
—o—
Relief for Artisans Abolished.
Artisans who work with the help of one worker, even with the help of their own son or daughter, will have to pay turnover tax from 1 January. Until now they were exempt. From now on only those artisans who work entirely alone, without any helper, will be exempt from turnover tax.

Rally of “HaShomer HaLeumi” and “Herzliya” in Będzin
[Będzin — Zionism, youth.] On Sunday the first gathering of the above-mentioned organisations took place in the premises of the Zionist Organisation in Będzin.
200 members took part in the gathering, from Sosnowiec, Będzin, Dąbrowa, Zawiercie, Miechów, etc. On behalf of the supreme leadership Mr. Meir Hartman took part. After the gathering was opened by Mr. Irbach, greetings were given in the name of the Central Committee (Ts. K.) and of the Zionist Organisation by Mrs. Ratner, Wygodzki [?] and Landner. The reports show that the above-mentioned organisations hold first place among the youth movements in the district.
At the gathering a series of ideological-educational and organisational questions was discussed. A whole series of resolutions was adopted, among others a protest against the Endek attacks and a resolution to strengthen the work for the KKL (Jewish National Fund).
Then a district (galil) leadership was elected, which includes Messrs.: Czarna, Szmitene (Sosnowiec), Aurbach, Frajberg, Suszek (Będzin). The gathering was closed with the singing of Eretz-Israel songs and with dances.

A Christian who has lived for many years with an apostate woman wants to convert to Judaism.
In Pradła (near Zawiercie), many years ago a Jewish girl married a Christian villager. „Shalom bayit“ (domestic peace) did not reign in this couple, and sharp quarrels were among their frequent occurrences. Suicide out of despair.
On Sunday evening a young couple from Sosnowiec came to the Będzin rabbinate to obtain a get [divorce]. The couple has already been separated for many years, but the the woman had suffered a great deal all the while from her husband, who had abandoned her.

15-year-old mother throws her child into a pit.

Horrible murder in a coal wagon.
On Tuesday at 11 in the morning a man in nightclothes was found in a coal wagon, showing no signs of life whatsoever. The medical examination established that the person had been murdered.
The next day the matter became clear. In Niwka an unknown person was arrested, who is indeed the one who murdered him in the wagon.
Under questioning the murderer declared that he is from Warsaw; he had travelled to Zagłębie to look for work, but as he had no money to buy a train ticket he got into a freight wagon and travelled „na gapę“ [Polish: as a stowaway]. In Częstochowa — as the murderer declares — the murdered man got into the same wagon; on the way a quarrel broke out between them and he murdered him with a knife. After the murder he went into another wagon, in which he travelled as far as Niwka.
The murderer will be brought before a summary court [Standgericht].

A Relief Campaign Must Be Started for the Fallen Small Traders and Merchants (A Letter to the Editor)

[Letter to the editor — merchants and small traders; followed by four Zagłębie news items: Strzemieszyce, Mstów/Żarki, Olkusz, trading patents.]
The Jewish merchant, who years ago played a dominant role in society, finds himself today, because of the general crisis, in a very bitter situation.
The Jewish small trader and merchant, however he may look outwardly, has today no possibility of buying out a patent [annual trading licence] with his own means, and we must also understand that a patent is the foundation of the merchant, because the merchant who has only a patent — even if he no longer has any goods — still finds ways to obtain a piece of dry bread for his wife and little children.
Unfortunately Jewish society in the whole country, and here too, is not able to come forward with greater help for the small traders and merchants. Bearing in mind that, as is written everywhere, our[?] merchant class today consists 90 per cent of small traders, the Jewish merchant and small trader struggles with all his strength, but he will not stretch out his hand for charity. Every day he has a piece of dry bread and eats it with tears at home. But when he goes out into the street you will recognise nothing in him, because he lives in hope of a better tomorrow. He hopes that he will hold out and live to see the better tomorrow. But despite everything, and despite all the direct and indirect taxes he must pay in the course of a whole year — when his second Day of Judgment comes, i.e. the month of December, and he has no means whatsoever to buy out the patent, then he must surrender. He is then like a soldier at his post whose ammunition has run out, facing two choices: either to commit suicide with the last bullet he has left, or to surrender to fate. Such a soldier is saved only when help comes to him from his close brothers. Such help is needed today by the Jewish small trader and merchant. And therefore the boards of the merchants' associations must undertake a campaign for the Jewish small traders and fallen merchants.
P. Sh.

Police Investigation into the Excesses in Strzemieszyce.
As in all places, a band of Christian pupils in Strzemieszyce ran riot and went out into the street "to defend the fatherland": they smashed windows, beat Jewish passers-by, etc.[?]
When the victims came to report it at the police station, the przodownik [police sergeant] would not react and did not allow reports to be drawn up about the incidents.
The victims turned with a complaint against the przodownik to the police commandant in Będzin, from where the Dąbrowa commissioner was delegated to investigate it.
The investigation took place this week. The victims confirmed what they had stated in the complaint.

Car Accident beyond Mstów[?]. The Żarki Rebbe Seriously Injured.
On Monday the following accident happened beyond Mstów:
A few in-laws drove from the shtetl to Żarki, among them the Żarki Rebbe, who had taken part in the engagement (tnoim) celebration held that same day in Mstów.
Driving up a hill, the chauffeur saw the car rolling backwards and shouted to the passengers to get out of the car as fast as possible. Everyone got out except the Rebbe, who ended up under the car and was seriously injured.

Who Will Be Able to Buy a Patent of the 3rd and 4th Category.
The Zagłębie tax offices have received an ordinance from the Finance Ministry about various relief measures in buying patents for the year 1932.
These reductions are for merchants who until now had a 2nd-category patent and will now be able to buy the 3rd category.
Those of the 3rd category will be able to buy the 4th category if the persons concerned submit a reasoned request to the tax office by 31 December at the latest. The tax authority will then carry out a check whether the business is actually threatened with ruin if it has to buy a larger trading patent. Further[?], [it] will be taken into account for 2nd[?] categories — if the turnover did not exceed 30 thousand zł., and for the 3rd category up to 10.000 zł.
Restaurant owners will be able to buy the 3rd category if the turnover does not exceed 15,000 zł. On the other hand, none of the restaurant owners who sell alcohol will benefit from a 4th-category patent.
Exempt from buying patents are the indigent[?] whose turnover has not exceeded 2000 zł.
