An Hour of Truth!...

Pini Baal Lashon.
(About the world and about ourselves).
Once, a very long time ago, I read a little book entitled „An Hour of Truth“. I no longer remember its contents exactly, but as far as it lies in my memory, the author puts forward the idea that if everyone went with the truth for just one hour, there would be an upheaval in the world.
And so the whole world has been persuaded to this day that one must not go with the truth. The truth is no good, it can, God forbid, do harm; it is very harmful both to the individual and to the community.
And even the „moralists“, supposedly those who hate falsehood, coined the saying: „A lie you may not tell, and the truth nobody forces you to tell.“
So indeed the whole world is not what it really is. Indeed it is hard to find anyone nowadays whom one could[?] see in his true shape.
People play theatre, individually and collectively, everywhere, in all countries, in all languages, in all movements, in all [—], in everything.
People disguise themselves in various garments in order to look as the demand of the moment requires.
People dissemble, put on make-up, paint themselves according to the role they want to play among others.
People speak such „phrases“[?], sing such „ditties“ and dance such „dances“ as others want to hear, in order to find favour, to be liked.
Shakespeare said long ago that the world is a theatre and people are the actors.
And being an actor is no easy job. To dissemble and play the role of someone else and not of oneself costs one's health — even when one has the talent for it.
Just as it is hard for everyone to be what one is, it is harder still to be what one is not.
And that is precisely why life is hard. And that is why everyone torments himself in his own little world.
So the question arises: why shouldn't the world try, out of curiosity, to hold at least one hour of truth? If one could at least see that falsehood makes the world a paradise, that all is good and pleasant and fine — well, why not [printed „machiko iti“ = mehaykha teitei], let things go on as they go; but since the world, with its falsehood, has the face it has now, it seems it no longer has much to fear from the truth...
— — —
And I picture to myself in my fantasy what would happen in the world if it held an hour of real truth.
It would be worth, I tell you, a million dollars just to take one look at it. People would be holding their sides laughing at it.
Imagine: all the states gather at a conference of the so-called „League of Nations“, and they sit there so [—] and listen to long speeches and reports on the question of disarmament.
And the best speakers put forward the best ideas: that weapons in general are a savage thing, a remnant of olden times when savage man lived „by his sword“. Not to mention war — that is surely a crime that no civilised state may even think of. That is, after all, sheer murder in broad daylight!...
But since one state is afraid of the other, one must have weapons; and since one has weapons, the hands itch, and from time to time there must be a little scuffle...
Therefore, it is only just that they stop building warships and other instruments of destruction, and with time wars too will disappear.
Well, and what if a dispute arises? — for that there is arbitration [din Torah] one can rely on. And as the saying goes: „Jak nie psak, to psakec“ [mock-Polish: if not a verdict, then a little verdict]!...
So they sit there chatting cosily, and suddenly the „hour of truth“ arrives. And the states see one another in their true shape and one hears plain words, the pure truth: that one state really wants to swallow the other „hooves and all“ [Polish aż z kopytami], and that not a single state thinks even for one minute of disarmament. Disarmament yes — but not by itself; let others do it.
And so all the representatives of the states remain standing facing one another with open mouths, staring at each other like hens[?], and they ask themselves:
— What is all this dissembling for? What is all this playing theatre for?... What is this falsehood for, which is called the „League of Nations“ [Yiddish „natsionen lig“] and is in truth the „Nations' Lies“ [„natsionen ligen“ — pun: lig/ligen = league/lie]?...
And everyone would burst out in the greatest laughter.
— — —
Or take such a simple little picture:
The biggest „carp-heads“ [fat cats] are sitting at a full supper and talking about the unemployed and the poor who are now flooding the country.
And the speeches are fine and warm. Feelings of pity pour out over all their hearts. They understand and know that the poor unemployed and destitute are dying of hunger and freezing from cold, and that something must be done for them.
And one flowery speech is stronger than the other. And the hearts warm up and melt like wax, and they resolve that everyone must now make sacrifices for the country; and they resolve again to turn to the people with an appeal for support, for donations...
And suddenly the „hour of truth“ arrives, and the millionaires around the table swallow the last bite of the good supper and come out with the real truth. Let us say, like this:
— This whole commotion about the crisis doesn't touch us even in the left heel; all these unemployed schleppers and idlers could just as well perish of hunger. Who needs them, what[?] sort of pity? Who listens to them, and who will [?] them — [?] no more than to be a little afraid, because they say „need breaks iron“... And we are a little ashamed before the world and before one another — one can't do otherwise...
Oh, what laughter there would be then in the rich hall.
— — —
Or take another, a Jewish picture.
Great Jewish minds sit and ponder how to reach the great world and enlighten it about our bitter lot on earth everywhere.
And they write down facts about attacks and pogroms against Jews in Romania, in Mexico, in Germany, in Congress Poland [„Kroyn-Poyln“], and where not — and they console themselves that the world will after all come to a just understanding, and will pity and help us, so that we can protect our heads from the bloody hands of the pogromists.
And they deliberate how to conduct the enlightenment of the world.
And suddenly the „hour of truth“ arrives, and the Jews open their holy mouths and tell the real truth to the whole world straight in the face:
— We know that all of you would like to drown us in a spoonful of water. There is not one among you who would love a Jew. Oppression[?] and murders and hatred burn in all of you everywhere. And no enlightenment will help us: we only need to learn to hit back in the face. Only then will you [—] us...
And oh, what laughter this truth would provoke among the gentiles...
— — —
So what do you say: would an „hour of truth“ be worse for the world? Believe me, no. Worse it can no longer be.
The Struggle Against Hellenism

[Essay — Hanukkah; history and thought.]
Dr. A. Gottesdiener.

The Babylonian exile cured the people of Judah and Israel of its Canaanite weakness for the ancient cultures of Assyria, Babylon, Tyre and Sidon, and for the oldest and highest of them all — the culture of Egypt. In the history of all these cultures the twilight judgment had set in; their gods had fallen into senile weakness, into consumption, and had begun to dry up, to sicken and to die.
Jewish culture in the new settlement in Judah began to develop anew, with its whole face turned toward itself — original, robust, with a special appearance, a special fragrance; drawing from the ancient, pure and eternally fresh cultural spring that its prophets had dug for it.
They also laid down its political line — not to meddle in the bloody struggles of the heathen neighbours, but to stay by the ploughshare and by the book. Quietly and calmly, like a sealed spring, like a pious bud, Jewish life develops in the Land of Israel.
When East and West seized each other by the beards, when Persia and Greece waged their wars and the fate of world dominion hung in the balance [?], Judah sits quietly. — Its history had taught it to believe neither in the gods of the East nor in the gods of the West. After all, the supreme Greek god Zeus also held a spear. True, the West also had its goddess of justice, but firstly she did not hold supreme power, secondly she was after all a weak woman, thirdly her eyes were bound, and the tongue of her scales she could only feel with her hand — might decided over right.
The definitive victory of the West over the East, achieved by the Macedonian king Alexander the Great, began the great work of fusion. East and West fell into each other's arms; lofty Greek art held its triumphal processions as far as the distant East, and the new Greek rulers in the East learned the methods of government of the old Oriental despots.
In truth the Oriental peoples of Asia remained, in the depth of their souls, alien to the whole of Greek culture, and under the names of the new Greek gods they went on worshipping their old ones. But on the surface of life a settlement was reached, a compromise, which history calls Hellenism. Hellenism is a culture, a compound between East and West; outwardly [?] it is like Aphrodite herself — like the Greek goddess of love — but its heart and its qualities are corrupt. Its highest ideal is — power. Respect for power passes over into deification of the holders of power, who force their way up into the very heavens of the gods and sit down at table with them as equals among equals, or even take the very highest seat in the pantheons.
In the Jewish heaven, however, there was no room for man-gods, as there was none for other gods in general. The Jewish heaven is, by the way, too high for man-gods and god-men to be able to climb up to it; in its height it spans East and West, and only beneath it do suns rise and suns set. In its clarity are reflected not, indeed, the beautiful plastic images of Greek art, but deep, pure human hearts and lofty ethical ideals, which gush forth from the words of the Jewish prophets, not weighed and not measured like the sounds of music, but daring [?], powerful, stormy and fiery — as the expression of the suffering of the Jewish nation, as the expression of the suffering of tormented mankind.
At that very historical moment, when the beautiful Greek life — not the beautiful Greek culture — made all the peoples of the Near East forget their old gods, and they crept with their old religions into the strange Greek garments, as the Negroes in Africa today [creep] into Parisian frock-coats and top hats — at that historical moment only the small people of Israel did not let itself be dazzled by the glitter of Greek life, did not let itself be bound in the golden chains, did not sacrifice its eternal life for momentary life, remained faithful to its God and its Torah, and taught mankind to give up its life for ideals.
Here lies the tragedy of its fate, here — the strength of its eternity.
The events in the time of Antiochus Epiphanes are the beginning of the struggle that continues to this very day. Everyone has learned from us the law of self-sacrifice for ethical, religious and national ideals. But everyone has forgotten the author, and toward no people in the world is the honour of ideals so desecrated as toward the people of Israel.—
The days of Hellenism are not yet over; reverence for power still occupies first place. Zeus with the spear still frequents the best society, only it is no longer as hospitable as it once was. Our prophets have been locked up in armoured cars, and with their bloody words they grease the wheels of the great cannons.
No, Hellenism has not yet died, neither in the great world nor in our world — and today they wander about in our camp, the old Jewish Hellenists; true, they wander about as in a world of chaos — for even bowing to the foreign gods does not help them to be admitted to the sugar-table [?], disowning their people does not help them to be received into the "mysteries of power", and yet they do not want to join the Jewish camp.
Desolate lie the fields of Judah and Galilee, where the daggers [kinjals] of wild Bedouins devour the blood of our noble youth, and they go on dancing drunkenly around the old "Bacchus". Thousands of Jewish youth abandon the synagogues and study-houses and run off to the old "gymnasia", where the haughty Greek youth meets them with cudgels and fists. They make their own [ones] for their own money, building them right up against the Temple itself.
Black, dark shadows still chase the little lights of the holy Menorah, but there still lives a handful of those old "Hasidim", there still live old Maccabees, who carry the banner high: "Who is like unto Thee among the mighty, O Lord" — who are able to shed their blood for the Land of Israel, who guard the holy olive oil, who kindle new light in the old Menorah, and anew the old battlefield is lit up — where the struggle still rages between Mount Sinai and Olympus, between Simeon the Just and Alexander of Macedon, between Antiochus Epiphanes and Judah the Maccabee: the struggle against Hellenism.
Little Candles

[Poetry — Hanukkah.]
Lejzer Szykman.

Be greeted, you symbolic little candles:
you eternal, eternal Jewish little fires!
Forever shall you light up dark worlds,
though evil winds are blowing.
O you small, much-meaning little candles,
some magic lies within your little flames;
always you tell old tales anew
and we listen to them so eagerly.
O you mysterious little flames,
it is good that you do not tell of Jews as little lambs,
but of true heroes, of martyrs and of victory —
we shall cheerfully fight against the eternal Jewish war [?]...
Be greeted, you symbolic little candles;
you eternal, eternal Jewish little fires!
Forever shall you light up dark worlds,
though evil winds are blowing.
Save Our Honour!

[Satire — antisemitism.] (A little letter from an Endek [National Democrat] “green ribbon”).
Szanowny Panie Redaktorze! [Dear Mr Editor]
You were right with your writing; my hands really[?] itched [Polish swędzić], and a little of your blood would have been a cure for me. But I am not just anybody, you know that my father and my grandfather, in a time of trouble, turned for advice and help only to you, Moszku kochany [dear Moshke], so do stay true to the old Polish tradition and give advice.
My green ribbons demand nothing else of me but that I boycott the Jews. You know, you Żydzi are worthy of such a boycott. Our boycott appeal is, after all, a holy one, and now I am told to boycott Jewish literature and art. I will do it. It plays no role. I don't read[?] any literature at all anyway, so it will come easy to me.
But I am also told to break off social relations with Jews — I'll tell you in deepest secret that such a sacrifice we can no longer make. Do tell your little Jewesses [żydóweczki] that we will not abandon them. No matter — even such as have Hasidim for husbands.
Moszku kochany! Our trouble is even greater on account of something else — specifically a Zagłębie trouble! You know what an ugly end our anti-Jewish actions in Sosnowiec came to: the town laughed at us. Not a single Jewish head did we split, not a single shop did we loot [Polish zrabować]; our whole fury[?] went out on a couple of windowpanes in the old Sosnowiec synagogue.
They — the Warsaw, the Kraków, the Vilna and even the Poznań students — have it as good as can be. They have Jewish students there, they have someone to throw at, someone to beat, they can fight for Poland's honour. With us here in Zagłębie there are great, chopped-up troubles.
Give here, Moshke, your Jewish mug [żydowska morda], and no one will see us kissing.
Wałach Endecki.
Starszy [senior] of the “Green Colour”.

A Hanukkah Chat

[Hanukkah — feuilleton.] H. Lazarson.
All other things may be important or interesting, but — one is Hanukkah.
Hanukkah comes only once a year, and other things come whenever they like.
It is indeed an event that lasts eight whole days, but still — once a year.
And you can't help it — you must give a thought to the dreidel.
Every year the same, yet the dreidel never grows old, just as the miracle of Hanukkah cannot grow old.
Just look how the dreidel spins and spins until it reaches such momentum that your eyes begin to swim, you can no longer make out what is spinning, and suddenly it begins to grow weaker and weaker until it spins itself out and falls down.
So the year has spun and spun, at times spun so hard that our eyes began to swim and we did not know in what world we were spinning, and suddenly it slows down and you look around — you have already spun round — Hanukkah again.
The same could be said, you'll think, of every day of the year: when you just open your eyes and consider where you are in the world — and that is indeed true.
But not every day of the year is Hanukkah, and Hanukkah is the time of the dreidel game — the game of all of life.
Above all, of Jewish life.
If we did not yet have a Hanukkah, we would have had to create one, because without it things would be too sad.
Without the little candles it would be too dark.
Without the dreidel we would have to stand in one place, and that is something they do not let us do.
So a few thousand years ago we were given something that is always good and suits all our times.
Today's world dictators, great-grandchildren of the Romans, are now interested in the question whether the Jews are a nation or a religious sect.
If they had the time to reflect[?] on the miracle of Hanukkah, perhaps they would find[?] an answer to his [sic] question.
For were it not for that miracle, there might have been neither a nation nor a religious sect. Through that miracle the two remained in one.
But not all outsiders can know the answer.
For them it is only a question. One big question.
Rome remained in its place, and the great-grandchildren of the Romans kept the inheritance, and there is someone to work with and something to show off before the world.
Jerusalem was laid waste and in ruins for two thousand years, and the great-grandchildren of the Hasmoneans were scattered over all seven seas — and the dictator of present-day Rome asks: who are they, these people?
An eternal question, an old question, as old as the seven hills on which Rome is built, and as old as the seven seas over which the Jews are sown and scattered.
And it was none other than old Mattathias who brought about the whole story back then.
That old man's obstinacy helped him carry out what was considered impossible to carry out.
The first thing — throwing the swine out of the Temple — that alone was already a historic deed, for had the swine stayed there then, it would have been worse with such a Temple than without one at all.
The second thing — the little candles that burned without olive oil. The enemies of the Jews took away all the olive oil and arranged it so that by all the laws of nature it had to be dark. That has always been their method — to do everything that can make it dark for the Jews. Well, and old Mattathias saw to it that there would be light: there was not enough even for one day, and it burned and shone no less than eight days.
And eight days, as you know, is no more than a parable, for in truth it has been burning and shining for the third thousand years now. Two thousand years it has shone — and with a smile, until now.
And then the foundation stone was laid of the dreidel that spins. It spins and spins and — falls down, and lo, it spins on. There is no end to it. Something that is not a dreidel, once it falls, can spin no more. But a dreidel spins on.
So then, the meaning of the candles and — of the dreidel is so clear and plain that everyone can understand it.
It would only be fair to find out the meaning of the latkes as well.
One should call in experts, you'll say, to examine the latkes and see what is hidden in them that has to do with Hanukkah.
Don't say that.
For experts have been examining the Jews for thousands of years and don't know what they are. Most likely they won't know what latkes are either.
We would have tried to answer it by the fact that latkes are fried in olive oil, and olive oil does have something to do with Hanukkah. Or perhaps by the fact that the potatoes from which latkes are made lie in the earth, and since that is so...
But no — it doesn't make sense.
We will try to give another explanation, and if anyone knows a better one, let him not be ashamed and speak up.
In short, as you know, latkes differ from all other dishes in that, whereas an ordinary dish such as a piece of goose, for example, is cooked all at once, served, eaten up, and done — latkes are a thing you fry little by little, and you keep serving fresh, hot ones, and the more you serve, the more one eats.
And with Hanukkah it is exactly the same: the more Jews celebrate[?] Hanukkah, the more latkes they will eat[?].
Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion (Vayeshev)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Vayeshev
The Portion
—o—
a) "And Jacob dwelt in the land of his father's sojournings" (Gen. 37:1)
The previous portion ends by listing the many chiefs of Esau, gentile lords, by whom Jacob was surrounded as if among wolves — and yet: "And Jacob dwelt." He sat in tranquillity. The hostile neighbours did not disturb his house. But when envy and hatred broke out among his children over a trifle, over a silk shirt, etc., that already led to what the most dangerous outside enemies had been unable to bring about — to misfortunes and exile.
Torat Moshe (Alshich).
b) "These are the generations of Jacob: Joseph" (ibid. 2)
"Jacob wished to dwell in tranquillity — the trouble of Joseph sprang upon him." Rashi.
1.
Jacob and Esau divided the worlds between them. Esau took this world, and Jacob — the world to come. But the strange thing is that he [Esau] is sure he will have the world to come as well. For had he doubted it, he would not have had this world (which is his) either — it would not have agreed with him... Jacob, on the other hand, is so preoccupied with his world to come that even the little bit of this world that he nibbles from Esau does not agree with him...
Kometz ha-Minchah (by[?] the Rebbe R' Heshel).
2.
The Egyptian exile already begins with Isaac. But Isaac did not need to come to Egypt; it pained him enough that he was driven out [sic] of the Land of Israel. But Jacob "wished to dwell in tranquillity." He wanted to settle into exile, live quietly and make peace with fate — "at once the trouble of Joseph sprang upon him": so go down to Egypt.
Imrei Shefer.
c) "And behold, your sheaves came round" (Gen. 37:7)
A rich Jew once had a desire to become parnas (communal head) in a shtetl. A clever Jew said to him: what is your pedigree, then? Your pedigree is only your money-pouch. Well, for your money-pouch I do indeed have respect — but for you? Your money-pouch is indeed bigger than ours, but you are not bigger than us...
Joseph's brothers argued with him: you dreamt that your sheaf (wealth) will be bigger than ours — but how do you come to [rule over us]?
Et Ratzon.
d) "Shalt thou indeed reign over us? Or shalt thou indeed have dominion over us?" (ibid. 8)
1.
"Do you think," the brothers argued to Joseph, "that by 'having dominion over us' — by ruling over us — you will 'reign', that you will acquire kingship? No, brothers: with dominion one acquires sooner servitude — bondage to those over whom you rule..."
Binah la-Ittim.
2.
"Shalt thou indeed have dominion over us": if you want to rule over us by force, "shalt thou indeed reign over us" — do you really think you will attain rulership? "Whoever pursues authority, authority flees from him"... Authority comes only to the one who runs away from it.
Ohel Yaakov.
e) "I seek my brethren" (ibid. 16)
All the Hasidic books speak a great deal about how a Jew should not complain that he is in exile, but only about the exile of the Shekhinah (Divine Presence). Very characteristic, therefore, are the words of the "Tiferet Shlomo" on this verse:
Over the exile of the Shekhinah alone one need not grieve. It does not need our pity... God can help Himself... "But Thou, O Lord, sittest forever" — You, God, may sit forever in exile... The main thing is only: "Why dost Thou forget us forever?" — us, do not forget...
This is also the meaning of Joseph's answer: "I seek my brethren" — I am interested only in the sufferings of my brothers. Jonah the prophet did not want to obey God and be an accuser against Jews — that is the way...
f) "By the hand of his friend the Adullamite" (Gen. 38:20)
A person should have such a friend — said Rabbi Mendele of Kotzk — to whom he can confide even a sin such as Judah's.
g) "Lest we be put to shame" (ibid. 23)
Judah was ashamed lest people find out about the affair; and the Adullamite — probably a playboy — was ashamed that he had not managed to find such-and-such a woman... for him that was a disgrace.
Pitgamei Oraita (R' Gedalia Tiktin).
h) "Bring her forth, and let her be burnt" (ibid. 24)
The usual translation is strange. The Talmud [printed: "the disciple"] indeed tries to explain it by way of pilpul. But most likely seems the commentary of R' Eliezer Ashkenazi (author of "Ma'asei ha-Shem"), that "let her be burnt" means branding a mark on the forehead, for this is still done today in Asian countries.
Haftarah
—o—
i) "That pant after the dust of the earth on the head of the poor" (Amos 2:7)
The prophet means here by "those who pant after the dust of the earth" those who go[?] with bowed heads, falsely lowering their eyes that shine with piety — but all their humility they merely simulate, so that "on the head of the poor" they may climb onto the neck of the masses and ride on the poor wretched nags..
Sha'ar Bat Rabim.
j) "Shall evil befall a city and the Lord hath not done it?" (ibid. 3:6)
If a misfortune comes, it was not God who did it, but you yourselves...
Remazei Rokeach.
Rasputin and His Jewish Beloved

A historical novel by Boris Maksimov.

Chapter One.
The Meeting.

In the palace of the banker Oskar Dimentstein, which stood in the richest district of the Russian capital, Petersburg, a select, narrow circle of respected wealthy Jews had gathered. They had come together for a meeting to which the banker Dimentstein had invited them through a special courier, who had visited each one of them in the course of the previous day and handed him the invitation.

They assembled in a splendidly beautiful reception hall, which had a high silvered [?] ceiling and marble columns. In the hall stood costly antique furniture, Persian carpets lay on the floor, and the electric lamps burned under fine, matte lampshades. On the walls hung artistic oil paintings set in costly gilded frames.

The assembled men kept very quiet; some smoked a cigar and some a papirosa, and all had very serious faces. All of them felt that they had been called here on account of a very serious and important matter.

The meeting was supposed to begin at seven o'clock; now it was already nearly eight, and it had still not begun. They were waiting for Baron Ginberg [?], who was at that time the representative of the Jews in Petersburg and a person of consequence in the high Russian circles.

The banker Mr. Dimentstein, a tall, solidly built man with a black moustache and clever black eyes, but already with grey hair at the temples, was restless. He could not stay seated in his place. So he rose, paced through the room and asked, as if to himself:
"What can it be, that the Baron is still not here?"

Nobody answered him, because all those present were indeed surprised that the Baron had not yet come. They all knew their Baron; they knew that he was a very punctual man who always arrives on time. Mr. Dimentstein said:
"Something must have happened..."
Again everyone fell silent.

Soon, however, a servant opened the door of the hall and announced the arrival of the Baron.

The Baron came in with hasty steps:
"Good evening, gentlemen!" he exclaimed in a loud, melodious voice, and bowed slightly to those assembled.

He was an elderly man of medium height, somewhat stout and very neat. He had a finely trimmed beard and a very bright face. Kindness, earnestness and dignity looked out of his blue-grey eyes. He remained standing in the middle of the hall and everyone surrounded him; Mr. Dimentstein pressed his hand warmly and respectfully:
"You are late, Baron..."
The Baron said:
"Forgive me, gentlemen... I am very sorry that you have had to wait for me..."
"But I could not help it... It is not my fault..."
"What on earth has happened, Baron?"

"I had a visitor who held me up against my will... When I was already ready to leave my house, to drive here and arrive on time, a high-standing official personage came to me and handed me an order..."
"An order!"
Everyone's face grew curious. The Baron caught his breath; his face was still very serious:
"He conveyed it to me as a request, but in fact it is an order.

"The matter is this: the Russian heir to the throne, little Alexei, is ill... So the official from the gradonachalnik [city governor] who visited me proposed that tomorrow I gather the Jews in the Great Synagogue, and that the rabbi, in the presence of all the gabbaim and respected Jews, hold a prayer service for the health of the 'naslednik' [heir]..."

Those assembled, except the banker, were astonished at the news. They had not known that the Russian heir to the throne was ill. Questions were heard from the assembly:
"The 'naslednik' is ill?"
"Nothing about it has been heard in town?"
"Has he been ill for long?"
"Is he very ill?"

"How long he has been ill I do not know, but it seems he is seriously ill, if they have already thought of turning to me about holding a prayer in the synagogue: if they are already turning for help to the Jewish God, it is a sign that the naslednik is very ill... I also know that the most famous professors have been summoned to Tsarskoye Selo... It goes without saying that I promised to carry out the order. We shall have to take every measure and see to it that tomorrow there is as large a congregation as possible in the synagogue. As I understood from the official's words, a representative of the gradonachalnik, and perhaps the gradonachalnik himself, will come to the synagogue tomorrow to attend the holding of the prayer... So we must see to it that there is a fine congregation."

"It goes without saying," said the banker, and his face was now deeply pensive [?], "we will have to let as many people as possible know that they should come to the synagogue at the appointed time... And now, gentlemen: please!"
He pointed with his hand to the door that led from the reception hall into a second room.

All those assembled went silently into the second room, which was Dimentstein's council chamber. The room was not as large as the hall, but no less richly furnished. In the middle of the room stood a large table, and around the table soft armchairs covered in dark green leather. Everyone sat down around the table. All were in expectation... When everyone was seated, the banker himself closed the door and took his place at the head of the table. His face had grown somewhat paler from inner agitation. The silence was pressed, dense.

At last the banker began:
"My dear gentlemen! I have called you here so that we may consult about a very important matter."

He caught his breath. All eyes were turned toward him. His voice grew clearer:

"From reliable sources I have learned that in Tsarskoye Selo a fierce agitation is going on against the Jewish citizens of the capital... Perhaps you know of it, and if you do not, I want to tell you now: I have free access to the salon of Countess Inatova [?]... I am in constant contact with that salon. There they know very well everything that happens in Tsarskoye Selo. And there I learned that for some time now a bitter agitation has been going on at the imperial court against the Jews of Petersburg... They are trying by every means to influence the Tsar and the Tsarina and to bring it about that A L L the Jews be sent out of Petersburg."

Consternation appeared on the faces of those assembled. All at once they felt a cold fear in their hearts. It was as if they had suddenly felt the ground begin to shake under his [sic] feet. Most of those present were merchants of the first guild, who had always had the right to live in Petersburg. Until now they had been sure that no one would take that right away from them, and here they felt that they were losing their security.

Mr. Dimentstein went on speaking:

"I have known of it for quite a while, but all this time I paid the matter no special attention. I knew that [printed: "di di"] the agitation was being conducted by clericals, and that the statesmen were against it. Now, however, as I have learned, the situation is taking on a serious character..."

"Really? Do you mean it seriously? Mr. Dimentstein! Is the situation really so serious?" asked one of those present, and there was fear in his voice.
Mr. Dimentstein slowly nodded his head:

"Regrettably, I do mean it... The situation is very serious... In connection with the naslednik's illness the agitation has grown stronger. For three days now the heir to the throne has been lying in bed suffering terrible pains; the best doctors cannot help him... they cannot ease his suffering. And the chief agitator against the Jews, the priest of the imperial court, Archimandrite Feofan, wants to exploit the opportunity and influence the Tsaritsa to have all the Jews expelled from the capital..."

"But what does the naslednik's illness have to do with the Jews?" someone asked in wonder.
Involuntarily, Mr. Dimentstein smiled.

A Reply to Mr. Witsch

[Debate — the general census in Poland; Hebrew or Yiddish as “mother tongue”.]
In last week’s “Zagl. Tsayt.” there appeared an article by an unknown person, signed [misprinted] Y. M. Witsch (apparently not quite bold enough to sign his full name), in which the author sharply condemns the “irresponsible persons” who agitate that at the forthcoming census one should give Hebrew as the mother tongue in the rubric dealing with “mother tongue”. The author of the article does not mention who these “irresponsible persons” are, and I suspect this was done with an ulterior motive [printed “piyune”], for had Mr. Witsch been honest and sincere, he would have seen that the “ha-ketza’akatah” [outcry] he is raising is not so dangerous. So, to the heart of the matter: the Zionist Organisation in Poland and the Central Committee of “Tarbut” have issued a circular to all their members, who are 100 per cent for Hebraising Jewish life in general and the Jewish school system in particular, that at the census they should give Hebrew as their mother tongue. So it is no longer a matter of mass agitation, of which Mr. Witsch is so afraid, but of an appeal of a purely principled character to the members of the organisations concerned, who agree with the “Tarbut” system — so what is all the noise about? Mr. Witsch further asserts that the value of Hebrew does not come into consideration at the census, since the count has an exclusively statistical character. I don’t know where Mr. Witsch gets the hundred-per-cent certainty that the census really has only a purely scientific-statistical value. It seems that, specifically with regard to the Jewish population, the census bears a definite political character; it is enough to point to the interpellation already submitted by the Jewish Koło [club] in the Sejm about ignoring the Yiddish language (a proof of the Zionists’ positive attitude to the Yiddish language) and to the absence of a rubric for “nationality”; and it seems to me superfluous to hold a discussion about it, for the political moment here is prominent enough.
Mr. Witsch further argues that if individuals give Hebrew as their mother tongue, this will be exploited by elements hostile to us as a justification for not wanting to found Jewish schools for Jewish children, on the pretext that some Jews do not recognise Yiddish as their language. But, Mr. Witsch, “mai chazit d’dam’kha didakh sumak tefei” [what makes you think your blood is redder?].
You are worried that giving Hebrew as mother tongue threatens the demand to found Jewish schools with Yiddish as the language of instruction. And [printed “in”] why do you not also take into account the just demand of the nationally Hebrew-conscious Jews, who require the competent factors to found Hebrew schools with Hebrew instruction? By completely passing over Hebrew in silence at the census we would endanger the whole already existing Hebrew school system. Can you dismiss with both hands[?] [printed “mit shtei pihei”] the large network of Tarbut schools in Poland, which is not much smaller than the Yiddishist schools? Although the Tarbut schools have lately not been receiving the subsidies from America, they nevertheless hold out, and in part their holdings are even growing. Are you not aware that a large Zionist-pioneering youth really regards Hebrew as its everyday language? It is enough to point to the recently held “Hashomer Hatzair” conference in Warsaw, which was conducted exclusively in Hebrew.
You further ask what will happen with the rubric “can you read and write, and in which language?”
And you ask: what will become of someone who has given Hebrew as mother tongue — what will he answer to the difficult question? For me, for instance, it is not at all such a difficult question as you imagine; the answer is quite simple: whoever says aleph must also say bet, and answer: I read and write Hebrew and Yiddish. In that very rubric one must also add the Yiddish language, for we Zionists have no intention, God forbid, of harming the Yiddish language. But we also do not want to threaten the existence of the Hebrew positions already conquered, and our Zionist Sejm deputies always demand equal rights for both languages. We hold that the two-language problem is our internal question, which we ourselves must solve, not with the help of outside factors.
This is how the question presents itself from the Zionist standpoint.
Nete Landner.

Magistrate reduces the rent of the halls
At Monday's session of the Commissioners' Council, Councillor (Ratman) Rechnitz asked why the square around the station is not being put in order. The Talmud Torah Is Subject to the Same Law as Leaven on Passover..

[Będzin — religious and educational institutions.] On Saturday night the second meeting to consider ways of putting the Talmud Torah back on its feet took place in the premises of the „Talmud Torah“. After the great public appeals and threats that the „shtiblekh“ [Hasidic prayer houses] would be closed, some 3–4 minyanim came to the meeting, headed by the rabbinate.
The meeting was chaired by Mr. Mordechai Dafner, and „speeches“ were made in which sharp reproaches were levelled at the trustees (apotropsim), who have taken the Talmud Torah as a monopoly and do not allow such elements as are able to benefit the institution to enter the board as well.
To this Mr. Rinski replied that „leaven on Passover is forbidden in the slightest amount“, i.e. that it is harmful for the „freethinkers“ (chofshim), who want to change the education as it has been until now, to be on the board“...
After the „speeches“ a committee was elected to consider how to improve the Talmud Torah's financial situation. The committee has already thought it over and found the following remedies: 1) the pledges (nedarim) on both Sabbaths of Hanukkah shall go to the Talmud Torah, and 2) a one-time collection of money shall be carried out in the town.

[Będzin — commerce.] The board of the local Small Traders' Association has addressed memoranda to the following authorities: 1) to the Post Office Directorate in Kraków, that a branch office (ekspozytura) of the post and telegraph be opened in Kołłątaja Street; 2) to the Chamber of Commerce in Sosnowiec, that when the smaller traders buy their trade licences (patents) no special payments for philanthropic purposes whatsoever be taken from them; and 3) to the postmaster (naczelnik) in Będzin, that he issue an order to the officials that members of the public who are already inside the post office at 12 noon and at 6 in the evening must be served without fail.
A Distraint over... 5 Groszy.

[Będzin — taxes.] A distraint (zajęcie) was carried out at the home of Mrs. A. Kornfeld[?] in Browarna Street for non-payment of a tax debt of 5 (read: five) groszy.
The enforcement costs amount to 1,25 zł.
Large Consultation on Fighting „Beggary“.

[Będzin — commerce and society.] How far the bitterness and hatred among the merchants have gone against the camps of beggars who wander from one shop to the next is shown by the large number of the most respected merchants who came on the strength of a short notice in our paper.
The consultation took place in the premises of the Merchants' Association under the chairmanship of Mr. Yakov Gutman: on this painful question Messrs. Gutman, Rubinlicht and others spoke, saying that the merchants must take the question seriously in order at long last to combat mass beggary.
A committee of 12 persons was elected. The committee holds regular meetings on the matter.
25th Jubilee of „Linat ha-Cholim“.

[Będzin — welfare institutions.] At the last board meeting it was resolved that in the first days of the coming month the 25th jubilee of the „Linat ha-Cholim“ society should be celebrated.

The Premises of „Hachnasat Orchim“ Open on Sunday

[Będzin — welfare institutions.] Next Sunday, the second day of Hanukkah, the festive opening of the „Hachnasat Orchim“ [hostel for poor wayfarers] will take place in premises of 5 rooms donated by Mr. Dawidowicz, which have been fitted out with all the equipment needed in such an establishment. Bit Off His Right Ear.

A Conference at the “Merchants' Association”.

[Będzin — merchants and taxes.]

Suicide of a Mentally Ill Woman.

A Meeting Devoted to the Population Census.

[Będzin — population census.]

General Meeting of the League for Labour Palestine.

[Będzin — Zionism.]
On Saturday the general meeting of the Będzin League for Labour Palestine took place in the premises of the “Hitachdut”, chaired by Mr. Gerstner.
The meeting, attended by up to 150 people, aroused great interest among all members. The meeting was opened by Mr. Rotenberg. Then Mr. Kozłowski reported on the activity of the working committee. The report shows that in the last half year the League collected over 3,000 zł. for the Kapa"i [Kupat Poalei Eretz Yisrael — the Palestine Workers' Fund].

The new committee, elected unanimously, consists of Messrs.: Dozer[?] A. Hampel, Kozłowski (Right Poale Zion), Ginzberg (Hitachdut), R. Liwer and K. Szwarcbaum (Gordonia), Majerowicz (Frayhayt), Grojer (Hashachar), S. Liwer and Szymon Rotenberg.
3 Jubilees.

[Będzin — Zionism.]

Brazen Bandit Attack on a Jewish Family in Zagórze

[Zagórze — armed robbery.]
One of the bandits — caught.
Last Tuesday at about 8 in the evening a brazen bandit attack was carried out in the flat of Mr. Shmelke Zadel[?] in Zagórze.
3 bandits with revolvers in their hands entered Zadel's flat, and after they had stuffed the mouths of the household they began to act as masters of the house.
The bandits, having robbed 2,000 zł. in cash, jewellery and other valuables, only then went into Zadel's shop, where they robbed bills of exchange and various grocery („colonial“) goods.
After carrying out the robbery the bandits ordered the household not to scream — if they did, they would shoot. To frighten them further a revolver was held to Zadel's head.
The damage from the robbery amounts to about 4,000 zł.
The police, which started an energetic operation, succeeded in catching one of the bandits in Piaski, where he was staying with a sister of his, at whose place part of the stolen grocery goods was found.

The Chamber of Commerce intervenes: the police should watch against the desecration of Sunday.
[Sosnowiec — trade; Sunday rest.]
The Polish „Merchants' Association“ in Sosnowiec applied to the Chamber of Commerce with a complaint against the trading that takes place on Sundays and other holidays.

Killed a Man in Order to „Inherit“ His Documents

[Częstochowa — murder.]

The „poor“ notaries also protest against the tax burden.
[Poland — taxes; the „crisis tax“.]
The new bill on the so-called „crisis tax“, which is to be introduced from the new year, has called forth a protest also on the part of the notaries, who will have to pay the tax.
Messrs. the notaries protest against the great „injustice“[?] and state that „only a small part of the notaries in Poland earn up to 10.000 zł. or something more monthly. (How much this „something more“ amounts to is not said.) The earnings of the majority amount to about 3.000 zł. That is the reality“.
This reality, however, is not at all a lamentable one. The greatest number of working Polish citizens would be entirely content with such a reality.
The total sum of all the taxes binding the notaries, already including the crisis tax, amounts to 12.3 per cent of earnings, i.e. out of 3 thousand zł. they will have to pay 369 zł., and they will be left with a net income of 1.631 zł. monthly.
It would be worthwhile for the merchants — on whom the greatest tax burden lies and for whom taxes have long ceased to be a part of earnings but are a part of capital, and very often even of other people's capital — to draw a moral: how one protests energetically against injustices that are no injustices at all; then perhaps a juster distribution of the tax burdens would come about...

„Oneg Shabbat“ at the Będzin „WIZO“.
[Będzin — WIZO; Palestine.]
On Wednesday evening Mrs. Leah[?] Hidrowicz of Tel Aviv gave a lecture in the premises of the Będzin „WIZO“. The lecturer described in splendid colours the life in the Jewish colonies, and in particular how the young generation is brought up.

Act of revenge by a sly [?] Jewish woman.
Into a Będzin cloth and [?] shop came an elegant lady, who declared to the merchant that she had come to buy for cash and therefore asked the merchant to treat her fairly.
The merchant, hearing that he had before him a customer with ready cash, offered her the best goods, for which he set exact prices.
After coming to terms on the prices, the woman insisted that the merchant cut the chosen [?] measure of goods from the pieces [bolts].
The merchant was not even willing to do so. But the urge to take in cash had its effect, and he cut up several perfectly saleable pieces.
When paying, [she] cried out:
— Oy, someone has stolen my money!
And crying "oy" she quickly left the shop.
The matter struck the merchant as odd, and after careful inquiry and investigation it became clear to him that the woman had done it deliberately to take revenge on the merchant, who had refused to give credit to her husband, a tailor from Olkusz.

An Open Letter to the Ringleaders of the Będzin Talmud Torah

[Będzin — Talmud Torah; open letter.]
(We have received this letter from a well-known Orthodox communal worker in Będzin. For certain reasons the letter is not signed with the full name. — The Editors.)
Reading in the "Zaglembier Tsaytung" No. 49 that at the meeting in the Talmud Torah a well-known Agudah leader in Będzin permitted himself to say that, just as chametz is forbidden in the slightest amount, so too it is forbidden to let such people take an interest in the Talmud Torah who are not harnessed to the Agudah wagon — this has compelled me to turn to you through the medium of the newspaper and ask you: have you given yourselves an account of the fact that 400 poor children, among them a large number of orphans, are growing up as ignoramuses and one-hundred-percent amei ha-aretz as far as Jewishness is concerned? Have you even once given thought to the fact that the host of Talmud Torah children must run at 7 o'clock in the morning to the state elementary schools (powszechne schools)? When do they pray? When do they wash their hands for a meal? Which Jewish law do they keep from 7 in the morning until 2 o'clock in the afternoon? Do you give your own children this sort of education too? With the meagre few gulden that you supposedly give them after a great hue and cry, you want to be dictators over hundreds of children? Woe to the eyes that see thus, and woe to the ears that hear thus. To play politics at the expense of 400 children...
For [printed "khayl", a misprint for "vayl"] when several people came forward — well-known and honest communal workers who had worked with self-sacrifice and finally obtained a concession for a state elementary school, and who wanted to raise the Talmud Torah to such a level that the children could study sacred subjects in the Talmud Torah in the morning and secular subjects in the afternoon — you wrecked the plans with your machinations, and on the ruins of the Talmud Torah you created for yourselves a new Torah shop by the name of "Ezrat Yesodei Torah"...
The upshot of my writing is: you should call a general meeting as quickly as possible and adopt the proposal that the esteemed parnas R' Yitzchak Aharon Landau made to you in his time. The proposal is that a special committee be created with the rabbi at its head to supervise the sacred studies, and at the same time influential persons from the town should be co-opted, who would oversee the secular studies and generally take an interest in the state of the Talmud Torah. When this happens, the Talmud Torah will gain the sympathy of all strata of the Jewish population of Będzin. The Talmud Torah will be a model for all of Poland; and if you again make use of the manipulations used until now, all the "zasshtshikes" [?] will help like cupping-glasses on a corpse, and the 400 poor children will, through you and your children, be unhappy forever, and the whole town will be against you.
Respectfully,
An Orthodox communal worker in Będzin.
(Former staff member of the "Agudah")

A Christian Buried in the Jewish Cemetery in Dąbrowa
[Dąbrowa — crime and community.]
Two weeks ago, as our readers know, a murdered unemployed man, who had wanted to travel to Mysłowice, was found in a coal wagon of a freight train that had arrived from Częstochowa.
The next day a suspicious stranger was noticed in Niwka. The police detained him, and at the first questions he became very flustered [printed "otumlt"]. Besides that, he was wearing clothes of the same material as the waistcoat of the murdered man who had been found. Bloodstains were also found on his clothes... After a strong cross-examination he confessed to the murder he had committed, giving the following gruesome details:
His name is Stefan Chałast [?] from Warsaw, and he is a shoemaker by trade. On 22 November he set out from Warsaw for Zagłębie to look for work. Not having money for a train ticket, he travelled in a coal wagon. In Częstochowa an unknown man got into the same wagon and introduced himself, saying that he too was going to Mysłowice to look for work. On the way Częstochowa — Dąbrowa, Chałast murdered and robbed him and fled to Niwka, where he was arrested.
Meanwhile a rumour spread in Dąbrowa that the tragically deceased man was a Jew. The local Chevra Kadisha, together with a mohel, immediately visited the mortuary at the local hospital where the body lay, and established that the deceased was circumcised. After great efforts with the prosecutor, they finally managed to obtain permission to bury the murdered man in the Dąbrowa Jewish cemetery.
Last Friday a woman presented herself to the Będzin examining magistrate, introducing herself as the murderer's mother and asking for permission to see her son.
The examining magistrate gave her such permission and sent two agents to the prison with the old woman. But how astonished they were when the old woman declared that this was not her son, and that it could only be that the murderer had murdered her son and robbed him of his documents.
She was then shown the photograph of the murdered man. She immediately recognized her son in him.
In connection with this, the board of the Jewish community in Dąbrowa turned to the local rabbi with the question of what to do.
The rabbi declared that as long as the prosecutor does not order the body to be released, the community should do nothing on its part.

Taxes in Kind
[Taxes — economy.]
As is known, the Ministry of Finance has decided that taxes are to be accepted in kind as well. In this connection, the Treasury Chamber announces that taxes can be settled with rye, wheat, barley, potatoes, peas, buckwheat, firewood and in general with all articles that can serve as relief for the unemployed.
In kind, only those tax arrears may be covered whose payment deadline was not later than 31 March 1930.
When tax arrears are settled with consumer articles, the articles are credited at 10 per cent above the market price.
Taxpayers wishing to cover their taxes in kind must submit special declarations to the tax authority, stating with what kind of goods they wish to pay, the quality, how much will be delivered, and also the time and place where the tax authority can collect the goods.
When the payer submits a declaration that he wishes to cover his tax arrears with goods, all distraints that the tax authority has carried out against him for the arrears are suspended.
The 20th of this month is the last date for submitting declarations on taxes in kind to the tax authority.

From the Hanukkah Evening at the WIZO Kindergarten in Będzin
[Będzin — WIZO; Hebrew education; Hanukkah.]
The mothers who send their little children to the Hebrew "Gan Yeladim" (kindergarten) maintained by the women's association "WIZO" spent several merry hours on Tuesday evening together with invited guests, and were delighted by the rich programme "artistically" performed by the little "flowers" nurtured in this "Gan".
The evening opens with a speech of welcome by Mrs. Ratner: at a time of economic suffering and boycott agitation, at a time when the persecutions of Jewish youth do not cease, we celebrate the festival of the Maccabees. And this gives us further courage to fight for our rights until the final goal of the Jewish renaissance.
Then the official part begins: to the sounds of music the little troop marches in, headed by the "commandant", five-year-old Shlomo Strachlic [?], who gives signals when the "little army" is to halt or march on. (The scene had great applause and the audience rolled with laughter.)
Very successful were also the following numbers: 1) the lighting of the Hanukkah candles and the singing of "Hadliku ha-nerot"; 2) the orchestra, which performed several Hebrew songs. Here one could truly appreciate the work of the kindergarten teacher Miss Glinka, who managed to set up such a harmonious orchestra out of such "tiny tots"... Tragic Death of a Girl.
In Katowice a tragic incident befell 11-year-old Elżbieta Funk, a pupil of a gymnasium [secondary school].

Coal Is Getting Cheaper.
Last week a breakthrough in the price of coal took place in Katowice: whereas until now one paid 42 zł. at the mines for a ton of 1000 kilos, the mines have now begun to sell a ton of coal for no more than 25 zł. This is because of competition from England.
