After the Kehilla Elections in Olkusz

[Olkusz — kehilla.] The result of the kehilla elections is a complete victory of the 4 united lists: Zionists, Mizrachi, the People's Union, artisans and non-party religious. — The lists together have a majority of 5 representatives; Agudah with its 3 allied lists suffered a defeat, and after all the election machinations obtained 2 representatives.
The national idea has won; the awareness of the voters overcame all obstacles; whose aim was to bring responsible work for the common good into the kehilla.
M. Sh.
The Labour Inspector's Office in Dąbrowa to Be Abolished

[Dąbrowa — administration.] As is reported, from 1 January 1932, for reasons of economy, the office of the labour inspector in Dąbrowa is to be abolished.
All matters concerning it will be settled, as before, by the labour inspector in Sosnowiec.
Regional conference of the Sosnowiec Chamber of Commerce in Częstochowa.

Last Sunday, on the initiative of the Sosnowiec Chamber of Commerce, a conference of merchants of the Częstochowa district took place in the hall of the fire brigade in Częstochowa.
The conference, in which about 400 merchants took part, is opened by the president of the Chamber, Mr. Gadomski, and the floor is given to the director Dietrich, who delivers a report on the activity of the Chamber of Commerce.
After the lectures on current commercial matters, those assembled submitted a series of proposals which the Sosnowiec Chamber of Commerce is to deal with.
At the conference, among other things, the question of harmful competition, which is now very topical in the trade market, was also touched upon.
A letter to the editor.

In the 'Zaglembier Tsaytung' No. 50, in the report on the presidium elections of the kehilla board in Dąbrowa, it is reported that Messrs. Gutman and Szpilberg read out a declaration that they take no part in the elections, because they do not want to be against the decision of the minister, who annulled the first elections. Reading this, I was disappointed. Is it possible? — I asked myself — is this a dream or reality? Can[?] the above-mentioned gentlemen already go so far from their national postulates? Are they already trampling underfoot that for which all of national Jewry is fighting? How does one say such a thing [—] aloud, that because the minister is against, one sells national honour and bows and kneels before the squire? At most we would have expected this from Agudah representatives, who are reproached for bowing to the 'button' [the uniformed authorities]; but — be appalled, O heavens! — people who supposedly stand at the head of national affairs: this is done by a president[?] of 'Keren Hayesod' and a 'president' of 'Mizrachi'! Have you read the latest article by Dr. Mann, who says that the kehillas must have the same rights as the municipalities and that no minister should interfere in our internal interests! Apparently you, too, are quite sympathetic to paragraph 120..
If you did not agree with the candidates for the presidium, you had the choice not to take part in the elections at all, or at least to put forward your own candidates; but to come and appear publicly with declarations from the Agudah cheder — you have committed 'a wrong that cannot be righted', and it is very desirable that the Zionist Central Committee should learn what kind[?] of national heroes stand at the head of Zionist activity in Dąbrowa.
Respectfully,
Parnas Icchak Mincz.
Arrests for Grabbing Money

Honest existence and deliberate swindles. — To what ruin does the latter lead?
The situation in the country is so tense that fear falls upon everyone; the economic state is so strained that often one can find no way out whatsoever. How many times have we witnessed citizens getting together — be they industrialists or merchants or craftsmen — who worry that there is no one to trade with and no one to work for; on the one hand the competition is enormously bitter, and on the other hand it is so complicated that even with the best will one cannot measure up to it, and yet we see how the most far-reaching offers are taken seriously and are confirmed as capable of delivery.
Those concerned do not understand in what way the person in question will carry out his part, but when some time passes one sees that the transaction was not made in the honest way, so that only thanks to these illegal combinations did he succeed in carrying out his part, which another, wishing to be honest and upright, could not have gone along with. This is thus a kind of speciality: how to fulfil every kind of delivery in a dishonest and indecent manner.
It goes without saying that honest and sound firms cannot compete with such sick combinations, and they must renounce every kind of dishonest dealing. This has led to the most respected solid firms going under, and their place is taken by refined schemers with whom no one can compete.
Whoever cannot calculate and whoever does not understand how all this happens is confronted with a terrible disharmony: how can one sell goods cheaper than at the first source? And how can one manage to hand over the article or the object, in finished form, cheaper than the raw material costs? And here one must come to the conviction that the basis of the trade — that all the circumstances are sick, and that everything is mere swindle and machinations with which no decent and honest firm can compete.
So it is when one sets out on these crooked paths and begins to go downhill. It goes without saying that such a combination, which is through and through built on dishonest foundations, must be radically destroyed root and branch; it is deadly poison for the future, and systematically a state of unheard-of lawlessness is reached.
And yet another dangerous feature can be noticed at the present moment: there are honest citizens, well-calculating merchants and industrialists, who are very careful about giving goods against bills of exchange, and one cannot persuade oneself either that one will get cash, so that even with the best will it comes down to either not trading at all, or else one must accept the bills. Of course in the future one gets no joy from them, and in the end, when drawing up the total, one realises that one has worked through a year with a deficit, and it is self-evident that after several such "fat" years the blessing does not come into the till, and serious talks begin about cutting the budget, about reducing the staff, and one begins to economise wherever one only can; but this seldom helps, since in the case we are in, the economising came too late and the firm is doomed to go under.
Of course the situation then is very uncomfortable, and the way out that could have existed earlier now belongs to the past.
But there is yet another category of trade, and it is one that adopts a broad scale[?], and the volume is so great that everyone is sure the firm is sound and that no blows will harm it; the end, however, is this: after one has prospered for several years on a large scale on all fronts, the great ruin comes, and then experts come along and prove in black and white that the firm was rotten from the very beginning. It turns out that one traded and swindled with dowry money and strove everywhere to acquire a good name in order to be able to take in as many goods as possible and to grab ever larger consignments. Nowadays this is done on a large scale. One advertises, one fills everything and everyone with oneself, the trading world looks all around at the firm with honour and respect. This costs, of course, a great deal of money, but it is done with so much understanding, with so much awareness. There is in it, one may say, so much intelligence that only after the collapse has come can one form an idea of how finely and systematically all this was worked out, and then one sees that it paid to create the good name in order to have open credit everywhere.
One thus arrives at the conclusion that the firm began to operate on its broad scale[?] exclusively in order to have open doors everywhere, which would bring it great benefit then, when the end would have to come.
Of course, as soon as such a big firm crashes, it causes a terrible ruin in the trading spheres and then drags along with it a whole camp of smaller merchants.
It is thus no wonder that people are beginning to look at this problem with full attention, and in the high spheres the question arises whether one should not arrest for deliberate bankruptcies. Of course such deliberate swindles must be rooted out, because they make it impossible to continue the honest economic struggle.
Under the prevailing conditions one must seek means of rooting out that which is so dangerous for the commercial and industrial world, because one sees no future under the lawless conditions in which we are now clamped as if under a kind of spell.
— It must be brought to other forms in present-day life.
R. Let.
The Enumerator.

(A sketch).

At last the census commissioner reached us. A young gymnasium pupil with a whole bundle of questionnaires carries out all the formalities. He tortures, poor fellow, his hearing on the foreign Jewish names. "Toybe" becomes "Talbe", "Feygl" becomes "Kheygl", and so on.

Angry, probably, at the tough mouthful of the Jewish names, the commissioner receives me in a temper. At the item "occupation" — the first conflict. I give myself as a "biuralista" [office clerk]. The commissioner translates it himself: urzędnik "prywatny" [private employee].

— Of course "prywatny", — I remark — Jewish state officials, after all, are not to be found.

The young schoolboy-commissioner considers it necessary to voice his competent opinion: "I tak was za dużo jest" [There are too many of you anyway]...

The listeners grimace even at the contrived "compliment", but forgive him everything, as long as the Yiddish language finds its due.

— "Język ojczysty?" [Mother tongue?] asks the commissioner.

As with one voice everyone states their mother tongue, and they steal a glance to see whether some annoying error has not slipped in by chance...

— Why don't you speak Polish with your mother? — the enumerator puts a blunt question to me.

— And how do you communicate, Mr. Commissioner, with your mother? — I hit back at him with the same question.

— In Polish, of course — he assures me in a confident voice, and adds: "But if I had lived in Germany, I would have spoken German."

So spoke the pure-blooded 100-percent Pole, and I, the superfluous one, the "stranger", have to admonish him:

— If so, we don't think well of you, young man... Your forefathers thought otherwise... They fought fervently and with self-sacrifice against the various oppressors of the Polish language...

With that our "dispute" ended.

M. Poznański.
Heard and Seen.

[Sosnowiec and Będzin — weekly feuilleton.] By Ben Amotz.

A tragedy of tragedies..
Himself a dramatist, a stage director, a "brand name" in the theatre world — and "himself" he cannot direct. He directs various character-type roles, even the "Dukhus"[?] too, and yet, and yet, when he comes to his own "I" he becomes — if I may be permitted to say so — helpless.
Among the nations of the world he is called Andrzej Marek; among us — Mark Arnshteyn, a "meshlnuriger"[?] of flesh and blood, who draws and drinks from our old well. His mission is to acquaint the nations of the world with our culture, a mission of a very high order; but from all his work among "them" he has been left with the mere name
— Andrzej Marek...
And when our Bronkas and Stefas read the poster about Andrzej's lecture, they were more than sure that Andrzej would speak Polish — anything else would hardly be fitting. How could it be otherwise? How can one touch on a part of the Jewish tragedy if not in Polish?.. Above all they — our Polish shmendrikes — were sure that the Polish intelligentsia would be present at the lecture, and why not?
— Andrzej Marek is going to speak, after all!
He himself — Mark Arnshteyn — understood it the same way. But again it must be stressed that the same man, who directs so many plays, has not yet come to the conclusion that when a more frequent[?] "kosher" Andrzej holds a lecture, most of the audience will be our own people; but if the Andrzej happens to have a Jewish background, he may have the greatest merits for Polish culture, he always remains, for them,
— Andrzej the Zhid [the Jew, pejorative]...
This well-known "secret" the esteemed lecturer only "discovered" in Będzin during his talk at the "Nowości".
— "I thought — he said (after the majority had demanded that he speak Yiddish) — that there were some non-Jews in the hall, for whom one must speak in their language so that they understand the content of my subject. But when I find myself only among our brethren, the children of Israel, I am of course very glad to speak in the language of my fathers, in the language which is dear and precious to me"...
These honest words, however, aroused great displeasure among some of the Polish-babblers, who had only just come away from their Sabbath tables, had greatly enjoyed a "feygem"[?] cholent — and here they pleaded with entreaties
— Po polskiemu [in Polish]...
But Mark Arnshteyn does not hold with "follow the majority", and in a truly Jewish manner he sat down and told of sayings of the Sages, aggadot and jokes — even, as he himself said, "bearded jokes"; but the main thing was that "the humour of the Jewish tragedy" was conveyed in the Jewish language, because to speak on a Jewish theme to a Jewish audience in a foreign language is truly a tragedy, or better said
— a tragedy of tragedies...

An old-new story.
In the premises of the Sosnowiec "Mizrachi".
The big hall is full of Jewish poverty. Half-naked, huddled children have come here for the shoes and coats being distributed by the society "Malbish Arumim" [Clothing the Naked].
The distribution takes place in a very modest manner. The management — incidentally, well-known Sosnowiec activists — works faithfully and is content with its mission of clothing poor Jewish children.
In a side corner stand 2 boys, very young indeed, with faded, pale little faces, dressed in little coats (zhupitses) that do not fit them — children of an exiled people...
— Who are they? I ask one of the activists.
— These are children of a very[?] respectable family. The father, "neyerer"[?], was ashamed to approach us even by letter, asking us to clothe his children.
— Well?
— They are not registered, but even so we will not let them leave without shoes, little coats and other things.
— You see the number of recipients here?
— a second activist speaks up — Here there is not even 50 percent of the number who come to us for clothing. But we unfortunately have to refuse them, because we have no funds; our income from the town is very small — there are no means.
— And where are the rich Jews? After all there are some rich Orthodox Jews in Sosnowiec — how do they fulfil the commandment of "clothing the naked"?
— About the rich Jews? Let me tell you a short anecdote:
When a storm broke out at sea, the passengers on the ship, wishing to lighten the ship's load, began throwing the luggage-bundles into the sea; only the Jewish passengers threw in first the bundles in which the tallit and tefillin were...
That — says the narrator — is what the Sosnowiec rich men do too: when the gmina burdens them with large budget[?] sums, they vent their anger on the institutions and stop paying their monthly dues...
If that is still too little for you, I will show you the "gift" of a local rich man who plays a big role in Orthodox circles, a whole "yesh" [a man of great wealth].
And they show me a few metres of cloth of the commonest sort; connoisseurs say that a metre of this cloth is worth at most 70 groszy — and this great Hasidic magnate donated no less than 4 and a half metres of such cloth to clothe poor children for the winter...
— It's no news to me — I tell them — it is
— an old-new story...

The "Desperate One"..
— Who would have counted on it? To whom could it even have occurred?
With this preamble a young man comes into the editorial office, repeating the words without stopping:
— Who would have counted on it?
— What has happened to you? — we ask him — Has your wife left you?
— No, not that.
— Has the sequestrator [tax bailiff] emptied your shop?
— Not that either.
— Then what? What has made you so worked up?
— Will you hear me out? Yes? Then I will tell you how nowadays one cannot have any "fun".
And he tells:
Reading in the newspaper that the Sosnowiec Revisionists were organising an Eretz-Israel ball, I danced for joy — why not? Grab a little dance and at the same time do a good deed?...
I could hardly wait for the day of the ball; I hurried to be among the "first ten" and off I went to the ball...
But as soon as I stepped over the threshold my head began to swim; I saw before me the whole "Gehenna" into which I had landed for my sins... Straight away I was dragged along by a tangle of people, flung from one end of the sling to the other, shoved about; it hurts me, and
— they laugh at me... Stand aside, I hear a voice calling to me, don't get in the way, there's no room...
— Well, what do you want from us?
— "I have come to the editorial office so that the editors will come out with a protest in the paper: why was I not allowed to dance? How can it be? I paid for a ticket to Dęblińska[?] and had to run after midnight looking for a place where my feet could do their exercises?...
— Truly a scandal"...
"The Offensive on the Złoty"

Of those who, on reading this heading, had a moment's fright, thinking that it has, God forbid, something to do with some currency speculation, with a crash on the stock exchange, or with any other trouble from those fields — I beg pardon. I declare openly that this is not my trade, and I would not have undertaken to devote a few lines to such a question.
This złoty, against which an offensive is now under way, is a reincarnation of that "Gilgul of a Rouble" ("Transmigration of a Rouble") which David Frischmann once described so aptly with his sarcastic pen. There are surely some who either never read that piece at all, or read it and forgot it. It will therefore be worth giving them the gist of "The Gilgul of a Rouble".
"I am afraid," writes David Frischmann there, "that the Jew understands of course that I mean here the kind of Jew who has already risen to the rank of being one of the givers — he actually has only one rouble, which he has consecrated and which he truly gives to every spiritual cause, to every communal matter. But each time it is the same rouble, his only son, that dances at all the weddings. A second rouble, a new rouble from the purse, the Jew does not give; it is the same rouble that appears to us every time in another incarnation. To the Jew it actually makes no difference for what purpose he gives; he only needs to discharge as quickly as possible the duty that lies upon him — to give. Whoever comes to him first takes the rouble from him first. A Jew gets up in the morning with his rouble in his purse and is ready to throw off the 'yoke' of giving, so as to fulfil his duty to his Jewishness or to his humanity, and it is only by chance who will be the first to open his door."
Since the time "The Gilgul of a Rouble" was written, the rouble — now the złoty — has taken on an entirely different face. Or — to put it in David Frischmann's style — it has gone through various incarnations. Nowadays the Jew who has still remained at the rank of a giver is no longer master of his złoty, and the name "giver" no longer suits him, for it is not he who gives — rather, it is taken from him, and simply by force, by various tricks, by various means. So we need not be surprised when we hear that So-and-so gave such-and-such a sum for this or that purpose, from which, by his spirit, he is as far as east is from west; for it was not he who gave of his own good will, out of conviction — rather, it was taken from him. They pressed him. They forced him; it is the old "kofin li-tsedaka" (charity enforced by compulsion), only in different clothing.
An offensive along the whole front is now under way against this złoty. The number of those lying in wait for it grows from day to day; no sooner does the Jew get up from his sleep and go out into the street than he immediately runs into the emissaries who are appointed to get the złoty out of him. Various tricks, various means have these appointees devised so that the rouble should fall as quickly as possible into their hands and not into anyone else's. Indeed it often comes to a war between these emissaries over who shall conquer the złoty first. Often they come to an alliance, and then a whole coalition marches against the poor złoty.
And like an enemy who treats the population of an occupied country brutally, the złoty-conquerors often treat its former owner. He is forced to wear a patch on his shoulders all day long and to proclaim the conqueror's slogans (in today's public activity this is called a "badge sale").
But that is not the only punishment the złoty-conquerors have devised for the defeated złoty-owner. After the victors have already attained their aim and the złoty is already in their pocket, the złoty-owner is forced to listen all night to a screeching jazz orchestra, or to dance all night.
In a word, a whole penal code with countless paragraphs has been created for this unfortunate from whom one can still extract a złoty for a public purpose; and if such a one dares to argue with those who took the złoty from him, as our father Abraham once argued, "Give me the persons, and take the goods for thyself" — you have already taken the złoty from me, so leave me in peace, don't force me to proclaim your slogans on my shoulders all day long; I forgive you your music, my feet are not inclined to dance —
"No," they tell him, "you have given money, and you will get punishment as well."
So the poor giver stands, the wretch, in the whirl of today's countless collections, levies, relief campaigns, rescue campaigns and "ktam" [?] campaigns, which are carried out day after day to save the barely-breathing institutions — like a helpless man attacked from all sides who is at his wits' end.
With longing the giver recalls former times, when everyone who was able to give a złoty for a charitable purpose was himself master of that złoty. He could give it to whom he wanted and for the purpose dearest to him, and one did not know of so many charity [printed "arke"] societies, cultural, philanthropic and social institutions; and in the heart of this giver a silent prayer rises — to be rescued as soon as possible from the "Offensive on the Złoty".
A. L.
A Hasidic Shtibl or a Kehilla?

This week I happened by chance to be in the private flat of a respected Jewish citizen of the town. There were guests there, people from various circles, but in all truth one must admit that they were progressive people, people from those circles who carry on their shoulders 75 per cent of the burden of the community (gmina) budget, and if a death is fated — the community wishes it first of all on these very circles... for here, after all, they "sweeten" [i.e. overcharge for] the burial plots.
Among those present there happened to be a member of the kehilla board, and he showed everyone the preliminary budget of the kehilla for the year 1932.
People looked, read, and did not believe their own eyes.
Is this supposed to be a document of a kehilla, which ought to be the protector and administrator of the entire Jewish community of the town?
Surely the kehilla can understand first of all that even rubber, if you stretch it too far, also bursts. The budget list cannot be stretched any longer. It must now be reduced, and reduced considerably, otherwise the bailiffs and sequestrators will get more out of the community budget than the kehilla itself; and if that should require cutting the expenses in the budget, everyone will agree to it. But one must absolutely remain honest and just. One may not argue like that wolf to the other, weaker animals: one share is due to me because I helped catch the lamb; one share is due to me because I am the strongest; a third share is due to me because that is what I want; and the fourth share is indeed yours — but just try and take it...
The projected preliminary budget says, as it were between the lines, the following:
You heretics (apikorsim) complain that the budget is too high? On the contrary: we shall make it smaller — only we shall strike out "your" hospice (Linat Holim), "your" libraries, "your" schools, "your" "HaZamir", your evening courses and children's homes — and now, what do you like better: toothache or burning wax on your head?
As mentioned above, the first "greeting" from this "righteous" preliminary budget was received in a private home where, as it happened, there were people from various circles and of various views. People literally clutched their heads, and from various sides there came short, clipped but very telling exclamations:
It's high time to think about a separate kehilla!
It goes without saying that these are not realistic outcries. One may not and need not think that way. But the outcries are justified and tell of moods that may ripen more and more, and then people will easily see where it can lead when one wants to run a Jewish kehilla on such an unfair principle: that the "apikorsim" should pay and only "our own people" (anshei shlomeinu) should benefit.
A kehilla is not a Hasidic shtibl.
A. Szwarcer.
The Sanctity of Rent.

Lately the prices of a number of goods have fallen. But earnings have fallen even more. People must now make a living on earnings that are 25 to 50 per cent smaller than a year ago (apart from the sort of people who earn nothing at all). But one expense has remained untouched. That is the rent.
The situation is easier with large flats. Here the landlords already have to bend a little. If not on the price, then at least in that they sometimes agree to take the rent in bills of exchange (weksle).
And here an interesting question has arisen. The tenant gives a bill of exchange and receives from the landlord a receipt (kwit) stating that he has paid the rent. But what is the law when the tenant (lokator) lets the bill be protested? When is the rent considered paid — on handing over the bill, or on paying the bill?
There have already been many disputes in this connection. The court has ruled that from the moment the landlord issued a receipt for the rent paid, he has already lost the right to eviction. So the tenant let the bills be protested? Then the protest is a debt, which the landlord may claim from him by all legal means — but evicting him from the flat, that he may not...
The landlords, however, argue that when they take rent in bills of exchange, they write explicitly on the slip that the sum was settled with bills, and if even one bill goes to protest, the receipt is no receipt.
Będzin Trousers and Czech Shoes

[Będzin — feuilleton, economic crisis.] By I. G. Sztejnsapir.
A strange encounter — Będzin trousers with Czech shoes...
One would think: where is Będzin and where is Czechia? But when it's fated, people meet.
As our sages say: "A mountain doesn't meet a mountain, but"... a pair of trousers with a pair of shoes.
And don't think they met somewhere in Karlsbad, Franzensbad or Marienbad, where a Będzin Jew had come to take a cure, and, "to recoup expenses," bought himself a pair of Czech shoes, which thus had the honour of meeting his Będzin trousers...
Nothing of the sort;
First, you must not forget that most Będzin Jews are now in such a state that does not allow them to travel to spas — unless they go without trousers...
And second, if there are indeed a few Jews who can afford it, they have wives, after all, and when it comes to going to a spa, the wife always comes first...
No, the encounter between the Będzin trousers and the Czech shoes took place in quite a different way:
As is well known, until now we used to manufacture trousers for England. But John Bull recently changed his mind and...
So our underpants fell victim to the "English disease" and set off back to Poland.
Arriving at the Polish border, they met there a shipment of Czech shoes, which greeted them with a broad shalom aleichem.
— Where are so many underpants coming from, no evil eye?
— We went to England, and they would not let us in. The Conservatives now sit on the benches there, and they hate proletarian underpants. "Proletarians," they say, "can manage without trousers. A shirt on the body is enough, like Gandhi"...
— So where are you heading now?
— Back home to Zagłębie.
— To Zagłębie? — the shoes rejoiced. — That's just splendid. We'll have company on the way; we're going there too.
On hearing that the shoes were also going to Zagłębie, the underpants goggled their eyes.
— Are you mad, or out of your minds? What will you do there?
— We'll help the public crawl in the mud...
— Excuse us, with us people lie in the mud even without you.
— Then we'll help them crawl out.
— Who's asking you? — the trousers boiled over. — Zagłębie has enough troubles of its own. Because England won't let us in, the poor tailors are left without work, and now...
— Now — the shoes laughed cynically — to the few thousand tailors will be added a few thousand shoemakers. If unemployed, all should be equal: "szewcy i krawcy" [shoemakers and tailors]..
— You're still being clever — the trousers lost their temper and began to quarrel hard with the shoes — Czech puppets..
— Brzeziny[?] rags — the shoes didn't want to be left without an answer — better shut your mugs, because we'll give one wink to your Polish government, and it won't let you back into the country...
— Who? You? To our government?
— Yes, yes, don't be amazed. With your government we are bigger operators than you... The Polish government is not the English one, that it should bother with such "foolishness" as protecting home production...
At this the trousers could no longer control themselves. Not only did their patience burst, but they began to burst altogether... And they resolved to send a delegation to the management of the customs house, so that it would not let the Czech shoes across the border.
But when the delegates entered the customs house, they couldn't believe their own eyes — not one of the officials wore home-made trousers, but they all wore Czech shoes...

Why Are Polish Jews Silent?

By Shabtai Weiss (Tel Aviv).

IV.
Thus will the period of rule of Sir [John] Chancellor be described: as the darkest, bloodiest, most wicked stretch of time in the history to date of the building of Jewish Palestine. And now, when the new High Commissioner has arrived in Palestine, we are not waiting for any declarations and statements from his mouth. We know that if "language was created only to cover up and disguise thought", then the declarations of sympathy for Jewish Palestine on the part of English High Commissioners and some statesmen were created only in order to cover up their plans of destruction of, and assault on, our work in Palestine. We now look reality straight in the eye. And the reality in Palestine now, after the fall of Passfield and after the departure of Chancellor, is a Passfield-Chancellor one. And one sees no signs whatsoever of creating a different reality, favourable to us. MacDonald's well-known letter to Professor Weizmann was, it appears, thrown straight into the waste-paper basket by the Palestine administration. In his letter MacDonald laid down the just principle that in all government and municipal works the Jewish worker must get his share according to the proportion of the Jewish participation in taxes; that would have meant roughly fifty per cent of all government works. In reality, however, the Jerusalem municipality builds roads and buildings for tens of thousands of pounds a year, with funds in which the Jewish taxpayer participates not with fifty but with eighty per cent — and the Jewish worker, on top of that, has literally no access at all.
For the half-year October 1931 – April 1932 the English government generously consented to give the Jewish Agency... 350 certificates. When one takes into account that the Jewish Agency holds 1400 requests from inhabitants of the country to bring over their relatives, for whom they will provide in any case, and that on the basis of an exact, cautious calculation the Jewish Agency requested 1720 certificates for workers to whom it guarantees work immediately, and that the Jewish calculation did not include various employment opportunities in plantations and house-building by private initiative — then one understands that the paltry number of 350 certificates for a period of six months is a cynical joke at the expense of Zionism.
Before our eyes the Mufti is preparing a Muslim World Congress, which is taking place in Jerusalem. With blood libels against the Jewish people — that it is a mortal enemy of the Mohammedan religion (this is stated explicitly in an appeal by the Hebron Arabs in Cairo), that it plans to carry out an attack on the Mosque of Omar in Jerusalem in order to build the Temple in its place, that it plans to drive all the Arabs out of Palestine — with this poisonous incitement the Mufti and his gang are arranging the Muslim World Congress, and the Palestine government tolerates it and grants permission for this congress. With exactly the same incitement motifs the Arabs operated two years ago and thereby prepared the bloody events, and the government is silent, and pays the Mufti a salary from the government treasury.
The Palestine police was reorganised after the events. The former police chief had to tender his resignation. The demand to allow the Jewish Yishuv to arm itself was not fulfilled, and we were assured that once the police had been reorganised this was no longer necessary. And lo, after the reorganisation of the police, the three halutzim of Yagur were shot dead ten minutes' walk from Haifa, and near Herzliya Yohanan Stahl and Selia[?] Zohar were [brutally?] murdered. It was not the reorganised police that found their dead bodies, nor was it the police that discovered the traces of the murderers — only private Jewish colonists from Petah Tikva and from Herzliya managed to do what is the duty of every well-equipped police force. And the murderers of Yagur have not been discovered by the "reorganised" police to this very day...

V.
Against the Passfield-Chancellor reality in Palestine we say that we will change this reality in our favour only through a forceful, aggressive Zionism, which will develop a courageous, powerful political activity throughout the whole length of the Jewish lands of the Diaspora. The way of Ireland cannot be our way. The way of negotiations by this or that member of the Zionist Executive with this or that English official, in the manner and spirit in which they have been conducted over the last years — that is a new incarnation of the old, bygone "Ma Yafit". Strong, shaking political actions, aimed at unmasking before the whole world the hypocrisy of the English Mandate policy in Palestine, aimed at breaking the political line that England has marked out for itself with regard to the building of the Jewish home — must be conducted permanently and purposefully[?], and not only when in Hebron and in Motza women and children, halutzim and rabbis are slaughtered. And the broad Jewish popular masses, the bearers of shame and mockery, living in various lands of exile — those who are constantly pushed out of their economic positions, those whose children are beaten at various universities and for whom the numerus clausus exists at almost all universities — they, the broad strata of the people, must push their leaders onto the path of a great political offensive for the building of Jewish Palestine.
And therefore the question arises: why are Polish Jews silent? The community of three million Jews in Poland, for whom Palestine is not a "halakhah for the days of the Messiah", not music of the future, but a real, bloody question of life, which could — given appropriate immigration conditions — settle and root in Palestine tens, tens of thousands of their brothers, who under the present conditions in Poland are condemned to economic ruin. Why does this Jewish community sit as if with folded hands, why does it not bring a revolutionary impetus into the backward political work for the building of the free, independent Jewish home in Palestine?
Why are you silent, Polish Jews? —
How Does the Zagłębie Merchant, Shopkeeper and Artisan Live? / What Does a Haberdashery Shopkeeper Say?

I am in a haberdashery shop on Modrzejowska Street in Sosnowiec. The shop is empty. During the hour in which I held the conversation with the shopkeeper, not a single customer came in.

Right at the first question the shopkeeper complained that Modrzejowska Street, which a few years ago was the only commercial street, has now died out completely. Above all, several new bazaars have been opened, and both those who come from Upper Silesia and the town's own residents go there to buy. Of Modrzejowska Street only the outward glitter has remained.

— What is the situation in the haberdashery trade in general?

— The general turnover has shrunk, compared with last year, by almost half. The main reason for this is that the officials' salaries have been cut by 15 per cent. Most of the buyers of the better haberdashery articles are the officials. The ordinary, everyday Jew makes do with cheaper kinds and wears one necktie, or two, a year.

Besides that, the turnover has also shrunk because of the fall in prices, which amounts to 20 to 40 per cent. Above all the prices of neckties have fallen; they cost 50 per cent less than two years ago. Knitwear has fallen by 15 per cent.

— What kinds do people buy?

Nowadays the demand is only for cheaper things. Instead of asking, as people once used to, for the best possible qualities, today they ask for the cheapest possible. There are very few willing to pay 10—12 zł. for a necktie, or 10 zł. for ladies' silk stockings. A good necktie can be bought today for 5—6 zł., a pair of silk stockings for 4—5 zł. But even for that there are no customers. People want it cheaper still.

— How are the earnings?

— Before the war there was a small number of haberdashery shops in Sosnowiec; today there are dozens of shops, and in addition peddling is very widespread, carrying the haberdashery goods around from house to house.

All this has created competition in the trade; one sells at the minimal profit. On 'Jaeger' [woollen underwear; ?] one earns 20—25 groszy on a piece of linen; a pair of galoshes costs the shopkeeper himself 7 zł. and he sells it at 7.30 zł. a pair. With knitwear goods things are no better either. Knitwear manufacturers have become fewer. The small number of manufacturers who remain therefore dictate the prices.

In this trade there is one more drawback concerning sales: the public constantly demands novelties, and in this way leftover goods pile up on the shopkeeper's shelves.

Because of this the shopkeeper has to reduce his turnover. He does not have so much money that he could keep stocks of goods lying, which in time lose their value entirely.

In general the shopkeeper has become very impoverished; there are no large, well-founded shops as there used to be. Even the wholesalers do very small turnovers, because the manufacturers send travelling salesmen around the provincial towns, so that the small-town shopkeeper no longer needs to come to the bigger city.

In a week's time — a conversation with a draper (textile shopkeeper).

Y. R. T.

Our Answer to the Enemies of the Jews

[Essay — antisemitism and a Jewish answer; plus the banner across the top of the page for the "Linas HaCholim" jubilee.]
By Efraim Kapłan.

We are a "goy elyon", a super-people. We possess great, spiritually great intellectual powers, and the treasury of our moral and spiritual qualities is relatively much, much richer than that of the other nations.

In the present dark, cruel time, when many of us go about with broken spirits and stand on the threshold of despair, seeing how almost the whole world has stormed up and seethed with murderous hatred against us — precisely at this time it is necessary to stress this fact.

A people with such virtues cannot perish and has no right to be downcast and to look with dark eyes at the future, even when its present is as black, as terribly sad, as the one we are now living through.

Should someone, a sceptic, or a Jewish-radical cynic who finds special pleasure in "running down" Jews and belittling them — should such a one claim "it never happened", that the fact is no fact and that this assertion is nothing more than the product of chauvinist imagination, we shall trouble him to take a stroll through the camps of our enemies, who breed the Judeophobic incitement and wave the pogrom sword over Jewish heads. Let him hear what they say, what they say about us. Then he will have to come to the same conclusion as we.

Like Balaam in his day, every Jew-baiter naturally sets out from the start with the exclusive intention of cursing us, of besmirching [?] us with the most shameful insults. But as soon as he opens his mouth he says "Ma tovu", he hails praises upon us and depicts us as the cream of humanity. He presents us as the greatest sages in the world, as the strongest heroes and the highest talents.

He means it, of course, as a reproach. He shouts that we use our wisdom, our strength, our talent to harm others, to destroy the world. But the bottom line remains that we are, even from his hostile, mortally [?] hateful standpoint, cleverer, mightier and more talented than all the nations on earth.

The Polish "Endeks", the bearers of extreme Polish chauvinism, who hold, it seems, that the Polish people is one of the cleverest, most capable and also strongest peoples, nevertheless cry "help!" that Jews are seizing Poland, that Jews are turning the state into a heap of ruins. The donkeys that they are, they do not grasp what a wild contradiction lies between their wild patriotic pride and their claim about Jews. The Jews in Poland number barely three million souls, and the Endeks tremble and flutter before this unarmed little Jewish handful. Well, shouldn't they hide for great shame?

The Hitlerites, the German "Nazis", who are saddling up to seize the government with the tactic of stirring up the German "Thou hast chosen us"; of re-sowing the old pre-war faith in "Deutschland über alles"; and who, forgetting, or pretending to forget, the great defeat which that blind and blinding faith suffered only just now in the bloody conflict, speak with wild impudence, threaten a new war of revenge that will defeat and annihilate all of Germany's former victors — these great braggarts [?] are not ashamed, in their very wildest bluster [?], to point their fingers at the half-million Jews and to scream "help!" against the Jewish danger. You see the logic: of France, of England, of Japan, of Italy, of America — of all the mighty peoples together, who broke Germany's horns, they are not afraid. Against those they have strength enough to stand up, but of the half-percent of Jews they are afraid indeed. That little percent does not let them fall asleep, hangs like a nightmare over their heads, lifts them out of their beds, throws them into a panic, stirs up their brains, and like mad dogs they hurl themselves to bite the Jew.

So it is clear that we really are a wonder-people, that it is not merely we who have imagined it, but that the whole world believes it with perfect faith.

No nation as small in number as we has ever played, or can ever play, such a role as ours. It has not had and cannot have so many and such embittered enemies as we have had and have.

The miniature little nations of our kind have always been rendered negligible ("batel be-shishim") among the populous gigantic nations. Nobody took any notice of them. They were placed beneath criticism. It was considered beneath one's dignity to speak of them, to laugh at them, to censure them, and certainly not — to base state policy on hatred of them. When it was found necessary to clear them out of the way, it was done without long deliberation, and — off the stage.

With us the story was, and is, exactly the reverse. Small as we may be, we have been given since ancient times a "place" at the eastern wall of the peoples. People always reckoned with us not only as with an equal, but [misprinted "nayr"] as with one who has an advantage over everybody. The most gigantic people saw in us a fearsome rival, and the shadow of the tiny Jewish little nation pursued it and cast terror upon it.

The first antisemitic Torah portion begins with "Come, let us deal wisely". Pharaoh, of Moses' time, the mightiest king of the mightiest and cleverest primeval people, trembled before the handful of Jews who slaved for him and kneaded clay.

And he felt that with all the wisdom and power that Egypt possessed, it was not mighty and clever enough to suppress Jewish spiritual genius, Jewish brilliance. So he ordered his magicians and sages to gird their loins, to sharpen their brains and to invent new devices for fighting the Jewish danger.

But exactly so read all the antisemitic portions of all generations and all times, right up to our own time and — he in general.

No antisemite and enemy of any real importance has spoken of us with disdain or with real contempt. His tone may indeed have been contemptuous, and he did indeed think that the bitter words, the wicked expressions, smear Jewish honour in the mud, but at bottom they were nothing more and nothing less than fine compliments and songs of praise, which excited and further stimulated the patriotic pride of the proudest people.

And the brand-new antisemitic portion too, which began with the great "world-liberating" war and gathers more momentum with every day, has the same plain meaning with the same Rashi.

The most gigantic nations of our time mobilised fabulously huge armies, with the most effective instruments of murder that ever existed. Each one of these nations had the power to destroy a thousand such small, weak peoples as we. Yet fear of the Jews pursued them.

The common denominator of both elements — of those who attacked us mercilessly and of those who tenderly stroked us and fed us sweet promises — is that both regarded us as a tremendously strong power.

And if we are heroes, champions — and if we really are such in reality — then we have, as a matter of course, the full right to hope for an honest victory.

Theatre Notes.

„Hiszpańska mucha“ [„The Spanish Fly“], a comedy in 3 acts, staged at the Sosnowiec Municipal Theatre.
„Hiszpańska mucha“ belongs to those comedies in which the author has one aim: to provoke strong and incessant laughter in the audience. He introduces no thought or idea whatsoever into his work, he does not rest on social conditions and does not care about logical consistency and connection between all the scenes and moments he brings onto the stage. Nevertheless the comedy possesses a whole series of conflicts, misunderstandings and coincidences, which very often border on the improbable. The author does not want to appear in the role of a moraliser or propagandist of ethical and social postulates. He does not use the pen or the stage to teach; he only wants to make the audience merry, so that it laughs and forgets the everyday worries and cares — and in this he succeeds beyond reproach. The actors' parts are so well fitted that they need not exert themselves much in order to play well. We must specially mention Mr. Tański, who has more than once shown that he possesses a great artistic culture. Very charming was Mrs. Sobotkiewina[?]. Mr. Bem understood well what kind of figure the author wants to make of him. Recognition was earned by Messrs. Polański, Archan[?] and Gałaszewski[?] in the role of a naive provincial young man.
Elge.

Parsha
a) Then Judah came near unto him (44:18)
Rav Simon said: In our laws [nimusin] it is written „if he have nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft“, and this one has [means] (Midrash Rabbah).
Once the Dubno Maggid was asked about this wondrous midrash: is it understandable of Judah that, when he questioned Joseph, whom he took for an Egyptian, about the Jewish Torah — what interest would the Egyptian viceroy have in „our laws“?
And they persuaded him to answer it without a parable...
The Maggid answered on the spot:
„If he have nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft“ is not merely a statute [beyond reason] but also an understandable law, although at first sight one asks: who will buy a thief, who will surely steal from him too?... In truth, however, a man steals only out of need. If he is sold and will have something to eat, he will no longer steal.
This is what Judah argued: Benjamin is a rich man's child, and if he did steal the goblet, it was not out of need but out of a criminal inclination; and if so, why do you keep him with you? He will surely steal from you...
Ohel Yaakov.
b) That it is my mouth that speaketh unto you (45:12)
In the holy tongue (Rashi)
Joseph feared that when the brothers told Jacob that he was an Egyptian viceroy, Jacob would think: ah, who knows how he stands there with his Jewishness..! So Joseph commanded him [sic]: Know that I speak Hebrew, and this is the best sign of my attachment to our tradition.
And from this, writes further the famous Gaon Rav Yosef Shaul Nathansohn, „one must draw a moral for our times, when people are disgusted with Hebrew so that[?] they can get along as gentile-speakers [lo'azim], may God have mercy“.
Divrei Shaul.
———
„Holy Jews! We are ashamed of you, how you have forgotten your holy, dear language! How great is the virtue of the holy tongue, that it brings near the salvation and the redemption!
„For our many sins the Hebrew language has become with us like an old-maid bride, insulted and withered, and nobody takes it to heart to speak a pure, genuine Hebrew.
Rav Yehonatan Eybeschütz (Yaarot Dvash).
———
Yiddish is the curtain [parochet] that guards the Holy Ark, the Torah and the holy tongue, so that strange dogs[?] shall not penetrate to them..
Rabbi Yisroel Chiedlinker[?].
c) See that ye fall not out by the way (45:24)
Do not quarrel on the way — do not occupy yourselves with a matter of halacha (Rashi).
Why did Joseph instruct them on the way back not to quarrel over learning, and Jacob did not on the way here?
Because on the way here they went hungry. Jacob knew that they would have no head to dispute in learning... „Where there is no flour there is no Torah“... Now, going back with sacks of grain, Joseph was indeed afraid that they might feel like a bit of pilpul.
Sefer HaChaim.
———
A folk saying puts it the other way round:
„Something is missing, and this is how it should read“ [chasurei mechasra vehachi katani] — a Jew studies only when his pocket is empty...
d) I will go down with thee into Egypt; and I will also surely bring thee up again (46:4)
When going into exile God says: I will go down with you — you, Israel, will go and I will go along. The Shechinah is in exile with us. But at the redemption it is not said „I will go up with you“, for the Jews will not want to go out; „I will bring you up“ — God will have to pull them out by force. You will be redeemed even if you do not want it...
Nachalat Yaakov.
———
The redemption will come when the Jews' hearts awaken and they say: is it good for you to dwell[?] outside, driven from your father's table? Do you have any pleasure from your life in a strange land? — And the great men of Israel will have to give an account of this to the Almighty, and from them He will demand the shame of the insulted House.
Or HaChaim.
e) And Joseph made ready his chariot (46:29)
It is truly a rarity that when a child is so exalted, so rich, he should rush so to his old father, harnessing the wagon for him himself. Usually when one is so elevated, one is ashamed of one's old father...
To'aliyot HaRalbag.
f) Wherefore shall we die before thine eyes (47:19)
Before, when we became poor, we were also like dead men — „a poor man is considered as dead“. But now, when we are starving, „we shall die before you“ [so printed] — we will really die; not be called dead, but simply die...
Be'er Yitzchak.
Haftarah: Ezekiel 37.
g) And join them one to another (37:17)
The symbolic sticks mean Messiah son of Joseph and Messiah son of David, and to unite even the two Messiahs one needs prophetic power... That is how hard a bit of unity comes among Jews, even between Messiahs...
Ahavat Yehonatan.

In a Crisis the Public Doesn't "Immerse"...

[Będzin — municipality / bathhouse.] From the magistrate we have received the following statistics on the number of persons who used the municipal bathhouse in the months of October and November.
In the month of October the establishment was used by 4446, and in November by only 3665 people.
Of that number, 2180 people used bathtubs, and the rest sweated [in the steam bath]...
The Talmud Torah Melamdim Are Already Getting Tuition Pay..

[Będzin — community / Talmud Torah.] The great to-do of the committee to put the Talmud Torah back on its feet has stopped. The pledges (nedarim) campaign has been completed, and, as we are informed, the melamdim (teachers) already received their salaries last Friday. Each melamed was paid a sum of 9 (nine) zł.
Heavy Penalty for Not Redeeming a Cheque

In the local municipal court a trial took place last Tuesday [15 December 1931] against the local merchant Ch. K., who, for a formal reason, did not redeem his own cheque.
Mr. K. was sentenced to pay 500 zł. or a month's arrest.
Bandit Shot Dead While Trying to Escape

The police received information that the long-sought bandit Glen [?] was in Gołonóg. When the police approached the house, the bandit tried to run away.
Then a policeman fired into the air, and when the bandit again did not stop, the policeman fired at the bandit and seriously wounded him.
The next day he died in the local hospital.
Lecture by Dr. Gottesdiener at WIZO

Next Tuesday [22 December 1931] at 8:30 in the evening the 4th entertainment evening will take place at the WIZO premises, with the participation of Dr. Abraham Gottesdiener, who will give a lecture on the topic "The Gallery of Women-Types in the Bible".
Snatched from Her Hand

On Monday [14 December 1931] at about 8 in the evening, as Regina Frenkel was walking along Kościuszki Street, she was attacked by an unknown person, who snatched from her hand a handbag containing 12 zł.
A Discussion Evening at "Mizrachi" / Break-in at the Table Wholesale Store / Session of the Commissarial Council Called Off / The "Family" Grows Smaller / A Theft / Shopping Hours for the Holidays

Next Sunday evening [20 December 1931] a discussion evening will take place at the "Mizrachi" premises. Our attitude to the "Torah va-Avoda" movement [?] with regard to the last Council (Moetza) session will be discussed.
—o—
Break-in at the Table Wholesale Store
In the night from Sunday to Monday [13–14 December 1931] the table warehouse at Małachowskiego 35 was broken into, and a considerable number of tables was taken from it.
—o—
Session of the Commissarial Council Called Off
On Tuesday [15 December 1931] a session of the local commissarial (appointed municipal) council was to take place; at the last minute the session was called off.
—o—
The "Family" Grows Smaller
Dr. Berliński [?] laid down his mandate as a member of the commissarial council this week.
—o—
A Theft
Thieves got into the flat of Mrs. K. Zajdelman and stole various objects and linen.
—o—
Shopping Hours for the Holidays
Next Sunday [20 December 1931] all shops may be open from 1 p.m. to 6 p.m. On the following days until 9 p.m., on Thursday [24 December] until 6 p.m.
Sosnowiec — The Kehilla Council Decides, Not the Board

Between the kehilla board and the council there is no "domestic peace": when the board says "day", the council says "night"...
Because of such a situation the setting of the new budget has been held up, and a plan arose to send 2 budgets for approval, one from the board and one from the council.
In this connection the head of the office reached an understanding on the matter with the starosta, and the latter declared that the budget depends on the final decision of the kehilla council.
Intervention by the Kehilla Concerning Religious Studies at the State Gymnasium

[Sosnowiec — kehilla, education.]
At the beginning of the current school year, religious studies for the Jewish pupils were abolished at the Staszic State Gymnasium.
This week the kehilla board turned to the management of the gymnasium with the request that the religious studies be renewed.
As religion teacher the board recommended Mr. Goldberg.
For Killing His Mother's Lover He Is Sentenced to 6 Months' Imprisonment

[Sosnowiec — court, crime.]
With the Czembrzyński [?] family in Płatków [?] there lived as a sub-tenant the 22-year-old Gawacki. The sub-tenant found favour with Mrs. Czembrzyński, and between the two of them a hot love flared up.
A terrible atmosphere began to reign in the house, constant scandals, which led to the point that at a certain moment the 20-year-old Czembrzyński murdered his mother's lover with a knife.
This week the murderer sat in the dock at the local district court, before which he described what reasons had caused him to commit the murderous deed.
Czembrzyński was punished with 10 months' imprisonment.
The Bandits of the Sadel Affair Caught

[Zagłębie — crime.]
All the bandits who carried out the daring attack on the Sadel family in Zagórze are already in prison.
Shackled in chains, the bandits were brought to the Sadel family, who recognised that they were the attackers.
During the interrogation the bandits confessed that they had taken part in the attack which had been carried out in its time on the Rudschler [?] family on the road from Sosnowiec to Będzin.
Celebration of Clothing Poor Children

[Sosnowiec — charity, community.]
On Saturday night the celebration of clothing a large number of needy children took place in the shul [synagogue].
Some 190 persons from the wealthier circles had been invited to the celebration, but not one of them came.
After the cantor and choir sang “Ma Tovu”, the chairman Mr. Lewi Jungster gave a speech, providing an overview of the activity of “Malbish Arumim” [Clothing the Naked], while at the same time criticising the town's lack of interest, in that none of the “notables” came to the celebration. Messrs. Ruben Binensztok and Josef Dawid Braner also spoke.
Then the cantor held a memorial prayer for the deceased member Glewicki and for those fallen in Eretz Israel. After the singing of the Polish anthem and Hatikvah the celebration was concluded.
—o—
Meir Grossman Comes to Sosnowiec
Next week the vice-president of the Revisionist organisation, Mr. Meir Grossman of London, is coming to Poland. During his stay in Poland he will visit Sosnowiec, where he will appear with a lecture on the present situation in Zionism.
Extraordinary Meeting of the Revisionists in Sosnowiec

[Sosnowiec — Zionism, Revisionists.]
In connection with the 5th Revisionist conference, an extraordinary meeting devoted to the withdrawal from the Zionist Organisation will take place this Sabbath in [the movement's] own premises.
—o—
Trade Licences by the 31st of This Month
We draw attention to the fact that the deadline for purchasing new patents [trade licences] is only until the 31st of December of this year.
Before It Is Finished, It Is Already Falling...

[Sosnowiec — construction, accident.]
On Third of May Street the Chamber of Commerce is building its own building. This week a construction disaster occurred in the not-yet-finished building. The ceiling on the first floor caved in, and all the material turned into dust and sand.
Luckily the disaster happened when the workers were not inside.
Final Result of the Kehilla Elections in Olkusz

[Olkusz — kehilla.] The result of the kehilla elections, which took place last Monday in Olkusz, is as follows: Agudah bloc — list no. 1: 52 votes, no. 5: 22 votes, number 8: 17 votes and no. 10: 43 votes, together 134 votes, 2 seats: Binyamin Eliezer Kan and Avrahamle Faluch. No. 2 People's Union (Folks-fareynikung): 82 votes, 2 seats: Shimon Stark and Yechiel Erlich. No. 3 "Mizrachi": 44 votes, 1 seat: Leibish Jeger. No. 4 Zionists: 58 votes, 1 seat: Moshel Szwarcberg; and no. 6 Artisans: 72 votes, 1 seat: Avraham Glikstein. No. 7 Beit HaMidrash (Avrahamle Kerner's list): 94 votes, 1 seat: Reuven Dafner. The artisans' and the Beit HaMidrash candidates are also Zionists. In all there were 530 eligible voters; 486 voted, i.e. more than 90 percent. The quota was 54 votes. The election campaign was very passionate, and the slogan of both sides was to deal the opponent a death blow. The National bloc fully succeeded in this. It is worth noting that the Rabbi, may he live long, despite his weakness also came to cast his vote and wanted to complete the victory of the Agudah...
A sensation was also the number of votes for Avrahamle Kerner's list, since the greatest optimists had not counted on such a success.
A. B.

—o—

Coal for the Unemployed.

[Będzin district — relief.] The Central Committee for Aid to the Unemployed has allotted to the Będzin county 170 wagons of potatoes, which have already been distributed.
Coal is also being given out from the allotted contingent. Of the 13470 wagons of coal each month, there are designated for Sosnowiec 4,700 korzec, for Będzin 1,800 korzec, for Dąbrowa 1928 and for Czeladź 688 korzec. A small family receives 1 korzec, a larger one — one and a half korzec.
Soon 20 thousand kilos of sugar are also due to arrive, which will be given only to children and the elderly.

—o—

Rabbi Saadia Gaon and His Book Emunot ve-De'ot.

[Będzin — lecture.] On this subject a lecture by Dr. Avraham Gottesdiener will be given this coming Saturday night (motzei Shabbat) in the "Mizrachi" hall.
From Sports Life

[Sport — Upper Silesia.] From the Katowice Ice Rink.

On Sunday an ice-hockey match between the national team of Poland and Upper Silesia took place at the Katowice ice rink. After a fairly interesting fight the Polish team won 1:2. The goals were scored for Poland by Harmiński [?] and for Upper Silesia by Klaszek.
— This Saturday at 8 o'clock in the evening a hockey match will take place at the Katowice ice rink between the well-known Czech "Troppauer Eislaufverein" (Opava skating club) and "Warsaw". The return match will take place on Sunday at half past twelve [printed "half 1 in the morning"]. During the intervals there will be performances by the 9-year-old Putzinger from Vienna, the 11-year-old Holzmann, and also Linhard, who already today has a name in the sports world as skater [?] no. 2.
— On the 27th and 29th two interesting hockey matches will take place at the Katowice ice rink between "Canada", represented by "Anitoba" [= Manitoba], and the Polish national team. After the defeat which the German national team suffered from "Anitoba", the matches are awaited with interest throughout Poland. (Vtki).

A fine deed by the Katowice rabbi Dr. Chameides. / Painting exhibition by a young man from Będzin / Last days to apply for reductions on trade licences / Campaign for the Yiddish secular school system / Accident while skating. / From the “Commerce Section” of the Association of Commercial and Office Employees in Będzin / An entertainment evening at “Hakoach”. / Grand ball of the “Hitachdut”.

A Jew from Będzin, a certain Gdalewicz, was sentenced by the Katowice court to 3 weeks' arrest or a fine of 350 złoty.
Mr. G. therefore turned to a number of Będzin public figures and asked them for any help whatsoever so that he might be freed from the undeserved penalty, but all efforts were without result. And Mr. G. finally decided to serve[?] his sentence.
Arriving in Katowice, G. turned to the local rabbi Dr. Kalman Chameides with the request that Mr. Chameides provide him with kosher food and see to it that he not be prevented from praying every day.
When Dr. Chameides heard this, he paid the 350 zł. fine out of his own pocket, and thereby[?] freed the Jew from 3 weeks' arrest.
—o—
Painting exhibition by a young man from Będzin
As we have already written, the young Jewish artist Abraham Goldkorn, who brilliantly completed his studies at the Royal Institute in Antwerp, has come to his home town Będzin, where he wi[—] hold an exhibition of his oil and zincography pictures.
The exhibition, which opens next Sunday, the 27th of this month, at 12 noon in the hall of “[—]”, Małachowska 35, is under the patronage of Dr[s].[?] Weinzieher, Wassercug, Director Fürstenberg and others.
—o—
Last days to apply for reductions on trade licences
We draw the attention of all merchants and shopkeepers who are entitled to apply for lower trade licences (patents) on the basis of the ministerial circular that there remain only a few days in which to submit[?] applications.
The day after tomorrow, Wednesday, and Thursday are the last days. Whoever has not submitted the application to his office[?] by one o'clock in the afternoon on Thursday will have to buy a regular licence.
The application must state the number of the circular and its date. The number is N. D. U. 2762/4/31, dated 10 November 1931.
—o—
Campaign for the Yiddish secular school system
In connection with the tragic situation of the Yiddish secular school system in Poland, the Central School Organisation is conducting a campaign at home and abroad.
This week such a campaign began in the Zagłębie district. The campaign is led by the well-known school and cultural activist Mr. M. Mendelman. Several conferences have already taken place in Będzin and in Sosnowiec. It is expected that every friend of the Y. Sh. O. (CYSHO) schools will support the campaign.
—o—
Accident while skating.
The 15-year-old Frehlich, while skating on Thursday evening on Third of May Square in Będzin, fell down and remained lying unconscious. In that state he was taken home, where he received medical help. Only the next morning did Frehlich regain consciousness.
—o—
From the “Commerce Section” of the Association of Commercial and Office Employees in Będzin
This Sabbath afternoon a meeting of the manufactured-textiles[?] and ready-made clothing branch will take place in the association's own premises, where very important questions will be discussed, especially concerning the present difficult situation of commercial employees.
The next day, Sunday afternoon — a meeting for the haberdashery and shoe section.
—o—
An entertainment evening at “Hakoach”.
Next Thursday evening an entertainment evening with a very rich programme will take place in the premises of “Hakoach”.
—o—
Grand ball of the “Hitachdut”.
This Saturday evening the Będzin “Hitachdut” is arranging[?] a Land-of-Israel ball with a varied programme. The organisers are endeavouring to create a Jewish atmosphere at the ball; in general it has been organised so that the attractions have a “Land-of-Israel” flavour.
And the main thing? 20 per cent of the proceeds go to the Keren Kayemet. That is, by dancing a “hora” the Keren Kayemet will also benefit...
No wonder, then, that the nationalist youth is preparing so eagerly for the ball.
Edward Nachner.

At the age of 71 there died on Tuesday in Sosnowiec one of the oldest residents, the house-owner and industrialist Edward Nachner.
The deceased was known in the town as an honest man who never refused any social help; for many years he was gabbai of the German synagogue and was respected by all strata of the Jewish population.

Notes of the Week

[Notes of the Week — abroad and Poland.] American students attacked their Jewish fellow students and also threw stones into the dwellings of the Jewish students.
—o—
Because of the Christian holidays the Brest trial was interrupted on Wednesday.
—o—
In a car accident outside Berlin the well-known leader Hitler was slightly injured.
—o—
In Germany a fire broke out in a hall where a children's performance was taking place. A large number of children were seriously injured.
—o—
In Berlin a fire broke out in a palace that is already 10.0[?] years old [probably 100]. The damage is very great.
—o—
The French parliament has adopted a law on protecting French workers against the competition of foreign workers.
The Będzin Kehilla Budget in Figures

[Będzin — kehilla.] (Continued from No. 51.)
Account No. 4 (office[?]).
Salaries for officials: secretary, assistant secretary, cashiers and other officials amount to 15,200 zł. Then the following expenses have been estimated: lighting 460 zł., heating 290[?] zł., telephone 848[?] zł., repairs 800, rent 800, printing and writing materials 200, newspapers and periodicals 380[?], tea and sugar 150 zł. Together 19.358 zł.
Account No. 5 (shechita — ritual slaughter).
For 4 shochtim (ritual slaughterers) a sum of 31,432 zł. has been estimated, i.e. for each shochet an income of 7,791 zł. 67 gr. has been fixed. (Here, however, it should be noted that the shochtim take almost half of the income flowing in from the slaughter.) Then 4 ne'emanim (supervisors): 2 receive 3,600 zł. a year each and 2 receive 2,400 zł. each. Controller 3.300. Then pensions[?] and other expenses, together 51,796 zł. 68 gr.
Account No. 6 (mikveh).
This means the old mikveh. For, as is known, a new mikveh building has already been under construction for several years, in connection with which, as is known, "sensational events" have occurred. But be that as it may, there is hope that in the end the building too will one day be finished...
For the year 1932 a sum of 15[?] zł. has been estimated; besides that 8,500[?] zł. for officials, bill discounting, repairs and other expenses.
(To be continued.)
A Holiday at the "Nowości". / Premiere of "Iber kvorim" (Over Graves)

[Będzin — theatre.] Every premiere of the Będzin "Muza" always arouses great interest.
Especially now, when it[?] has invited the famous artist Abraham Wolfsztat[?] and "Iber kvorim" ("Over Graves") is being staged — his own creation — this performance is doubly interesting. Mr. Abraham Wolfsztat is no new face for us; every one of his appearances here always passes with great success, especially his own creations which he presented: "Broysh", "Harugim" (The Slain) and "Di shlakht" (The Battle), which carried the audience away and are still remembered. And since "Iber kvorim" is Wolfsztat's own creation, the performance is doubly interesting. Wherever "Iber kvorim" has been played, it has passed with great success. "Iber kvorim" [printed "Ibige[?] kvorim"] depicts a piece of Jewish life at the time of the bloody civil war between the "Reds" and the "Whites". We therefore hope that no one will miss the opportunity of such a festive performance, which takes place next Monday at the "Nowości" in Będzin.
Mrs. Widrowicz's Visit to Zagłębie

[Zagłębie — Zionism, JNF.] The visit of the delegate of the head office of the "Keren Kayemet" (Jewish National Fund) in Jerusalem, Mrs. Lea Widrowicz[?], to Zagłębie (Sosnowiec, Dąbrowa, Zawiercie, Będzin) has passed with success. The dunam campaign for the "Bilu colony", which Mrs. Widrowicz conducted in Zagłębie, has so far brought in 6 thousand zł., of which Będzin — thanks to the initiative and full support of "WIZO" — gave over 3,000 zł.
Everywhere, with the participation of Mrs. Widrowicz, jubilee celebrations took place in honour of the 50th[?] anniversary of "Hibbat Zion" and 30 years of the National Fund. Mrs. Widrowicz succeeded in drawing into the dunam campaign also all the Zionist youth organizations and Zionist political parties.
In Sosnowiec the Zionist Organization decided to inscribe in the Golden Book of the JNF the late devoted Zionist activist Israel Moshe Weinreb, of blessed memory. In the week of Tu Bishvat (the fifteenth of Shevat) "WIZO" in Sosnowiec is holding a grand jubilee bazaar for the Keren Kayemet.
—o—
The "Hibbat Zion" Celebration at the Będzin "Gordonia"
The celebration held at the Będzin "Gordonia" last Saturday night (motsei Shabbat) in honour of the jubilee of "Hibbat Zion" and the "Keren Kayemet", as well as in connection with the festive opening of the "Keren Kayemet corner" — passed impressively.
In the presence of over 250 Gordonia members and several invited older national activists, the "celebration" was opened by Mr. M. Hampel, who spoke about the significance of the recent Zionist festivals.
The JNF activist [printed "di KKL askonus"], Mrs. G. Ratner, spoke about the great spirit of self-sacrifice of the pioneering youth for the building of the Land.
The delegate of the JNF directorate in Jerusalem, Mrs. Lea Widrowicz, very warmly depicted her own pictures and fragments of the life of workers in Eretz Israel, and spoke about the spiritual father of working Eretz Israel, A. D. Gordon, of blessed memory, and about the kvutzot "Degania" and "Hulda".
The vice-chairwoman of "WIZO", Mrs. Hutner, expressed sympathy to "Gordonia" for its work for the National Fund.
Mr. Abraham Felberg then announced that the Będzin "Gordonia" is planting 8 trees, in the sum of 108 zł., in the "A. D. Gordon Grove" in memory of the jubilee celebrations.
With "Hatikvah", pioneer songs and hora dances the fine youthful JNF event was concluded, leaving a good impression.
All participants then visited the beautifully decorated premises, where the impressive "corner" is located, in whose making Messrs. Gleter, Hersh Y[—]s and Ferens distinguished themselves.
What's New in Upper Silesia?

[Upper Silesia — short news items.]
Poland Should Give Up the Gold Cover.
On Sunday the third general convention of the trade unions of Moraczewski's group took place in Katowice. Also taking part in the convention were former Premier Moraczewski and Deputies Malinowski, Tomaszkiewicz, Gawlik, Kapuściński[?], Meser[?] and Karyaszka[?].
After the greetings, former Premier Moraczewski took the floor; in his address on the economic situation he pointed out that the greatest burden of the severe crisis falls on the workers.
The speaker further pointed out that most of the industrial plants in Upper Silesia are in the hands of foreigners, so that the profits quickly wander off abroad. What remains is only what the Polish worker draws [in wages].
At the end of his address Moraczewski pointed out that one of the main causes of the present crisis is the shortage of cash. He therefore proposes that the Polish currency should rest on a different basis and not on gold parity.
—o—
Echoes of the Anti-Jewish Excesses in Cieszyn
This week the municipal court in Cieszyn heard the trial of three hooligans who were the chief culprits in the anti-Jewish excesses that took place in Cieszyn a few weeks ago. During the excesses many Jews were beaten, and the windowpanes of the local synagogue were smashed.
After the speeches of the defence counsel, the court sentenced the one who incited the excesses to 4 months in prison, the one who resisted the police to 3 weeks' arrest, and the one who smashed the windowpanes of the synagogue to pay 26[?] zł. or 3 days in prison.
The sentence may be carried out within 3[?] years... [i.e. suspended.]
The defence counsel have filed an appeal.
—o—
An Earthquake.
On Sunday afternoon an earthquake was felt around Katowice.
The earthquake, which lasted 4 seconds, caused no damage.
—o—
German Consul Injured in a Bus Accident.
On the highway beyond Katowice there was an accident involving the car in which the German Consul in Katowice, Mr. Kwiringen[?], the Vice-Consul Dr. Fischer and the court councillor (Gerichtsrat) from Beuthen, Mr. Mitschka, were travelling.
The Consul General was injured on the forehead. Dr. Fischer received severe injuries to his body. Mitschka was lightly injured.
—o—
Visit of Minister Kühn.
On Sunday the Minister of Communications Kühn stayed in Katowice. The minister visited a number of government institutions.
—o—
Barbershops Must Be Closed on Sunday.
A delegation of the barbers' association in Katowice turned[?] to the voivode asking him to permit barbershops to stay open on Sundays and holidays.
The voivode rejected the proposal.
—o—
A Woman Gives Her Blood to Save a Person.
The tenor of the Katowice opera, Marian, suddenly suffered a severe haemorrhage. Because of the great loss of blood the doctors determined that the patient must have an immediate blood transfusion, but nobody was willing to decide to do it. When Mrs. Krajewska learned of it, she announced that she was ready to give her blood for the patient. The transfusion was performed, and thanks to it the artist was saved.
—o—
A Bankruptcy of 80 Million Złoty.
In the financial world tremendous commotion was caused by the news that the largest ironworks in Polish Upper Silesia, „Huta Pokój“, has gone bankrupt. Earlier the firm had been under „nadzór“ (supervision); now its bankruptcy has already been officially declared. The firm owes 80 million zł. This is the largest bankruptcy there has been in Poland to date.
—o—
They Robbed a Restaurant and Murdered the Owner.
In Janowiec[?] [Janów?] on Sunday night a car drove up to a local restaurant; out of it came 5 elegantly dressed young men, who went into the restaurant and ordered a rich meal. After eating they asked for the bill. When the owner bent down to fill out the bill, one of the guests pulled out a revolver and with a single shot laid the restaurateur dead on the spot. Then the „guests“ robbed everything that was in the restaurant and left.
—o—
Correction.
In the last issue of our paper, owing to an oversight on the part of the proofreading, the following regrettable error crept in: instead of „Friedenshütte under court supervision“ it was printed „Königshütte under court supervision“.
From Sport.

[Sport — Silesia and Zagłębie.] On Saturday and Sunday 2 hockey matches took place on the Katowice ice rink between the Czech „Troppau Skating Club“ (Troppauer Eisläufer-Verein) and the „Warsaw“ representative team. On both days the „Warsaw“ team won: on the first day 3:1 and on the second day 2:1. The Polish goalkeeper Stogowski distinguished himself best of all.
— On Sunday the 27th of this month the long-awaited match „Canada“ — „Poland“ will take place on the Katowice ice rink. Because of the recent great victories that „Canada“ has won in Europe, this match is awaited throughout Poland with great interest.
From the Sosnowiec „Maccabi“.
